2120.oneLiner: Book this Denny Triangle dining room when someone else is picking up the check.
2120.blurb: Save 2120 for the night someone else is hosting. The cooking is New American, the room is dressed for a celebration, and Denny Triangle is simply where the table happens to be.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting New American at 2120

altitude-sky-lounge.name: ALTITUDE Sky Lounge
altitude-sky-lounge.oneLiner: Take visitors up here for skyline cocktails that last past eleven.
altitude-sky-lounge.blurb: Up on a South Lake Union rooftop, ALTITUDE Sky Lounge keeps pouring drinks with city views well past eleven.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at ALTITUDE Sky Lounge

market-grill.name: Market Grill

orderThis.note: The counter order this stall is known for.
The cup that belongs next to the sandwich.

market-grill.oneLiner: Get the blackened salmon sandwich with rosemary mayo and a cup of chowder.
market-grill.blurb: Squeezing through Pike Place crowds sounds like a bad lunch plan, but Market Grill makes it pay off. The counter sits right in the middle of the action, where the cooks sear a blackened salmon sandwich slicked in rosemary mayo. Add the herby clam chowder on the side. Solo diners can usually snag a stool, while groups should take it to go.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at Market Grill

the-walrus-and-the-carpenter.name: The Walrus and The Carpenter
the-walrus-and-the-carpenter.oneLiner: Come before sunset, sit at the marble bar, and order oysters by the dozen.
the-walrus-and-the-carpenter.blurb: The Walrus and The Carpenter draws an oyster line in Ballard even though the bay is nowhere in sight. The room feels like a farmhouse that traded livestock for shellfish, and it shines in late afternoon when sunlight bounces off the mirrors. Happy hour helps, and a date here rarely goes wrong.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at The Walrus and The Carpenter

island-soul-restaurant.name: Island Soul Restaurant
island-soul-restaurant.oneLiner: Leave work early for rum punch, gumbo, and a coconut corn muffin.
island-soul-restaurant.blurb: Island Soul Restaurant brings lively Caribbean energy to Columbia City, with soccer on the TVs and wide windows open to the street. Fill the table with creamy mac and cheese, sticky wings, and glossy gumbo. Don't skip the coconut corn muffin, and expect one rum punch to turn into two. The kitchen also stays open late.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Caribbean at Island Soul Restaurant

how-to-cook-a-wolf.name: How to Cook a Wolf
how-to-cook-a-wolf.address: 2208 Queen Anne Ave N, Seattle, WA  98109
how-to-cook-a-wolf.oneLiner: Settle into the snug room and order a couple of handmade pastas.
how-to-cook-a-wolf.blurb: Named after a wartime cookbook, How to Cook a Wolf turns out fresh pasta and Italian small plates in an intimate Queen Anne room. The kitchen runs late, so Queen Anne can still get pasta after the first plan falls through.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at How to Cook a Wolf

loretta-s-northwesterner.name: Loretta's Northwesterner
loretta-s-northwesterner.oneLiner: South Park's double tavern burger, charred, and better at the bar than in the car.
loretta-s-northwesterner.blurb: Loretta's Northwesterner is the South Park dive organized around a double tavern burger: charred, stacked, special sauce, pickles, cheese, onion, and nothing clever after that. Fries and a beer at the bar are the indoor plan. The back patio is the move when the weather remembers the south end. Carry one out only if you are walking a short block. The sear loses the argument inside a car.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting American at Loretta's Northwesterner

toulouse-petit.name: Toulouse Petit
toulouse-petit.address: 601 Queen Anne Ave N, Seattle, WA  98109
toulouse-petit.oneLiner: Order the BBQ shrimp with grits and bring the whole birthday crew.
toulouse-petit.blurb: Stick with Creole standbys at Toulouse Petit, like barbecue shrimp over grits or a bowl of seafood gumbo, and you'll leave happy. The antique-feeling Lower Queen Anne dining room hums with energy, which makes it great for birthdays and anniversaries. Brunch starts early, happy hour is popular.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cajun at Toulouse Petit

eldr.name: ELDR.
eldr.oneLiner: A Ballard dinner pick for New American plates once the craving is special.
eldr.blurb: For contemporary American plates in Ballard, book a table at ELDR.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting New American at ELDR.

alibi-room.name: Alibi Room
alibi-room.oneLiner: Order the rosemary brown sugar sazerac and a bowl of spicy mac.
alibi-room.blurb: Tucked down Post Alley past the gum wall, Alibi Room pours serious cocktails steps from the Market. Any well drink is fair game, but the house specialties are the move, especially a sazerac sweetened with brown sugar and rosemary. Pair it with the spicy mac and cheese.

photos.alt: Alibi Room in Seattle
Illustration suggesting Pizza at Alibi Room

ba-bar.name: Ba Bar
ba-bar.oneLiner: Brisket pho and a gin cocktail in a dark, moody room is the move.
ba-bar.blurb: Ba Bar pulls off a very particular mood, bowls of brisket phở and gin drinks under low light with jazz playing. The towering bar is the first thing you see, tall enough to need a ladder and backed by a giant vintage Vietnamese rock album poster. It feels like a candlelit back alley with nice furniture, and it's open late with a happy hour worth catching.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Vietnamese at Ba Bar

seattle-meowtropolitan.name: Seattle Meowtropolitan
seattle-meowtropolitan.oneLiner: Book a session, order a latte, and let the resident cats pick you.
seattle-meowtropolitan.blurb: The draw at Seattle Meowtropolitan is the cats, since this Fremont cafe doubles as a hangout for adoptable felines. Plan ahead, because time in the cat room is usually booked in advance.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cafe at Seattle Meowtropolitan

cheese-room-seattle.name: Cheese Room Seattle
cheese-room-seattle.oneLiner: A cheap Capitol Hill sandwich counter that's easy to slot into lunch.
cheese-room-seattle.blurb: Inexpensive sandwiches are the whole business at Cheese Room Seattle, a Capitol Hill counter.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sandwiches at Cheese Room Seattle

dough-zone.name: Dough Zone

orderThis.note: Xiao long bao is the reason for the line.

dough-zone.oneLiner: Come hungry for soup dumplings and let everything else play backup.
dough-zone.blurb: Dough Zone moves fast, and the soup dumplings are the reason to come, thin-skinned and full of hot broth. Round out the order with whatever noodles or buns catch your eye in this Chinatown-International District dining room.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Chinese (Dumplings at Dough Zone

monorail-espresso.name: Monorail Espresso
monorail-espresso.oneLiner: A walk-up espresso window for a fast, cheap shot on the way in.
monorail-espresso.blurb: From a tiny walk-up window near the Denny Triangle, Monorail Espresso pulls inexpensive shots starting early.

photos.alt: Monorail Espresso in Seattle
photos.credit: Monorail Espresso, Seattle Convention Center, August 2024.jpg

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at Monorail Espresso

ludi-s-restaurant.name: Ludi's Restaurant
ludi-s-restaurant.oneLiner: Order the purple ube pancakes and settle into a booth.
ludi-s-restaurant.blurb: Seattle mourned hard when Ludi's Restaurant closed in 2019, and the reopening a few years later felt like a homecoming. The Filipino diner now sits a couple of blocks from its old Downtown home, with the same family running the griddle and breakfast served all day. Grab a booth and get the ube pancakes, still as bright purple as ever.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Filipino at Ludi's Restaurant

inside-passage.name: Inside Passage
inside-passage.oneLiner: Order something with rum and sit beneath the nautical kitsch.
inside-passage.blurb: Tiki drinks rule at Inside Passage, a Capitol Hill cocktail bar dressed up like the hold of a ship. Service continues after eleven, so it makes a fine last stop.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Inside Passage

the-shop-by-porter.name: The Shop by Porter
the-shop-by-porter.oneLiner: A cheap, early-opening downtown cafe for coffee before work.
the-shop-by-porter.blurb: Downtown coffee from The Shop by Porter starts early in the morning and won't cost much.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at The Shop by Porter

the-other-coast-cafe.name: The Other Coast Cafe
the-other-coast-cafe.oneLiner: Order the Rajun Cajun, or the Michael King if you're skipping meat.
the-other-coast-cafe.blurb: Sandwiches at The Other Coast Cafe are big, saucy, and built to satisfy, like the Electric Wizard, which layers ham and smoked mozzarella under balsamic mayo. The turkey and pepper jack in the Cajun sandwich get drenched in spicy salsa mayo, while the vegan option stacks roasted yams with dry-rubbed tofu. Eat on a stool inside or carry it along the Ballard shopping strip. Prices stay pleasantly low.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sandwiches at The Other Coast Cafe

birrieria-pepe-el-toro.name: Birrieria Pepe El Toro
birrieria-pepe-el-toro.oneLiner: Head here for birria tacos when you're near the University District.
birrieria-pepe-el-toro.blurb: Birrieria Pepe El Toro, as the name suggests, centers its U District menu on birria and tacos.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Mexican at Birrieria Pepe El Toro

queen-anne-beerhall.name: Queen Anne Beerhall
queen-anne-beerhall.oneLiner: Long communal tables and liters of German beer make group nights easy.
queen-anne-beerhall.blurb: Near Seattle Center, Queen Anne Beerhall is a roomy German-style beer hall with shared tables and plenty of space for a crowd. That early drink deal is a solid deal, and the bar keeps pouring well past eleven, which helps after a game or concert next door.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Beer at Queen Anne Beerhall

mean-sandwich.name: Mean Sandwich
mean-sandwich.oneLiner: A cheap Ballard lunch counter where the sandwiches carry the whole show.
mean-sandwich.blurb: An inexpensive Ballard sandwich counter, Mean Sandwich is a reliable lunch with no fuss.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sandwiches at Mean Sandwich

glo-s.name: Glo’s
glo-s.address: 928 E Barbara Bailey Way, Seattle, WA 98122
glo-s.oneLiner: Brave the weekend line, because these hash browns justify every minute of it.
glo-s.blurb: Glo’s moved off its old Olive Way corner but kept the neon, the stone walls, and the mid-century charm. The wait still stretches past an hour on weekends, and it still pays off. Expect hash browns with a shattering golden crust, scallion and garlic scrambles, and a tangy homemade corned beef hash.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Breakfast & Brunch at Glo’s

fob-sushi-bar.name: FOB Sushi Bar
fob-sushi-bar.oneLiner: Belltown sushi that can stand alone on a crowded list of contenders.
fob-sushi-bar.blurb: FOB Sushi Bar handles raw fish in Belltown and earns a mention among the city's better sushi spots.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sushi at FOB Sushi Bar

pick-quick-drive-in.name: Pick-Quick Drive In
pick-quick-drive-in.oneLiner: Eat a double cheeseburger and a root beer float in the car.
pick-quick-drive-in.blurb: For a double cheeseburger with fries and a shake on pocket change, Pick-Quick Drive In has you covered. The burgers beat Dick's handily, and you get to sit down while you eat them. Load your friends into the car and get everyone root beer floats made with real soft serve.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Burgers at Pick-Quick Drive In

shibuya-hifi.name: Shibuya HiFi
shibuya-hifi.oneLiner: Come for the records and the cocktails, and keep the conversation low.
shibuya-hifi.blurb: Music comes first at Shibuya HiFi, a Ballard listening bar where the sound system and the vinyl get as much attention as the drinks. The cocktails hold up their end, and the night runs long here.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Shibuya HiFi

the-white-swan-public-house.name: The White Swan Public House
the-white-swan-public-house.oneLiner: Skip the sunny-afternoon crowds and come after dark for the lit-up lake.
the-white-swan-public-house.blurb: Nautical decor and big water views make The White Swan Public House look like a tourist trap, but it mostly sidesteps the clichés. Stick with the seafood and you'll eat well. Warm afternoons get packed, so come after sundown, when tables open up and party boats drift across Lake Union. Happy hour and big groups are both easy here.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at The White Swan Public House

general-porpoise.name: General Porpoise
general-porpoise.oneLiner: Get a custard-filled doughnut early and eat it before you reach the door.
general-porpoise.blurb: General Porpoise fills its pillowy yeast doughnuts with custards and jams, and the Pioneer Square shop opens early.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Donuts at General Porpoise

konvene-coffee-cafe.name: Konvene Coffee Cafe
konvene-coffee-cafe.oneLiner: Hide out upstairs with a latte and the bacon, egg, and Beecher's sandwich.
konvene-coffee-cafe.blurb: Konvene Coffee Cafe is tucked upstairs inside a QFC. The baristas are friendly and steam milk beautifully. Seating is limited and there are no outlets, so plan on a short work session. Hungry visitors should order the bacon and egg sandwich with Beecher's cheese and aioli on brioche.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at Konvene Coffee Cafe

fremont-brewing.name: Fremont Brewing
fremont-brewing.oneLiner: Bring takeout barbecue and spend a long afternoon at the picnic tables.
fremont-brewing.blurb: Fremont Brewing is daytime drinking at its most generous, with a sprawling patio, long communal tables, and free pretzels. Two infused Randall taps rotate constantly, so there's always something new to try. Outside food is welcome, which means a sack of Roro BBQ and a flight make a great Fremont outing.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Beer at Fremont Brewing

valentina-s-cafe.name: Valentina’s Cafe
valentina-s-cafe.oneLiner: An early Ballard coffee stop for your first cup of the day.
valentina-s-cafe.blurb: Valentina’s Cafe pours coffee in Ballard from early morning on.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at Valentina’s Cafe

indigo-cow.name: Indigo Cow
indigo-cow.oneLiner: The plain Hokkaido milk soft serve is all you need, though toppings help.
indigo-cow.blurb: Wallingford's Indigo Cow builds its soft serve around milk from Hokkaido, and the result is gently sweet and remarkably light. Expect a line down the block in any weather. It's great unadorned, but a dip of Theo dark chocolate or brown sugar syrup with roasted soybean powder is worth adding.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Ice Cream at Indigo Cow

dahlia-bakery.name: Dahlia Bakery
dahlia-bakery.oneLiner: Get the breakfast sandwich and a few coconut cream pie bites to go.
dahlia-bakery.blurb: Dahlia Bakery's pastry case runs deep, but the move is a breakfast sandwich stacked with egg, ham, pepper jack, arugula, and spicy jalapeño aioli. The house English muffins taste nothing like the supermarket kind, which turns out to be a good thing. Seating amounts to a few spots outside, so plan on eating on the go in Belltown.

photos.alt: Dahlia Bakery in Seattle
photos.credit: Serious Pie and Dahlia Bakery, Belltown, Seattle 1.jpg

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at Dahlia Bakery

wild-ginger-kitchen.name: Wild Ginger Kitchen
wild-ginger-kitchen.oneLiner: A polished downtown pick for pan-Asian plates before a show or meeting.
wild-ginger-kitchen.blurb: Wild Ginger Kitchen serves Asian fusion dishes in a polished downtown dining room.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Asian Fusion at Wild Ginger Kitchen

seattle-fish-guys.name: Seattle Fish Guys
seattle-fish-guys.oneLiner: Order the poke with spicy salmon and a scoop of smoky mac salad.
seattle-fish-guys.blurb: The poke at Seattle Fish Guys in the Central District earns a spot on any short list of things that never disappoint. Each piece pulls its weight, from the soy-soaked tuna and spicy salmon to the furikake-dusted rice and smoky mac salad, and together they add up to something even better.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at Seattle Fish Guys

be-mi.name: Bé Mi
be-mi.oneLiner: These loaded bánh mì prove that more toppings can absolutely mean better.
be-mi.blurb: Bé Mi skips the minimalist approach to bánh mì, layering on crushed peanuts, chili jam, fried shallots, and heaps of herbs. The fillings hold their own, whether it's charred, fatty pork or cold cuts with pâté. The dining room has just enough energy and makes a good escape from the Pioneer Square tour crowds.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Vietnamese at Bé Mi

maximilien.name: Maximilien
maximilien.oneLiner: Classic French cooking and a water view, tucked away from the market crowds.
maximilien.blurb: Maximilien serves French food in Pike Place Market, with windows looking out over Elliott Bay.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting French at Maximilien

honeyhole-sandwiches.name: Honeyhole Sandwiches
honeyhole-sandwiches.oneLiner: Late-night sandwich cravings on Capitol Hill have a reliable answer right here.
honeyhole-sandwiches.blurb: Cheap sandwiches and a kitchen that runs late make Honeyhole Sandwiches a Capitol Hill standby.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sandwiches at Honeyhole Sandwiches

seoul-bowl-co.name: Seoul Bowl Co
seoul-bowl-co.oneLiner: A quick Korean counter on Capitol Hill for a filling bowl at lunch.
seoul-bowl-co.blurb: Korean bowls come over the counter at Seoul Bowl Co, a quick-service stop on Capitol Hill.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Korean at Seoul Bowl Co

archipelago.name: Archipelago
archipelago.oneLiner: Book well ahead for a Filipino tasting menu that tells a personal story.
archipelago.blurb: Archipelago runs a small, story-driven tasting menu that ties Filipino-American history to Pacific Northwest ingredients. Seats are few and the bill is a splurge, so plan a real celebration around it.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Filipino at Archipelago

indi-chocolate.name: Indi Chocolate
indi-chocolate.address: 1901 Western Ave, Unit D, Seattle, WA 98101
indi-chocolate.oneLiner: Chocolate lovers should stop here for bars made from the bean up.
indi-chocolate.blurb: In the market, Indi Chocolate makes its own chocolate from scratch and sells bars and other treats at the counter.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Chocolate at Indi Chocolate

le-panier.name: Le Panier
le-panier.oneLiner: Get here early for croissants and baguettes before the market wakes up.
le-panier.blurb: Le Panier has been baking French bread and pastries at Pike Place for decades, and it remains a classic for good reason. Go early and grab a flaky croissant or a crusty loaf.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at Le Panier

milstead-co.name: Milstead & Co.
milstead-co.oneLiner: Serious coffee, communal tables, and a homemade Oreo you shouldn't skip.
milstead-co.blurb: Coffee obsessives in Fremont already know Milstead & Co. as the shop that gets every cup right. Seating is mostly communal and there's wifi, so it works for heads-down solo time or a team work session. Grab the house-made Oreo from Standard Bakery before you go.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at Milstead & Co.

saigon-viet-nam-deli.name: Saigon Viet Nam Deli
saigon-viet-nam-deli.oneLiner: The grilled pork bánh mì here is still a cheap lunch miracle.
saigon-viet-nam-deli.blurb: Prices creep up everywhere, but Saigon Viet Nam Deli in the International District still sells a bánh mì that barely dents your wallet. The grilled pork version comes on crackly fresh bread with a generous swipe of bơ and plenty of coarse black pepper. It tastes the same every time, which is the highest compliment.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Vietnamese at Saigon Viet Nam Deli

buckley-s.name: Buckley's
buckley-s.oneLiner: Rally a big group here to watch the game and eat bar food.
buckley-s.blurb: Game days in Belltown mean a crowd at Buckley's, a sports bar with plenty of room for groups and a kitchen open late.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bar Food at Buckley's

joe-the-juice.name: JOE & THE JUICE
joe-the-juice.oneLiner: Swing by early for a fresh juice on the way to work.
joe-the-juice.blurb: JOE & THE JUICE pours inexpensive fresh juice early, on the north edge of downtown.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Juice at JOE & THE JUICE

dave-s-hot-chicken.name: Dave's Hot Chicken
dave-s-hot-chicken.address: 1200 E Pike St, Ste 2, Seattle, WA  98122
dave-s-hot-chicken.oneLiner: Pick a heat level one notch below your ego and order the sliders.
dave-s-hot-chicken.blurb: Nashville-style hot chicken tenders and sliders make up nearly the whole menu at Dave's Hot Chicken, with spice that runs from mild to genuinely painful. The Capitol Hill counter keeps it cheap.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Fried Chicken at Dave's Hot Chicken

von-s-1000spirits.name: Von's 1000Spirits
von-s-1000spirits.oneLiner: Use it for happy hour and stick around for the hourly drink wheel.
von-s-1000spirits.blurb: Von's 1000Spirits lives up to its name with a huge bar and a long list of bottles. The sourdough pizza and pasta are solid and the cocktails are better, but this is mostly a happy hour or post-day-drinking lunch move. Every hour they spin a wheel to pick the drink special, and it stays open late.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting American at Von's 1000Spirits

mamma-melina-ristorante-pizzeria.name: Mamma Melina Ristorante + Pizzeria
mamma-melina-ristorante-pizzeria.oneLiner: An easy U District pick for Italian dinner and a pizza to share.
mamma-melina-ristorante-pizzeria.blurb: Mamma Melina Ristorante + Pizzeria serves Italian plates and pizza to a U District crowd.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Mamma Melina Ristorante + Pizzeria

zig-zag-cafe.name: Zig Zag Café
zig-zag-cafe.oneLiner: Order a classic cocktail and the lamb pastitsio, then share a booth.
zig-zag-cafe.blurb: Zig Zag Café is known for cocktails, but skipping the Greek food here would be a mistake. Go for the lamb pastitsio, marinated chicken kebabs with a side of tzatziki, and a sesame-rich hummus. Booths force you onto the same side. It stays open late, and happy hour is a classic.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Zig Zag Café

le-caviste.name: Le Caviste
le-caviste.oneLiner: Sit at the bar with champagne and a board of charcuterie.
le-caviste.blurb: When you want Paris without the flight, Le Caviste delivers a candlelit bar, a glass of bubbly, and excellent cured meats. It suits a quick bite before a date or a solo unwind after a rough workday. The bar pours past eleven.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Wine at Le Caviste

take-5-urban-market.name: Take 5 Urban Market
take-5-urban-market.oneLiner: Order the chicken caesar wrap, then come back another day for the reuben.
take-5-urban-market.blurb: Take 5 Urban Market has the Moon Pies and fruit sodas of a proper corner store, plus a short sandwich menu that deserves real attention. The reuben swaps kraut for creamy slaw and gets a crisp layer of griddled swiss, and the sriracha chicken melt brings plenty of avocado and actual heat. Still, the one you will crave is the chicken caesar, packed with bacon, tomato, and crouton bits.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sandwiches at Take 5 Urban Market

three-girls-bakery.name: Three Girls Bakery
three-girls-bakery.oneLiner: Do not leave without the giant shortbread cookie crowned with fudge.
three-girls-bakery.blurb: It's really just a long glass case and a register in Pike Place Market, but everything inside Three Girls Bakery is good. Look for the oversized m&m cookie, the peanut butter cookie hiding a whole Reese's cup, and the raspberry crumble bar. The fudge-topped shortbread dot is mandatory. For lunch, the counter next door makes a salmon salad sandwich.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at Three Girls Bakery

l-oursin.name: L'Oursin
l-oursin.oneLiner: Order the steak frites and let the server describe the wine.
l-oursin.blurb: L'Oursin pairs a Wes Anderson palette with a playful streak, but this Central District French restaurant cooks seriously. Raw scallops and the fish of the day nod to its seafood roots, while panisse with harissa dip keeps things unpredictable. The steak frites is great, and the witty wine notes make choosing a bottle part of the fun.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting French at L'Oursin

pufftown-bakehouse.name: Pufftown Bakehouse
pufftown-bakehouse.oneLiner: An early pastry stop for market wanderers who want something flaky and cheap.
pufftown-bakehouse.blurb: Inexpensive pastries and an early opening make Pufftown Bakehouse an easy first stop on a Pike Place Market morning.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at Pufftown Bakehouse

driftwood.name: Driftwood
driftwood.oneLiner: Stick with spritzes, small plates, and the excellent bread, and you'll leave happy.
driftwood.blurb: Pastel, polished, and very Alki, Driftwood calls for dressing up a little while keeping the sandals on. The seafood mains can get fussy with too many toppings, but the cocktails are refreshing and the smaller dishes hold up nicely. Order the table bread, which ranks with the city's best, and make it a date.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at Driftwood

aviv-hummus-bar.name: Aviv Hummus Bar
aviv-hummus-bar.oneLiner: Order the falafel first, then the shawarma-spiced cheeps with amba aioli.
aviv-hummus-bar.blurb: Aviv Hummus Bar up on the Hill feels like a proper sit-down lunch even though you order at the counter. Hummus is the headliner by name, but the falafel steals the plate and ranks among the city's best. Build a spread around both, and add the cheeps, shawarma-dusted fries with a garlicky amba dip.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Mediterranean at Aviv Hummus Bar

lark.name: Lark
lark.oneLiner: Treat this as a backup plan, not your first choice for a big night.
lark.blurb: Expect a pleasant but forgettable evening at Lark, an upscale New American standby with a fairly bland dining room. The menu runs through familiar territory like fresh pasta, steak, crudo, and seasonal sorbet. The bolognese is fine, the raw tuna is just raw tuna, and the bread basket is hit or miss. Keep it in your back pocket rather than leading with it.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting New American at Lark

oliver-s-lounge.name: Oliver's Lounge
oliver-s-lounge.oneLiner: A classic downtown hotel lounge for a cold martini and quiet conversation.
oliver-s-lounge.blurb: Inside the Mayflower Park Hotel downtown, Oliver's Lounge has a long reputation for its martinis. Big windows look out on the street, and it's a calm spot for a drink after shopping.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Oliver's Lounge

assaggio-ristorante.name: Assaggio Ristorante
assaggio-ristorante.oneLiner: A dependable Belltown Italian dining room for a relaxed weeknight dinner.
assaggio-ristorante.blurb: Anyone in Belltown looking for a sit-down Italian meal can head to Assaggio Ristorante.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Assaggio Ristorante

duke-s-seafood-south-lake-union.name: Duke's Seafood South Lake Union
duke-s-seafood-south-lake-union.oneLiner: Grab a deck table at happy hour and order a cup of chowder.
duke-s-seafood-south-lake-union.blurb: Lake Union views and a packed deck pull a crowd into Duke's Seafood South Lake Union, along with the creamy clam chowder the local chain built its name on. The pre-dinner window is a solid deal.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at Duke's Seafood South Lake Union

salumi.name: Salumi
salumi.oneLiner: Get the porchetta sandwich and accept that the line is part of lunch.
salumi.blurb: A Pioneer Square institution for cured meats, Salumi turns out sandwiches stacked with salami made in-house. The porchetta is the one to order, and it's worth planning around the hours, since the counter is small and keeps a short schedule.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian (Sandwiches at Salumi

the-usual.name: The Usual
the-usual.oneLiner: Order a latte with the chicken pelmeni and you'll understand the hype.
the-usual.blurb: The Usual looks like any coffee shop on the ground floor of a new apartment building, complete with croissants and latte art. The surprise is the Eastern European dumplings, like dill-brightened chicken pelmeni and potato vareniki topped with bacon. Paired with espresso on a cold Central District morning, they hit hard.

photos.alt: The Usual in Seattle
photos.credit: Indian boat races on Elliott Bay, Seattle, circa 1910 (MOHAI 9640).jpg

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at The Usual

rachel-s-bagels-burritos.name: Rachel's Bagels & Burritos
rachel-s-bagels-burritos.oneLiner: Indecisive mornings end well here, since the bagels and burritos are both excellent.
rachel-s-bagels-burritos.blurb: The name tells you the plan, and Rachel's Bagels & Burritos delivers on both halves. Bagels come chewy with a crackly shell, great under a thick smear of cream cheese and some everything-seasoned chile crisp. Burritos are stuffed with roasted potato chunks and fillings like celery root al pastor or maitake mushrooms.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bagels at Rachel's Bagels & Burritos

star-sushi-bar.name: Star Sushi & Bar
star-sushi-bar.oneLiner: A Capitol Hill sushi bar to know for an unfussy weeknight roll.
star-sushi-bar.blurb: Sushi and drinks are the draw at Star Sushi & Bar on Capitol Hill.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sushi at Star Sushi & Bar

bell-s-cookie-co.name: Bell's Cookie Co
bell-s-cookie-co.address: 6900 E Green Lake Way N, Unit D, Seattle, WA 98115
bell-s-cookie-co.oneLiner: Walk a loop of the lake path, then reward yourself with a cookie here.
bell-s-cookie-co.blurb: Bell's Cookie Co bakes cookies near Green Lake and keeps ice cream around for a full dessert run.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Dessert at Bell's Cookie Co

betty-restaurant-bar.name: Betty Restaurant & Bar
betty-restaurant-bar.address: 1507 Queen Anne Ave N, Seattle, WA  98109
betty-restaurant-bar.oneLiner: Take your parents to Queen Anne for a dressed-up New American dinner.
betty-restaurant-bar.blurb: Betty Restaurant & Bar runs a special-occasion check on Queen Anne.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting New American at Betty Restaurant & Bar

hood-famous.name: Hood Famous
hood-famous.oneLiner: Order an ube latte and a slice of ube cheesecake to go.
hood-famous.blurb: Hood Famous built its name on Filipino baked goods, and its Chinatown-International District cafe pairs them with early coffee service. Ube shows up everywhere, from the lattes to the cheesecake that made the bakery a local favorite.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at Hood Famous

the-capital-grille.name: The Capital Grille
the-capital-grille.oneLiner: A classic special-occasion steakhouse for impressing your parents, ideally on their dime.
the-capital-grille.blurb: Downtown, The Capital Grille sticks to the dark-wood steakhouse formula with a big check and the polish that parents tend to appreciate.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Steakhouse at The Capital Grille

baxter-frost.name: Baxter & Frost
baxter-frost.oneLiner: A cheap and cheerful pastry stop when you're wandering the Market.
baxter-frost.blurb: Anyone wandering Pike Place Market can grab an inexpensive pastry at Baxter & Frost.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at Baxter & Frost

taste-of-india.name: Taste of India
taste-of-india.oneLiner: Grab a table under the string lights and order the fish coconut curry.
taste-of-india.blurb: A giant pergola strung with lights shelters the outdoor seating at Taste of India, which feels more like a mellow backyard than a U District restaurant. Free potato and pea samosas land soon after you sit, and the long menu moves fast. Get the tandoori wings, butter chicken, and shimla paneer, but save room for the coconut fish curry, which is impossibly tender.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Indian at Taste of India

macrina-bakery-cafe.name: Macrina Bakery & Cafe
macrina-bakery-cafe.oneLiner: Get there early, grab a loaf for later, and eat a pastry now.
macrina-bakery-cafe.blurb: Macrina Bakery & Cafe has been baking bread for Seattle since the nineties, and the Belltown original still opens early. Settle in with a pastry and coffee, then leave with a crusty loaf under your arm.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at Macrina Bakery & Cafe

aroom.name: Aroom
aroom.address: 3801 Stone Way N, Suite C, Seattle, WA 98103
aroom.oneLiner: Order the Vietnamese iced coffee topped with black sesame cream, no question.
aroom.blurb: Aroom's spare, design-studio look in Fremont hides a seriously strong Vietnamese iced coffee. Soften the jolt with a topping like salty foam, house coconut ice cream, or nutty, lightly sweet black sesame cream, which is the best of the bunch.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at Aroom

eggslut.name: Eggslut
eggslut.oneLiner: The Fairfax on a warm brioche bun fixes almost any rough morning.
eggslut.blurb: The LA egg sandwich chain Eggslut landed on Capitol Hill, and the Fairfax, with soft scrambled eggs, chives, cheddar, and sriracha mayo on a brioche bun, is the order regulars make. Doors open early, and the bill stays gentle enough for a weekday treat.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Breakfast Sandwiches at Eggslut

surrell.name: Surrell
surrell.oneLiner: Save this Madison Valley tasting menu for a milestone dinner worth dressing up.
surrell.blurb: Surrell builds a multi-course meal around Pacific Northwest ingredients in an intimate Madison Valley room. This is a dressed-up night, best saved for anniversaries and big celebrations.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pacific Northwest at Surrell

top-pot-doughnuts.name: Top Pot Doughnuts
top-pot-doughnuts.oneLiner: Grab an old-fashioned and a coffee, then settle in under the towering bookshelves.
top-pot-doughnuts.blurb: Top Pot Doughnuts has been a Seattle staple for years, and the Belltown flagship with tall glass windows and floor-to-ceiling bookshelves is the one to visit. The hand-forged doughnuts are classic rather than trendy, and the shop opens early.

photos.alt: Top Pot Doughnuts in Seattle
photos.credit: Seattle - people lined up outside Top Pot Doughnuts in Alki during the COVID-19 outbreak.jpg

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Donuts at Top Pot Doughnuts

otherworld.name: Otherworld
otherworld.oneLiner: Natural wine nerds, this is your clubhouse, deep cuts and murky pours included.
otherworld.blurb: Remember the Juice Club pop-up? Its crew now runs Otherworld, a Capitol Hill natural wine bar built for glou-glou devotees. Prices hang on a deli-style felt board, the shelves are lined with bottles sporting arty labels, and the music runs funky and obscure. Settle in with small glasses of something cloudy, and know the night runs long here.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Wine at Otherworld

nielsens-pastries.name: Nielsens Pastries
nielsens-pastries.oneLiner: Order a Snitter, then grab marzipan almond cake for someone you love.
nielsens-pastries.blurb: Everyone comes to this cheerful Danish bakery for the Snitter, a pastry that tastes like a cinnamon roll crossed with a cheese danish. Nielsens Pastries has been at it in Lower Queen Anne for decades, and the case explains why. The marzipan almond cake is a birthday-worthy dessert you'll probably start eating on the drive home.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at Nielsens Pastries

cinque-terre-ristorante.name: Cinque Terre Ristorante
cinque-terre-ristorante.oneLiner: Skip the pricey entrees and order the margherita with a pasta on the side.
cinque-terre-ristorante.blurb: Blue neon under the bar and champagne bottles as decor make Cinque Terre Ristorante feel a bit like a hotel lobby. Ignore that, because the Neapolitan pies are the real deal, with a charred, crackly crust and a balanced layer of San Marzano and mozzarella. Round things out with casarecce tossed with pesto and ricotta, or boar sugo over rigatoni, and leave the main courses alone.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Cinque Terre Ristorante

neb.name: Neb
neb.oneLiner: A Belltown wine bar for a thoughtful glass before or after dinner.
neb.blurb: For a glass of wine in Belltown that feels like a step up from the usual bar, Neb is a smart pick.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Wine at Neb

percy-s-and-co.name: Percy's and Co.
percy-s-and-co.oneLiner: A Ballard cocktail bar for a late round after dinner nearby.
percy-s-and-co.blurb: In Ballard, Percy's and Co. keeps the cocktails coming past eleven.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Percy's and Co.

radiator-whiskey.name: Radiator Whiskey
radiator-whiskey.oneLiner: Order the pork belly burnt ends and a whiskey, then stay for another round.
radiator-whiskey.blurb: Climb the stairs above the market and you'll find Radiator Whiskey, a small, dark room with a deep whiskey list and food built to absorb it. Think burnt ends, tots smothered in gravy with a fried egg, and marrow bones set up for a luge. Reserve ahead for the smoked pig's head, though landing a table on a Friday is usually painless.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting American at Radiator Whiskey

chez-phinney.name: Chez Phinney
chez-phinney.oneLiner: Self-pour wine machines and late-night dance music make this the north end's best wine stop.
chez-phinney.blurb: Hand over a card, grab an empty glass, and work your way through the self-serve taps at Chez Phinney. Snack on house chocolate truffles plus Michou Deli dips between pours. By day the room looks like a Parisian cafe inside an airport terminal, but after dark the music gets loud and nobody's rushing you out.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Wine at Chez Phinney

palace-kitchen.name: Palace Kitchen
palace-kitchen.oneLiner: A Belltown classic for a late dinner at the bar with a cocktail.
palace-kitchen.blurb: Palace Kitchen has anchored Belltown dining for decades well past eleven. Claim a stool along the big bar for happy hour or a late meal after a show.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting New American at Palace Kitchen

cortina.name: Cortina
cortina.oneLiner: A reliable downtown Italian option when the plan calls for a sit-down meal nearby.
cortina.blurb: Cortina brings an Italian menu to the office towers of Downtown Seattle.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Cortina

artly.name: Artly
artly.oneLiner: An easy early espresso stop for anyone working downtown.
artly.blurb: Downtown commuters can count on Artly for inexpensive coffee starting first thing in the morning.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at Artly

wasabi-sushi-izakaya.name: Wasabi Sushi & Izakaya
wasabi-sushi-izakaya.oneLiner: A late Belltown sushi spot with a happy hour worth planning around.
wasabi-sushi-izakaya.blurb: Belltown's Wasabi Sushi & Izakaya serves sushi and izakaya plates late into the night, and the discounted hour is a strong reason to stop in.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sushi at Wasabi Sushi & Izakaya

spinasse.name: Spinasse
spinasse.oneLiner: Order every pasta you can justify, starting with the buttery tajarin.
spinasse.blurb: For a splurge Italian dinner in Seattle, Spinasse sets the bar, with handmade Piedmontese pasta and service that runs like clockwork. The Capitol Hill dining room mixes reclaimed wood with a sleek marble bar and an open kitchen where you can watch the noodles being made. Expect a special-occasion check, and know the kitchen keeps going late.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Spinasse

chung-chun-rice-dog.name: Chung Chun Rice Dog
chung-chun-rice-dog.oneLiner: Get a mozzarella dog, add sugar and ketchup, and don't overthink it.
chung-chun-rice-dog.blurb: Korean-style corn dogs in a crisp rice-flour batter are the specialty at Chung Chun Rice Dog, including cheesy and potato-studded versions. It's an inexpensive snack stop in the Chinatown-International District.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Hot Dogs at Chung Chun Rice Dog

dreamland.name: Dreamland
dreamland.oneLiner: Order a disco ball of margaritas and the gooey cheeseburger, then claim the balcony.
dreamland.blurb: Dreamland looks like a space jungle grotto stitched together from sci-fi movies and roller disco fantasy, and it's a blast. Head for the patio for drag brunch or a night with friends, and grab grasshopper slushies or Jell-O shots for the table. The bar snacks are excellent, especially that burger, and the party runs late.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Dreamland

paju.name: Paju
paju.oneLiner: Start with the seafood pancake and a chili lime martini, then keep ordering.
paju.blurb: Paju traded its cramped Queen Anne home for a much bigger South Lake Union space with a full bar, a wood-fired grill anchoring the open kitchen, and plenty of black marble. The menu grew too, but the reasons to come are the same ones as before. A savory seafood pancake buried in wiggling bonito flakes goes great with the chili lime oil martini, and squid-ink kimchi fried rice comes with bacon. Bring a special-occasion budget.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Korean at Paju

umi-sake-house.name: Umi Sake House
umi-sake-house.oneLiner: Book the back room for a date fueled by salmon nigiri and sake.
umi-sake-house.blurb: Before Momiji, there was Umi Sake House, and the first one is still the pick. Ask for the back dining room, which feels like a bamboo garden turned lounge, and order a nigiri sampler plus rolls with seared snow crab or spicy yellowtail. Big groups can usually book even the night before, and the happy hour and late kitchen help.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sushi at Umi Sake House

mas-cafe.name: Mas Cafe
mas-cafe.oneLiner: The bacon breakfast sandwich here is worth a scratch from a stray shard.
mas-cafe.blurb: A tiny roadside coffee shop in Wallingford, Mas Cafe does Mexican breakfasts and a bacon sandwich that might be the city's best. A soft Macrina bun holds a lacy fried egg, grilled onions, red chile aioli, white cheddar, and a heap of bacon cooked until it shatters. The sausage version with provolone is excellent too, and so are the breakfast burritos.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at Mas Cafe

the-brim-coffee-shop.name: The Brim Coffee Shop
the-brim-coffee-shop.oneLiner: Cheap, early coffee in Belltown, plus a rooftop to drink it on.
the-brim-coffee-shop.blurb: Early risers in Belltown can grab inexpensive coffee at The Brim Coffee Shop, which also has a rooftop for sipping it.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at The Brim Coffee Shop

jebena-cafe.name: Jebena Cafe
jebena-cafe.oneLiner: Order the green lamb alongside a bowl of curried cabbage.
jebena-cafe.blurb: Lime-green walls and warm service set the tone at Jebena Cafe, an inexpensive Ethiopian spot in Lake City. The Jebena combo comes on a huge platter with several meats, vegetable sides, and house-made ayib. The best thing on the menu is the green lamb, tender and loaded with herbs and collards, and it's even better next to the curried cabbage.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Ethiopian at Jebena Cafe

cafe-lolo.name: Cafe Lolo
cafe-lolo.oneLiner: Share a couple of salads and order the soft wheat porridge at lunch.
cafe-lolo.blurb: Counter service, folk murals, and fizzy pop music give Cafe Lolo on Capitol Hill a soothing, unhurried feel. The menu goes well past standard soups and sandwiches, with seasonal twists like melon topped with coppa and plum agrodolce, plus pasta made from house-milled flour. At lunch, split a few salads and a bowl of soft wheat porridge, and leave room for the blintzes.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pacific Northwest at Cafe Lolo

hushy-s-sandwiches.name: Hushy's Sandwiches
hushy-s-sandwiches.address: 3400 Stone Way N, Ste 105, Seattle, WA  98103
hushy-s-sandwiches.oneLiner: Grab a cheap sandwich here when you're wandering around Wallingford hungry.
hushy-s-sandwiches.blurb: Hushy's Sandwiches keeps things inexpensive at its Wallingford sandwich counter.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sandwiches at Hushy's Sandwiches

chengdu-taste.name: Chengdu Taste
chengdu-taste.oneLiner: Bring friends with a high spice tolerance and order more than you need.
chengdu-taste.blurb: Chengdu Taste brings fiery Sichuan cooking to the Chinatown-International District.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Chinese at Chengdu Taste

shuckers-oyster-bar.name: SHUCKERS OYSTER BAR
shuckers-oyster-bar.oneLiner: Take a bar stool, order a dirty martini, and work through a dozen oysters.
shuckers-oyster-bar.blurb: Inside the Fairmont Olympic, SHUCKERS OYSTER BAR is an old-school room that smells faintly of brine and polished leather. Happy hour knocks the price of local raw oysters way down, and the baked ones topped with toasted brioche and lemony herb butter deserve a spot in your order. The space was a haberdashery in the early twentieth century, and it still has that buttoned-up charm.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at SHUCKERS OYSTER BAR

cardoon.name: Cardoon
cardoon.oneLiner: Get the licorice caramel latte and dunk a cardamom rose cookie in it.
cardoon.blurb: This tiny Ballard cafe pulls Kuma espresso with Chinese and German touches, and its oat lattes come out impossibly silky. A salty licorice caramel drink brings a gentle anise edge. Sunlight pours through the windows at Cardoon, the snug corner seats are surprisingly comfortable, and the doors open early.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at Cardoon

house-of-eve.name: House Of Eve
house-of-eve.oneLiner: Start a Belltown night with a cocktail here before heading to dinner.
house-of-eve.blurb: Cocktails lead the menu at House Of Eve, a bar in Belltown.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at House Of Eve

portage-bay-cafe.name: Portage Bay Cafe
portage-bay-cafe.oneLiner: Bring the whole brunch crew, picky eaters and toddlers included, and nobody leaves unhappy.
portage-bay-cafe.blurb: When a weekend brunch involves ten people with ten opinions, Portage Bay Cafe is the safe call. The menu is enormous, the ingredients lean local, and pancakes or french toast come with access to a toppings bar piled with fruit and whipped cream. You can even skip the plate entirely and just graze the bar.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Breakfast & Brunch at Portage Bay Cafe

bad-chancla.name: Bad Chancla
bad-chancla.oneLiner: A Capitol Hill option when the group is craving Latin American food.
bad-chancla.blurb: On Capitol Hill, Bad Chancla is where to go for Latin American cooking.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Latin American at Bad Chancla

louie-s-deli.name: Louie's Deli
louie-s-deli.oneLiner: Show up before noon if you want the turkey sub on a sesame roll.
louie-s-deli.blurb: The Good Shape Pizza team turned its attention to sandwiches at Louie's Deli, a royal blue counter in Pioneer Square. Sesame hoagie rolls are crunchy and chewy, bacon is chopped into small bits, and cold cuts are shaved impossibly thin. Rolls are limited, so get there early for the turkey sub. There's an arcade room next door for pinball after lunch.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sandwiches at Louie's Deli

pink-salt.name: Pink Salt
pink-salt.oneLiner: A Magnolia option for Peruvian food when you want something beyond the usual.
pink-salt.blurb: For Peruvian food without leaving Magnolia, Pink Salt is the neighborhood answer.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Peruvian at Pink Salt

the-wayland-mill.name: The Wayland Mill
the-wayland-mill.address: 3800 Latona Ave NE, Ste 112, Seattle, WA 98105
the-wayland-mill.oneLiner: Bring a book for breakfast or five friends for dinner, and always get the canele.
the-wayland-mill.blurb: Japanese cooking with a Midwestern diner attitude is the deal at The Wayland Mill, a big, bright Wallingford space near the water. Mornings bring scallion biscuits with miso gravy, and the canele is excellent. Later, clarified cocktails and a serious wine list take over, and service stays quick whether you're alone or with a crowd.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Japanese at The Wayland Mill

beecher-s-handmade-cheese.name: Beecher's Handmade Cheese
beecher-s-handmade-cheese.oneLiner: Brave the line of tourists for a cup of that famous mac and cheese.
beecher-s-handmade-cheese.blurb: The nutty, sharp Flagship cheddar from Beecher's Handmade Cheese is in every grocery store in town, but the Pike Place Market shop is where it all gets made. Expect a line packed with curd-sampling tourists at lunch. The reward is a creamy mac and cheese that once made Oprah's list of favorite things, and it's inexpensive.

photos.alt: Beecher's Handmade Cheese in Seattle
photos.credit: Beecher's Handmade Cheese, Pike Place, Seattle (2014).JPG

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cheese at Beecher's Handmade Cheese

hamdi.name: Hamdi
hamdi.oneLiner: Skip the dry-aged steak and build your meal from the mezze instead.
hamdi.blurb: Hamdi grew from a brewery pop-up into a special-occasion Turkish restaurant built around a big open wood-fired grill. The servers will push the steaks, but the smarter move is a spread of small plates, like a garlicky celery root dip studded with dried figs. A watermelon salad with warm spices and salty Tulum cheese is another reason to order light and still enjoy the show.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Turkish at Hamdi

tulio.name: Tulio
tulio.oneLiner: A dependable downtown Italian dining room for pasta before a night out.
tulio.blurb: Downtown's Tulio has been serving Italian food out of the Hotel Vintage for decades, and pasta is the draw.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Tulio

maneki.name: Maneki
maneki.oneLiner: Book a tatami room, take your shoes off, and let the sake flow.
maneki.blurb: Open since before the Model T, Maneki holds the title of Seattle's oldest Japanese restaurant, and it still fills up most nights in the Chinatown-International District. Text ahead for a reservation or expect a very late seating. The main room has a lively hum, but the private tatami rooms are the real move, quiet and closed off with good sushi and plenty of sake.

photos.alt: Maneki in Seattle
Illustration suggesting Sushi at Maneki

elysian-brewing-capitol-hill.name: Elysian Brewing - Capitol Hill
elysian-brewing-capitol-hill.oneLiner: Gather a big group, order pints of Space Dust, and settle in.
elysian-brewing-capitol-hill.blurb: Big tables, a long tap list, and Space Dust IPA at the source make Elysian Brewing - Capitol Hill a simple yes for groups. Happy hour helps, and the pub keeps pouring late.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Beer at Elysian Brewing - Capitol Hill

sushi-kappo-tamura.name: Sushi Kappo Tamura
sushi-kappo-tamura.oneLiner: Come for anything from a casual Tuesday to a proposal, and order omakase.
sushi-kappo-tamura.blurb: Eastlake's Sushi Kappo Tamura fits nearly any occasion, from a no-reason weeknight dinner to a big romantic moment. Tables are easier to land here than at the city's other famous sushi counters, and the fish quality is excellent. Sustainability matters, with careful seafood sourcing and produce from the restaurant's own rooftop garden. The chef's tasting menu is a happy choice if you want to hand over the reins.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sushi at Sushi Kappo Tamura

piroshky-piroshky.name: Piroshky Piroshky
piroshky-piroshky.oneLiner: Get the beef and cheese, eat it standing up, and don't mind the line.
piroshky-piroshky.blurb: Since the early nineties, Piroshky Piroshky has filled the market with the smell of baked Russian hand pies, both savory and sweet. The line moves faster than it looks, prices stay friendly, and the counter opens early enough to make breakfast out of a smoked salmon pastry.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Russian at Piroshky Piroshky

the-roanoke.name: The Roanoke
the-roanoke.oneLiner: A Capitol Hill pub that stays open until 2 and skips the cocktail lecture.
the-roanoke.blurb: The Roanoke is a Capitol Hill pub with a dive's closing time and a screen somewhere if the game is on. It runs until 2, the lights stay low, and the order is a beer rather than a ten-ingredient drink. Take a stool if you came alone. Let the table get loud if you did not. It is the neighborhood tavern for a night that needs neither a reservation nor an occasion.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bar Food at The Roanoke

old-stove-brewing.name: Old Stove Brewing
old-stove-brewing.address: 1901 Western Ave, Unit A, Seattle, WA  98101
old-stove-brewing.oneLiner: House beers and plenty of tables when your whole crew hits the market.
old-stove-brewing.blurb: In the market, Old Stove Brewing pours its own beer and has room for a big group.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Beer at Old Stove Brewing

matt-s-in-the-market.name: Matt's in the Market
matt-s-in-the-market.oneLiner: Book a window table upstairs and make lunch the best part of the day.
matt-s-in-the-market.blurb: Pike Place on a rainy Saturday, elbow to elbow with tourists, rarely feels romantic. Climb the stairs to Matt's in the Market and the whole thing shifts, with seafood and a window view that make the market look charming again. You are paying for the room too, so save it for a date or a lunch you want to remember.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting New American at Matt's in the Market

kobuta-and-ookami.name: Kobuta and Ookami
kobuta-and-ookami.oneLiner: Order the tomato and mozzarella katsu for an extremely cheesy pork cutlet.
kobuta-and-ookami.blurb: Katsu is the entire focus at Kobuta and Ookami, a Capitol Hill spot with plenty of ways to customize your cutlet. Curry katsu comes with a choice of kurobuta or iberico pork, and miso katsu works with shrimp or chicken. The standout wraps thin pork tenderloin around tomato and a heroic amount of melted mozzarella. Every set arrives with miso soup, pickles, and sesame seeds you grind yourself.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Japanese at Kobuta and Ookami

taylor-shellfish-farms.name: Taylor Shellfish Farms
taylor-shellfish-farms.oneLiner: Order raw oysters by the dozen and grab the wall tables if you brought a date.
taylor-shellfish-farms.blurb: Taylor Shellfish Farms has been growing oysters in Washington for well over a century, and this Pioneer Square bar puts that harvest on ice. Branch out with Dungeness crab or Manila clams once the first round is gone. Couples should claim the tables along the wall, and the bar is there when you would rather face the shells than each other. Happy hour makes a second round easier to justify.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at Taylor Shellfish Farms

storyville-coffee-company.name: Storyville Coffee Company
storyville-coffee-company.oneLiner: Climb the stairs for a latte by the fireplace and a market view.
storyville-coffee-company.blurb: Tucked upstairs above the market, Storyville Coffee Company trades the crowds below for a calm, dark-wood room with a fireplace and windows over the action. The fireplace room is already open before the stalls downstairs get loud.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at Storyville Coffee Company

grappa.name: Grappa
grappa.address: 2133 Queen Anne Ave N, Seattle, WA  98109
grappa.oneLiner: Bring your parents here for a polished Mediterranean dinner on Queen Anne.
grappa.blurb: On Queen Anne, Grappa serves Mediterranean food that suits date night or a dinner with the folks.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Mediterranean at Grappa

le-pichet.name: Le Pichet
le-pichet.oneLiner: Linger over a slow lunch of roast chicken, charcuterie, and frites.
le-pichet.blurb: Steps from the Pike Place frenzy, Le Pichet is a calm French bistro escape. It suits a long lunch, a solo dinner, or any moment the market crowds start wearing you down. Settle in and order cured pork, roast chicken, and a pile of fries.

photos.alt: Le Pichet in Seattle
Illustration suggesting French at Le Pichet

franz-bakery-outlet.name: Franz Bakery Outlet
franz-bakery-outlet.oneLiner: Stock up on discounted bread and buns before work at this Central District outlet.
franz-bakery-outlet.blurb: The Franz Bakery Outlet sells the familiar packaged loaves and sweets at a markdown, and it opens early.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at Franz Bakery Outlet

rojo-s-mexican-food.name: Rojo’s Mexican Food
rojo-s-mexican-food.oneLiner: Vegan tortas this good might convert the most committed carnitas fan at lunch.
rojo-s-mexican-food.blurb: Everything at Rojo’s Mexican Food is plant-based, though you'd hardly guess from a menu of asada, chicken, and carnitas-style fillings made in-house. Strong marinades do the heavy lifting, and the jackfruit is a convincing stand-in for braised pork. The small, bright room in Pioneer Square works for a quick lunch with coworkers or a burrito to carry into a Mariners game.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Mexican at Rojo’s Mexican Food

ox-burger.name: Ox Burger
ox-burger.address: 1523 E Madison St, Ste 101, Seattle, WA  98122
ox-burger.oneLiner: A cheap Central District burger fix you can grab at the counter.
ox-burger.blurb: Inexpensive burgers from a casual counter make Ox Burger an easy Central District stop.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Burgers at Ox Burger

alki-spud-fish-and-chips.name: Alki Spud Fish and Chips
alki-spud-fish-and-chips.oneLiner: Pay the extra few bucks for halibut and eat it near the beach.
alki-spud-fish-and-chips.blurb: Alki Spud Fish and Chips has been frying seafood by the beach since the thirties, and old photos and maps of West Seattle cover the walls to prove it. The halibut costs a little more and is absolutely the order, flaky and tender under a crisp, well-seasoned batter. Portions can run huge, and it all comes cheap enough when midday has to be fast or a visit with out-of-town guests.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at Alki Spud Fish and Chips

salt-straw.name: Salt & Straw
salt-straw.oneLiner: Expect a line, a pile of tasting spoons, and flavors you won't find elsewhere.
salt-straw.blurb: The Portland-born Salt & Straw brings its oddball, seasonal scoops to Ballard, and the counter stays open late. Staff hand out samples freely, which helps when the monthly specials get weird.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Ice Cream at Salt & Straw

the-little-beast.name: The Little Beast
the-little-beast.oneLiner: Get the korma pie and accept every extra pour of gravy offered.
the-little-beast.blurb: From the folks behind Beast & Cleaver, The Little Beast looks like a regular British pub on Ballard's main drag until the food arrives. The lamb korma pie comes buried in gravy, the currywurst sausage roll pairs well with a Pimm's cup, and the charred pork chop with grilled nectarines is a standout. Scotch eggs and sing-along rock round out the evening.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting New American at The Little Beast

fog-room.name: Fog Room
fog-room.oneLiner: Take visitors up for a cocktail with the city spread out below.
fog-room.blurb: Fog Room pours drinks on a Downtown rooftop with skyline views, and you can linger past eleven.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Fog Room

familyfriend.name: Familyfriend
familyfriend.oneLiner: Bring a date to Beacon Hill for Chamorro and Filipino flavors done with care.
familyfriend.blurb: Familyfriend cooks Chamorro and Filipino food on Beacon Hill, and it makes a strong date-night pick.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Chamorro at Familyfriend

delaurenti.name: DeLaurenti
delaurenti.oneLiner: Build a picnic from the cheese counter, then grab a cannoli filled on the spot.
delaurenti.blurb: DeLaurenti stocks shelves of imported and local pantry goods among the market stalls, from olive oils and jams to a dangerously good bag of black truffle chips. Upstairs you'll find a smart wine and beer selection, and the charcuterie and cheese case is excellent. Grab a cold cut sandwich up front, and don't skip the chocolate chip cookie or Linzer tarts.

photos.alt: DeLaurenti in Seattle
Illustration suggesting Italian at DeLaurenti

nick-s-on-madison.name: Nick's on Madison
nick-s-on-madison.address: 3131 E Madison St, Ste 100, Seattle, WA 98112
nick-s-on-madison.oneLiner: A Madison Park neighborhood dinner when you would rather not leave the area.
nick-s-on-madison.blurb: Madison Park neighbors have Nick's on Madison for New American cooking close to home.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting New American at Nick's on Madison

alebrijes-kitchen.name: Alebrijes Kitchen
alebrijes-kitchen.oneLiner: A sleepy little dining room turning out seriously great Mexican food.
alebrijes-kitchen.blurb: The room at Alebrijes Kitchen is quiet, with only a few tables, but the kitchen is anything but. Tortilla-wrapped dishes fly out at a steady clip and can rescue the dullest weeknight. Start with the fiery orange salsa and build from there.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Mexican at Alebrijes Kitchen

matsu.name: Matsu
matsu.oneLiner: Late-night sushi in Pioneer Square once the craving is better than bar food.
matsu.blurb: Matsu keeps its Pioneer Square sushi spot going past eleven, which is rare in this part of town.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sushi at Matsu

flatstick-pub.name: Flatstick Pub
flatstick-pub.oneLiner: Eight dollars, a putter, and thirty-two taps in South Lake Union.
flatstick-pub.blurb: Flatstick Pub built a mini-golf course into a South Lake Union bar. A round costs eight dollars, the floor is big enough for a group that cannot choose a restaurant, and 32 taps end the argument about beer. Order the brick-oven pizza instead of stopping at onion rings. Keep the putter away from anyone's face. The person who loses can buy the next round without a meeting about it.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bar Food at Flatstick Pub

harvest-beat.name: Harvest Beat
harvest-beat.oneLiner: Book the single nightly seating for a vegan tasting menu worth celebrating.
harvest-beat.blurb: Harvest Beat makes the case that a special occasion doesn't need meat or butter. There's one seating each night, kicked off by a gong and a speech from the chef about the farmers and foragers behind dishes like carrot ginger bisque and a cashew paneer loaf. Wine pairing is part of the deal, though the fresh-pressed elixir pairing is the more interesting route, and a berry bread pudding often closes things out with birthday candles.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Vegetarian at Harvest Beat

locus-wines.name: Locus Wines
locus-wines.oneLiner: Stop in for a pour of red before dinner in Pioneer Square.
locus-wines.blurb: Pioneer Square wine drinkers can settle in at Locus Wines.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Wine at Locus Wines

mee-sum-pastry.name: Mee Sum Pastry
mee-sum-pastry.oneLiner: Get the steamed barbecue pork bao and eat it walking through the stalls.
mee-sum-pastry.blurb: Swing by in the late morning, before the market fully wakes up, and you'll catch the crew at Mee Sum Pastry folding potstickers and pinching shumai. Grab an assortment and snack your way through Pike Place. It's all good, but the steamed pork hum bao is the order regulars make, and it's open early and inexpensive.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Chinese Bakery at Mee Sum Pastry

nue.name: Nue
nue.oneLiner: Bring a group to brunch and order the Sichuan wings for the table.
nue.blurb: Street food from all over the map shares one menu on Capitol Hill, from Burmese and Jamaican to South African and Chinese. It should be a mess, but Nue makes every detour land. Weekend mornings here swap the benedict for tocino and fried rice, harissa-laced octopus, and pineapple-coconut cornbread. A pile of crunchy Sichuan wings never hurts either.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Global Street Food at Nue

aroy-mak-thai-food.name: Aroy Mak Thai Food
aroy-mak-thai-food.address: 14419 Greenwood Ave N, Unit C, Seattle, WA  98133
aroy-mak-thai-food.oneLiner: Worth crossing town for, even if three Thai places sit closer to home.
aroy-mak-thai-food.blurb: Aroy Mak Thai Food, an all-day strip mall spot up in Bitter Lake, deserves a detour from anywhere in the city. The menu stays short, with just green, yellow, and panang curries, and every one of them lands. Spice is set by the kitchen, though a chili caddy sits on the table if you want more heat, and both the chicken thigh and tofu options are excellent.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Thai at Aroy Mak Thai Food

that-s-amore-italian-cafe.name: That’s Amore Italian Cafe
that-s-amore-italian-cafe.oneLiner: A relaxed neighborhood Italian spot that makes dinner with your parents easy.
that-s-amore-italian-cafe.blurb: Over in Mount Baker, That’s Amore Italian Cafe serves Italian comfort food in a setting that suits a family dinner or a parent visit.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at That’s Amore Italian Cafe

the-chicken-supply.name: The Chicken Supply
the-chicken-supply.oneLiner: This gluten-free Filipino fried chicken is crispier than nearly anything else in town.
the-chicken-supply.blurb: The Chicken Supply dredges its Filipino fried chicken in tapioca, rice flour, and potato starch, and that celiac-friendly coating is exactly why it's so good. Thigh skin crackles like a chip, and the skewers of white meat stay remarkably juicy. Seating is limited to a handful of tables in the small Phinney Ridge room. Prices stay pleasantly low.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Fried Chicken at The Chicken Supply

due-cucina-italiana.name: Due' Cucina Italiana
due-cucina-italiana.oneLiner: A Capitol Hill Italian option for an easygoing weeknight bowl of something comforting.
due-cucina-italiana.blurb: Due' Cucina Italiana cooks Italian food on Capitol Hill for neighborhood dinners.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Due' Cucina Italiana

santo-coffee-co.name: Santo Coffee Co
santo-coffee-co.oneLiner: An early-opening Roosevelt coffee shop for a cheap, well-made morning cup.
santo-coffee-co.blurb: Santo Coffee Co pours coffee in Roosevelt from early morning, and it won't cost you much.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at Santo Coffee Co

milk-drunk.name: Milk Drunk
milk-drunk.oneLiner: Cheap Beacon Hill ice cream that makes dessert an easy yes.
milk-drunk.blurb: On Beacon Hill, Milk Drunk scoops inexpensive ice cream for a sweet stop after dinner.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Ice Cream at Milk Drunk

sugar-bakery-cafe.name: Sugar Bakery & Cafe
sugar-bakery-cafe.oneLiner: Don't skip the bacon chocolate chip cookie, salt and pepper and all.
sugar-bakery-cafe.blurb: Sugar Bakery & Cafe on First Hill handles both a quick morning coffee with a pastry and a baguette sandwich at lunch. Anything in the case is a safe bet, but the cookie with bacon and a sprinkle of black pepper on top is the surprise hit.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at Sugar Bakery & Cafe

pie-bar.name: Pie Bar
pie-bar.oneLiner: Get peanut butter mud a la mode and a glass of bourbon.
pie-bar.blurb: Pie Bar is basically that late Thanksgiving fridge raid turned into a business, minus the aunt catching you in the act. Everything here is excellent, from the warm apple crumble and whiskey chocolate pecan to the peanut butter mud and whatever's rotating. Pietinis blend fruit, cream, and crumbled crust into a dessert you drink, and they pack a punch. It's open late on Capitol Hill.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pie at Pie Bar

my-friend-derek-s.name: My Friend Derek’s
my-friend-derek-s.oneLiner: A Wallingford pizza spot that belongs in your regular weeknight rotation.
my-friend-derek-s.blurb: Wallingford gets solid pizza from My Friend Derek’s, a neighborhood spot for a casual dinner.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pizza at My Friend Derek’s

pacha-collective.name: Pacha Collective
pacha-collective.oneLiner: Get the early cup at Pacha Collective, then go walk it off.
pacha-collective.blurb: Near Green Lake, Pacha Collective opens early for an inexpensive morning cup.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at Pacha Collective

vendemmia.name: Vendemmia
vendemmia.oneLiner: Hide out here with a bowl of pasta and a good bottle of wine.
vendemmia.blurb: Opened by the people behind Le Messe, Vendemmia is a quiet Madrona escape built around pasta and wine. Pick a bottle, then choose between spaghetti with tomato and chili or taleggio-filled agnolotti. Expect a special-occasion bill, and treat it as a reliable date night.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Vendemmia

add-a-ball.name: Add-a-Ball
add-a-ball.oneLiner: Pinball, a fair well drink, and four-player Pac-Man in Fremont.
add-a-ball.blurb: Add-a-Ball is a Fremont arcade for people 21 and over. Beer is priced like a neighborhood bar, and the wells do not taste like melted ice. Four-player Pac-Man has settled nights here. Killer Queen will unsettle them if anyone actually knows the rules. On Saturday evenings, Good Shape parks a pizza pop-up beside the machines, so dinner never requires a coat. Stay until the last ball drains.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bar at Add-a-Ball

kona-kitchen.name: Kona Kitchen
kona-kitchen.oneLiner: Order the kalua pig and cabbage, and get it in a quesadilla.
kona-kitchen.blurb: Maple Leaf's Kona Kitchen feels like a roadside stop on Oahu, with island memorabilia on the walls and squishy booths to sink into. The mai tais are strong, the spam musubi is reliable, and the loco moco comes smothered in gravy with your pick of rice and protein. Smoky kalua pig with cabbage is the real highlight, and the kitchen runs from breakfast through late night.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Hawaiian at Kona Kitchen

tacos-chukis.name: Tacos Chukis

orderThis.note: The taco this window is known for.

tacos-chukis.oneLiner: Order the adobada tacos with grilled pineapple and you've made the right call.
tacos-chukis.blurb: The Broadway taco counter in a building shared with a tattoo shop stopped being a secret long ago, and Tacos Chukis earned the crowds. The house adobada tacos stack marinated grilled pork with avocado salsa, cilantro, onion, and a seared slab of pineapple. Food comes out quickly, it's cheap, and it's an ideal stop before a night out.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Mexican at Tacos Chukis

ghost-alley-espresso.name: Ghost Alley Espresso
ghost-alley-espresso.oneLiner: Skip the gum wall selfies and get a nutella latte instead.
ghost-alley-espresso.blurb: Tucked beside the gum wall, Ghost Alley Espresso is a tiny walk-up window that rescues any Pike Place errand. The lattes run playful, with nutella and blueberry cheesecake among the options, and the house nut milks are a real draw. It's inexpensive, quick, and far better than lingering with the tourists outside.

photos.alt: Ghost Alley Espresso in Seattle
Illustration suggesting Coffee at Ghost Alley Espresso

dark-room.name: Dark Room
dark-room.oneLiner: A Greenwood cocktail bar that's still pouring when everywhere else has closed.
dark-room.blurb: Dark Room mixes drinks on the Greenwood strip and stays open well past eleven.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Dark Room

il-bistro.name: IL Bistro
il-bistro.address: 93 Pike St, Unit A, Seattle, WA  98101
il-bistro.oneLiner: Duck out of the market crowds for a sit-down Italian dinner.
il-bistro.blurb: IL Bistro gives Pike Place Market a proper Italian dining room away from the snack stalls.

photos.alt: IL Bistro in Seattle
Illustration suggesting Italian at IL Bistro

le-coin.name: Le Coin
le-coin.oneLiner: Get the eggs benedict and a round of mini apple fritters.
le-coin.blurb: Fremont's Le Coin handles a celebratory brunch or a natural wine daytime date with ease. The eggs benedict with smoky ham, crispy potatoes, and mustard seed hollandaise is essential, as are the little apple fritters. The breakfast sandwich with pork belly, arugula, pepperoncini, radish, and fried eggs on a seedy bun is also excellent.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting French at Le Coin

il-terrazzo-carmine.name: Il Terrazzo Carmine
il-terrazzo-carmine.oneLiner: Book this old-school Pioneer Square Italian for a classic date night.
il-terrazzo-carmine.blurb: Il Terrazzo Carmine has long been a Pioneer Square standby for traditional Italian dinners. It suits a romantic evening, and that early drink deal is a lower-cost way to experience it.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Il Terrazzo Carmine

petoskey-s-sports-bar.name: Petoskey's Sports Bar
petoskey-s-sports-bar.oneLiner: Fremont's go-to for watching the game with a big, loud group.
petoskey-s-sports-bar.blurb: Bring the whole crew to Petoskey's Sports Bar in Fremont for the game, bar food, and a late close.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bar Food at Petoskey's Sports Bar

lenox.name: Lenox
lenox.oneLiner: Bring the parents to Belltown for a Latin American dinner.
lenox.blurb: Lenox serves Latin American food in Belltown, and it works well for a meal with your folks.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Latin American at Lenox

aladdin-gyro-cery.name: Aladdin Gyro-Cery
aladdin-gyro-cery.oneLiner: Skip the other falafel joints near campus and come straight here.
aladdin-gyro-cery.blurb: Of all the falafel options around the University District, Aladdin Gyro-Cery should stay on your list. The falafel comes out shatteringly crisp, and the tahini sauce is good enough to sip. Orders move fast for takeout, though you can also settle into the couches in back with feta fries.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Mediterranean at Aladdin Gyro-Cery

snapshot-brewing.name: Snapshot Brewing
snapshot-brewing.oneLiner: A Greenwood brewery with room enough to bring the whole crew along.
snapshot-brewing.blurb: Big groups can spread out over a round of beers at Snapshot Brewing, a brewery in Greenwood.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Beer at Snapshot Brewing

unicorn.name: Unicorn
unicorn.oneLiner: Capitol Hill's late arcade bar, for people who will actually take a turn.
unicorn.blurb: Unicorn is Capitol Hill's arcade bar, open late and meant to be played in rather than admired. Cocktails and bar food share the floor with the games, and the room belongs to the hill's queer night as much as to anyone who only wanted pinball. Bring people who will take a turn. A hushed date will feel like it opened the wrong door. Something fried helps. A speech about amaro does not.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Unicorn

kamonegi.name: Kamonegi
kamonegi.oneLiner: When nobody can decide on dinner, soba and tempura settle the argument.
kamonegi.blurb: Fremont's Kamonegi ends dinner indecision fast with a pairing of soba and tempura that's hard to beat. The noodles are made by hand, the tempura is crisp, and after a long day of choices it feels good to let the kitchen lead. Book it for a low-key date night.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Japanese at Kamonegi

mt-bagel.name: Mt. Bagel
mt-bagel.oneLiner: Buy a bag of everything bagels and a tub of the spicy scallion schmear.
mt-bagel.blurb: Seattle's bagel scene changed when Mt. Bagel showed up selling them whole, with tubs of schmear to take home. Inside, they're malty, chewy, and a little sweet, and they hold up great frozen and toasted later. The crust's crackle can vary, but the flavor never does, especially on the garlicky everything.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bagels at Mt. Bagel

king-s-hardware.name: King's Hardware
king-s-hardware.oneLiner: Skee-ball, buffalo wings, and a mango slushie if the machine is kind.
king-s-hardware.blurb: King's Hardware is a dim Ballard bar with taxidermy on the walls, baskets of buffalo wings, and two Skee-Ball lanes that turn a round into a score. Slushies rotate. Hope for mango lemonade, then roll anyway. Weekends fill the room without tipping into a shout. Play a game before the second basket arrives, and leave the coaster lecture to a lounge that scheduled its lighting.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bar Food at King's Hardware

tivoli.name: Tivoli
tivoli.oneLiner: Treat the pizza as a side and load up on focaccia and cold noodles.
tivoli.blurb: Tivoli comes from the crews behind Post Alley Pizza and Saint Bread, and the pies at this Fremont spot are excellent. Still, the smart move is building a meal around everything else, like focaccia with tomato nori butter, Philly tomato pie under house ricotta, and chilled noodles in pistachio butter and chili crisp. Share one pizza among four and fill in the rest.

photos.alt: Tivoli in Seattle
photos.credit: Tivoli Movie Theatre, 207 2nd Ave. S., Seattle (CURTIS 99).jpg

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pizza at Tivoli

1988-cocktail-lounge.name: 1988 Cocktail Lounge
1988-cocktail-lounge.oneLiner: Georgetown night owls should keep this cocktail lounge in their back pocket.
1988-cocktail-lounge.blurb: Late-night drinkers in Georgetown land at 1988 Cocktail Lounge for mixed drinks that keep coming well after eleven.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at 1988 Cocktail Lounge

caffe-umbria.name: Caffè Umbria
caffe-umbria.oneLiner: Stop in for an Italian-style espresso before the workday kicks off.
caffe-umbria.blurb: Early risers by the south end of the lake can count on Caffè Umbria for a proper coffee.

photos.alt: Caffè Umbria in Seattle
Illustration suggesting Coffee at Caffè Umbria

bottega-italiana.name: Bottega Italiana
bottega-italiana.oneLiner: Grab a cup of gelato here while you wander the Market.
bottega-italiana.blurb: Italian-style ice cream justifies stopping at stop at Bottega Italiana inside the arcade.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Ice Cream at Bottega Italiana

the-doctor-s-office.name: The Doctor's Office
the-doctor-s-office.oneLiner: Tell the bartender your mood and let them write you a cocktail prescription.
the-doctor-s-office.blurb: Drinks at The Doctor's Office feel like a generous friend is mixing them in their living room. You might be greeted with a splash of Champagne, and the small, dark room holds just a sofa and a marble bar. The menu takes some decoding, so describe what you want and trust the staff. You should book a reservation.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at The Doctor's Office

marmalade.name: Marmalade
marmalade.oneLiner: Order the salted graham in an affogato and forget about the weather.
marmalade.blurb: Whimsical signs out front hint at what's inside Marmalade, a Fremont gelato shop that might spoil you for the rest of the city. The gelato is spun fresh and airy, and the flavors get creative without getting silly. White chocolate tastes rich and buttery, salted graham is nutty and layered, and strawberry lemonade sorbetto is as smooth as soft serve. Go big with the Americano cup or get a scoop drowned in espresso.

photos.alt: Marmalade in Seattle
Illustration suggesting Ice Cream at Marmalade

deep-sea-sugar-salt.name: Deep Sea Sugar & Salt
deep-sea-sugar-salt.oneLiner: The Funfetti slice, with cream cheese frosting and a hint of almond, wins.
deep-sea-sugar-salt.blurb: Deep Sea Sugar & Salt bakes gorgeous layer cakes in Georgetown, with flavors like dark chocolate spiked with local porter or earl grey with bergamot mascarpone. Whole cakes aren't cheap, but slices make an easy treat. People line up before opening, though you can also reserve same-day slices online in the morning.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Dessert at Deep Sea Sugar & Salt

big-max-burger-co.name: Big Max Burger Co
big-max-burger-co.address: 1935 Queen Anne Ave N, Seattle, WA  98109
big-max-burger-co.oneLiner: The bacon-beef burger and herby shoestring fries are worth earning with a hike.
