big-max-burger-co.blurb: Patties topped with special sauce, sharp aged cheddar, sweet onions, and thick-cut pickles are the headliners at Big Max Burger Co. The Nashville-style hot chicken sandwich, glazed with smoky chili and served with plenty of ranch, is just as good. Round things out with a milkshake, kettle corn brussels sprouts, or puffy chicken nuggets and sweet and sour sauce.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Burgers at Big Max Burger Co

la-parisienne-french-bakery.name: La Parisienne French Bakery
la-parisienne-french-bakery.oneLiner: Get a croissant and peel it apart like a cinnamon roll.
la-parisienne-french-bakery.blurb: Belltown's La Parisienne French Bakery makes plenty of tarts and pastries, but the croissants deserve your full attention. Their thick layers unravel in spirals, with a light yeasty flavor, gentle sweetness, and a toasty, sturdy base. It's inexpensive and opens early, so it fits a regular morning routine.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting French Bakery at La Parisienne French Bakery

cafe-campagne.name: Café Campagne
cafe-campagne.oneLiner: Come for weekend brunch, when the room is loud and the bread is crusty.
cafe-campagne.blurb: Café Campagne has been cooking French comfort food in Post Alley for more than forty years, and the dining room still channels a Paris bistro with old posters and lamps made from wine bottles. Dinner is mellow and the steak frites are great, but brunch is when this place comes alive. Market crowds spill in to share fluffy egg dishes and good bread over upbeat music, and the check lands in special-occasion range.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting French at Café Campagne

cactus.name: Cactus
cactus.oneLiner: Hit the happy hour here for tacos and a cold drink near the lake.
cactus.blurb: By the south end of the lake, Cactus is a solid call for tacos, especially once happy hour rolls around.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Mexican at Cactus

mike-s-noodle-house.name: Mike's Noodle House
mike-s-noodle-house.oneLiner: Bring cash, order the brisket noodles, and add a bowl of congee.
mike-s-noodle-house.blurb: Two neon signs under the red awning spell it out, congee and noodles, and Mike's Noodle House has been nailing both for years in the CID. Springy egg noodles come loaded with tender brisket and bright greens, while the congee is thick, warm, and soothing. The small dining room hums with chatter and fast service. It's cash only, so stop at the ATM first.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Chinese (Noodles at Mike's Noodle House

bar-sabine.name: Bar Sabine
bar-sabine.oneLiner: Claim an alley table, order the eggplant dip, and take your time.
bar-sabine.blurb: Most Ballard patios are wedged onto the sidewalk, but Bar Sabine has an entire alley to itself, with heaters, plenty of tables, and a floral mural. Cocktails are intricate but balanced, built from things like rhubarb Aperol, sandalwood, and pistachio, sometimes with a dusting of glitter. Pair one with smoked eggplant dip, house potato chips, and other Mediterranean small plates, and know that the bar keeps going late.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Bar Sabine

g-h-pasta-pizza.name: G.H. Pasta & Pizza
g-h-pasta-pizza.oneLiner: A West Seattle neighborhood pick when the family can't agree between pizza and pasta.
g-h-pasta-pizza.blurb: Locals lean on G.H. Pasta & Pizza for West Seattle pizza and pasta nights.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pizza at G.H. Pasta & Pizza

many-bennies.name: Many Bennies
many-bennies.oneLiner: Cheap scoops in Wallingford, no planning required, just show up hungry.
many-bennies.blurb: Inexpensive ice cream in Wallingford is the whole pitch at Many Bennies, and you can just walk in.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Ice Cream at Many Bennies

pike-place-market.name: Pike Place Market
pike-place-market.oneLiner: Go early on a weekday, graze the stalls, and watch the fish fly.
pike-place-market.blurb: Seattle's famous public market opens early, and a weekday morning is the best time to wander before the crowds arrive. Pike Place Market rewards grazing, with produce, flowers, baked goods, and seafood counters at every turn.

photos.alt: Pike Place Market in Seattle
photos.credit: Blown Glass for sale in Pike Place Market, Seattle, Washington, 2025.jpg

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Market at Pike Place Market

cotto-belltown.name: Cotto Belltown
cotto-belltown.oneLiner: Late Italian in Belltown for when a bar menu just won't do.
cotto-belltown.blurb: Cotto Belltown serves Italian food and keeps the kitchen going late, which counts for a lot around here.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Cotto Belltown

pasta-casalinga.name: Pasta Casalinga
pasta-casalinga.oneLiner: Get the pomodoro with burrata and leave space for the ricotta crostata.
pasta-casalinga.blurb: Inside Pike Place Market, Pasta Casalinga turns out handmade bowls that would hold their own in Italy. The rotating menu pulls from ocean, garden, and farm, think rigatoni with lamb and juniper ragu or spaghettoni tossed in kale pesto. The best bowl is the simplest one, pomodoro topped with a cool spoonful of burrata. If the ricotta chocolate crostata is on, order it, and bring your parents.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Pasta Casalinga

bongos-cafe.name: Bongos Cafe
bongos-cafe.oneLiner: After a Green Lake loop, bring the dog and order jerk chicken.
bongos-cafe.blurb: Bongos Cafe lives in a brightly painted old gas station by the lake, and the beachy patio always feels like a party. The jerk chicken is excellent, the Caribbean sandwiches stand up to the best around, and the fried yucca balls come filled with molten cheese. Wash it all down with a coconut-heavy piña, and brace yourself for the spicy shrimp.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cuban at Bongos Cafe

toasted-bagels-coffee.name: TOASTED Bagels & Coffee
toasted-bagels-coffee.oneLiner: An early, inexpensive U District stop for a bagel before class.
toasted-bagels-coffee.blurb: Bagels and coffee at TOASTED Bagels & Coffee start early in the U District, and prices stay low.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bagels at TOASTED Bagels & Coffee

paper-fan-cocktail-bar.name: Paper Fan Cocktail Bar
paper-fan-cocktail-bar.address: 601 E Pike St, Unit 100, Seattle, WA  98122
paper-fan-cocktail-bar.oneLiner: Order the Lychee Blossom and bring a first date up to the loft.
paper-fan-cocktail-bar.blurb: Most trips to Biang Biang Noodles end face-first in a bowl of mala beef, but look up next time. Behind red velvet curtains sits Paper Fan Cocktail Bar, a snug loft dressed with ornate lamps and delicate fans. A few of the tea-based drinks lean medicinal, though the Lychee Blossom, made with gin, green tea, and lemon, drinks bright and easy. It fills up fast, so reserve ahead for a first date.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Paper Fan Cocktail Bar

maripili-tapas-bar.name: Maripili Tapas Bar
maripili-tapas-bar.oneLiner: The best tapas in town, and the right call for a double date.
maripili-tapas-bar.blurb: Galician cooking with a light hand and real restraint is the draw at Maripili Tapas Bar on Capitol Hill. Expect ling cod in a sharp, tangy fish broth, manchego gnocchi, a runny-centered tortilla de patata, and garlic aioli on just about everything. Come with another couple, mark a low-key celebration, or sit solo at the bar and graze. The wine list leans Spanish and Washington.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Spanish at Maripili Tapas Bar

beast-cleaver.name: Beast & Cleaver
beast-cleaver.oneLiner: Book the weekend tasting dinner for a nonstop parade of beautifully cooked meat.
beast-cleaver.blurb: By day Beast & Cleaver is a high-end Ballard butcher shop, and late in the week it turns into a tasting-menu restaurant showing off what it sells. The five-course dinner moves from beef carpaccio or rabbit rillette through clever middle courses, like a duck galantine paired with pork mousseline. Sundays bring themed meat dinners, sometimes built around a striking charcuterie board.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Butcher at Beast & Cleaver

red-mill-burgers.name: Red Mill Burgers
red-mill-burgers.oneLiner: Get onion rings to dunk in fry sauce, plus a mint truffle shake.
red-mill-burgers.blurb: Nobody comes to Red Mill Burgers for gourmet toppings or atmosphere. You come for a charbroiled diner-style patty, cornmeal-crusted onion rings dunked in fry sauce, and a thick shake in flavors like s'mores. Grab a spot at one of the bright red picnic tables, ideally after a hike or a slow afternoon around Phinney Ridge.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Burgers at Red Mill Burgers

re-public.name: Re:public
re-public.oneLiner: Call here when you need a last-minute birthday table for a dozen friends.
re-public.blurb: The menu at Re:public dresses up comfort food, with burgers, Nashville hot chicken sandwiches, and mac and cheese loaded with prawns and pork belly. It's more about the mood than the cooking, especially in summer when the garage doors roll up. Groups can usually claim a section of the bar with little notice, the kitchen stays open late, and there's a happy hour too.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting New American at Re:public

rob-roy.name: Rob Roy
rob-roy.oneLiner: Settle into a dark corner and order something stirred, strong, and classic.
rob-roy.blurb: A dark, grown-up Belltown bar, Rob Roy takes cocktails seriously without getting precious about them. Happy hour is the smart way in, and the bartenders are as comfortable with the classics as with their own inventions.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Rob Roy

life-on-mars.name: Life on Mars
life-on-mars.oneLiner: Come for the vinyl wall then linger over a late cocktail.
life-on-mars.blurb: Thousands of records line the walls at Life on Mars, a Capitol Hill cocktail bar where the music matters as much as the drinks. The bar runs late, so it's an easy final stop.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Life on Mars

mashiko-japanese-restaurant.name: Mashiko Japanese Restaurant
mashiko-japanese-restaurant.oneLiner: A West Seattle sushi bar that takes sourcing as seriously as the knife work.
mashiko-japanese-restaurant.blurb: Mashiko Japanese Restaurant has anchored the West Seattle sushi scene for years, known for its focus on sustainably sourced fish.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sushi at Mashiko Japanese Restaurant

bar-del-corso.name: Bar Del Corso
bar-del-corso.oneLiner: Neapolitan pies with real char and crispness make this a Beacon Hill classic.
bar-del-corso.blurb: A big, leisurely dinner at Bar Del Corso ranks among the most reliably happy nights in Seattle. Neapolitan pizza and small plates keep this Beacon Hill Italian spot packed most evenings. The crust is charred with a light crispness all the way through, a welcome contrast to the floppier pies around town.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Bar Del Corso

darkalino-s.name: Darkalino's
darkalino-s.oneLiner: Grab a bar seat solo and twirl through a plate of amatriciana.
darkalino-s.blurb: Darkalino's took over the old London Plane space in Pioneer Square, keeping the towering columns, huge windows, and all that brick. The all-day Italian menu is casual, and the pasta all'amatriciana is the thing to get. Romance isn't really the vibe, so come alone or bring a crew of friends while wedding-reception hits play overhead.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Darkalino's

sushi-by-scratch-restaurants.name: Sushi by Scratch Restaurants
sushi-by-scratch-restaurants.oneLiner: Book the counter for a parade of nigiri and a seriously special night.
sushi-by-scratch-restaurants.blurb: Sushi by Scratch Restaurants runs an intimate omakase counter in Belltown where chefs work through a long series of creative nigiri right in front of you. It's a special-occasion check, seatings run late, and it's a strong move for impressing visiting parents.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sushi at Sushi by Scratch Restaurants

lowrider-cookie-company.name: Lowrider Cookie Company
lowrider-cookie-company.address: 2407 E Union St, Unit C, Seattle, WA 98122
lowrider-cookie-company.oneLiner: Pick up a box of cookies and an ice cream treat on your way home.
lowrider-cookie-company.blurb: Cookies and ice cream are the business at Lowrider Cookie Company in the Central District.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Dessert at Lowrider Cookie Company

la-palmera.name: La Palmera
la-palmera.oneLiner: Grab tacos at La Palmera when South Lake Union wants something with salsa.
la-palmera.blurb: La Palmera serves tacos and other Mexican staples in South Lake Union.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Mexican at La Palmera

japonessa-sushi-cocina.name: Japonessa Sushi Cocina
japonessa-sushi-cocina.oneLiner: Come for pico-topped rolls and sukiyaki tacos when you want a flashy dinner.
japonessa-sushi-cocina.blurb: Japonessa Sushi Cocina mixes sushi with Latin flavors, so rolls get salsa and tortillas get filled with beef sukiyaki. It's loud, touristy, and busy even midweek, but the fish is reliably good. Happy hour and a late kitchen make it an easy Downtown call.

photos.alt: Japonessa Sushi Cocina in Seattle
photos.credit: Corner of 1st Ave and Union St, Seattle, circa 1903 (MOHAI 8997).jpg

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sushi at Japonessa Sushi Cocina

cookie-s-country-chicken.name: Cookie’s Country Chicken
cookie-s-country-chicken.oneLiner: Fried chicken from a counter, which is exactly how lunch should go.
cookie-s-country-chicken.blurb: A no-fuss Pioneer Square counter, Cookie’s Country Chicken is all about the fried bird.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Fried Chicken at Cookie’s Country Chicken

cafe-hagen.name: Café Hagen
cafe-hagen.oneLiner: Settle onto the astroturf patio with a lavender oat milk latte.
cafe-hagen.blurb: Built around the Danish idea of hygge, Café Hagen is a cozy escape amid South Lake Union's tech offices. There's an astroturf patio, lavender oat lattes, and enough houseplants to make the whole place feel calm, and the door opens before nine.

photos.alt: Café Hagen in Seattle
photos.credit: Cafe Hagen at 1252 Thomas Street, South Lake Union, Seattle - 5 (cropped).jpg

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at Café Hagen

lola.name: Lola
lola.oneLiner: Order the doughnuts with mascarpone for the table and break the ice.
lola.blurb: Lola brings Greek cooking to Belltown in a room that lands right between casual and upscale, which makes it ideal for having a new partner meet your parents. Brunch calls for the seasonal scramble, and dinner calls for the lamb burger. Then get the cinnamon doughnuts, which come with vanilla bean mascarpone and a fruit compote, and eat one in a single bite.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Greek at Lola

wa-z.name: wa'z
wa-z.oneLiner: Save the kaiseki menu for an occasion, and savor the sushi courses most.
wa-z.blurb: Near the Space Needle, where most restaurants disappoint, wa'z quietly serves an excellent kaiseki menu on beautiful dinnerware. The eight courses change monthly but usually include soup, a generous piece of wagyu, and terrific sushi, often brightened with yuzu and mirin. Flavors lean subtle rather than flashy. It's a special-occasion check.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Japanese at wa'z

cafe-flora.name: Cafe Flora
cafe-flora.oneLiner: Bring your meat-loving friends and don't mention that everything here is vegetarian.
cafe-flora.blurb: Take your carnivore friends to Cafe Flora and maybe skip the part where you mention it's meat-free. Smoked mozzarella pizza and mushroom risotto make a real argument for meatless cooking, and the airy greenhouse feel of the room helps too. The door opens before nine, so brunch is fair game.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Vegetarian at Cafe Flora

sen-noodle-bar.name: Sen Noodle Bar
sen-noodle-bar.oneLiner: A Ballard noodle bar to remember when a big bowl sounds right.
sen-noodle-bar.blurb: Chinese noodle bowls are the focus at Sen Noodle Bar in Ballard.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Chinese at Sen Noodle Bar

afternoon-tea-at-fairmont-olympic-hotel.name: Afternoon Tea at Fairmont Olympic Hotel
afternoon-tea-at-fairmont-olympic-hotel.oneLiner: Claim a stool along the round center bar and play hotel guest for an evening.
afternoon-tea-at-fairmont-olympic-hotel.blurb: Afternoon Tea at Fairmont Olympic Hotel sits inside one of downtown's grandest old lobbies, where it's easy to pretend you have a room upstairs. Skip the hidden speakeasy and take a stool at the circular counter at the center of the room. The cocktails hold up well, with pairings like cognac and orgeat or tequila with chocolate bitters.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Afternoon Tea at Afternoon Tea at Fairmont Olympic Hotel

w-living-room-bar.name: W Living Room Bar
w-living-room-bar.oneLiner: A sleek downtown hotel lounge for a late cocktail after dinner.
w-living-room-bar.blurb: Inside the downtown W hotel, W Living Room Bar pours pricier cocktails late into the night.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at W Living Room Bar

pike-place-chowder.name: Pike Place Chowder

orderThis.note: The bowl the stall is named for.

pike-place-chowder.oneLiner: Classic clam chowder, cheap and hot, is the only order that matters here.
pike-place-chowder.blurb: Pike Place Chowder has turned a cup of New England clam chowder into a market ritual, and it's inexpensive enough to grab on a whim. Expect a line at peak hours, then take your bowl outside.

photos.alt: Pike Place Chowder in Seattle
Illustration suggesting Seafood at Pike Place Chowder

young-s-restaurant.name: Young's Restaurant
young-s-restaurant.oneLiner: Order Mickey Mouse pancakes and Mongolian beef at the same table.
young-s-restaurant.blurb: Out in White Center, Young's Restaurant serves American diner breakfasts alongside a long list of Chinese and Thai dishes. Picture deep booths, checkered floors, and little creamer cups on every table. It's ideal on a Sunday morning when nobody agrees, since one person can get an omelette with hash browns while another orders garlic fried chicken and crab rangoons.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Chinese at Young's Restaurant

slim-goody.name: Slim Goody
slim-goody.oneLiner: A Ballard bar with easygoing bar food for low-effort nights out.
slim-goody.blurb: Bar food and drinks are what you'll find at Slim Goody in Ballard.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bar Food at Slim Goody

jack-s-bbq.name: Jack's BBQ
jack-s-bbq.oneLiner: Get the pulled chicken sandwich with slaw plus a bowl of queso mac.
jack-s-bbq.blurb: The South Lake Union outpost of Jack's BBQ outshines the SoDo original, and it's easy to find a table even at lunch. The room has a laid-back honky-tonk feel. Order a barbecue-sauced pulled chicken sandwich topped with slaw, with queso mac and cheese alongside.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting BBQ at Jack's BBQ

musang.name: Musang
musang.oneLiner: Filipino cooking on Beacon Hill worth dressing up for, parents or date in tow.
musang.blurb: Musang turns Filipino food into a full-on celebration on Beacon Hill, and you are paying for the room too. Bring a date or bring the folks, and order plenty to share.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Filipino at Musang

starbucks-coffee-company.name: Starbucks Coffee Company
starbucks-coffee-company.oneLiner: Visit once for the history, then drink your daily coffee somewhere quieter.
starbucks-coffee-company.blurb: Tourists line up at the market's Starbucks Coffee Company for the vintage logo and bragging rights to the brand's oldest store. It opens early, so arrive before the crowds if you want the souvenir mug without the wait.

photos.alt: Starbucks Coffee Company in Seattle
Illustration suggesting Coffee at Starbucks Coffee Company

delancey.name: Delancey

orderThis.note: A whole pie, not a novelty topping.

delancey.oneLiner: Ballard's candlelit wood-fired pies prove Seattle belongs in the great pizza conversation.
delancey.blurb: Seattle can hold its own as a pizza town, and Delancey is the proof. Start with burrata swimming in pesto or the towering Jersey Salad, then focus on the blistered pies topped with fennel sausage, sweet Walla Walla onions, or kalamatas. The dim room smells like the oven and works for date night or dinner with the family.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pizza at Delancey

andaluca-restaurant.name: Andaluca Restaurant
andaluca-restaurant.oneLiner: A downtown Mediterranean dining room that starts serving before nine.
andaluca-restaurant.blurb: Downtown early birds can get Mediterranean food at Andaluca Restaurant, which opens in time for a breakfast meeting.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Mediterranean at Andaluca Restaurant

voodoo-doughnut.name: Voodoo Doughnut
voodoo-doughnut.oneLiner: Grab a bacon maple bar at an hour when nothing else is open.
voodoo-doughnut.blurb: Voodoo Doughnut brings its Portland weirdness to Capitol Hill, with cheap, over-the-top doughnuts available early in the morning and late at night.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Donuts at Voodoo Doughnut

geraldine-s-counter.name: Geraldine's Counter
geraldine-s-counter.oneLiner: Go on a weekday morning and claim a swivel stool at the counter.
geraldine-s-counter.blurb: Every neighborhood deserves a diner as cheerful as Geraldine's Counter, where the coffee refills never stop coming. Take a window seat, soak up the Rainier Avenue light, and work through crisp french toast and thick-cut bacon. Weekend waits run long, so a quieter weekday is the smarter play.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Breakfast & Brunch at Geraldine's Counter

royal-grinders.name: Royal Grinders
royal-grinders.oneLiner: Split the Italian with a friend, or don't, and grab a bag of chips.
royal-grinders.blurb: Proper East Coast-style subs are rare in Seattle, which makes Royal Grinders in Fremont a real asset. The Italian is what you should request, stacked with pepperoni, salami, ham, provolone, swiss, and chopped pepperoncini on bread that's crisp outside and soft within, plus a ranch spread you'll want to take home. Every sandwich here is massive, so sharing is reasonable.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sandwiches at Royal Grinders

post-alley-pizza.name: Post Alley Pizza
post-alley-pizza.oneLiner: Grab a charred, chewy slice and shake on more garlic than seems reasonable.
post-alley-pizza.blurb: Ignore the name, because Post Alley Pizza isn't actually in the market. It's a dependable downtown lunch slice with a crust that manages to be both blistered and chewy, plus dipping sauces like house ranch and a Calabrian chili buffalo. The real perk is a shaker of granulated garlic, which almost no other slice shop in town bothers to put out.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pizza at Post Alley Pizza

messina.name: Messina
messina.oneLiner: Save this Lower Queen Anne Italian spot for your next date night.
messina.blurb: For an Italian date night by Seattle Center, Messina is a strong call.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Messina

capitale-pizzeria.name: Capitale Pizzeria
capitale-pizzeria.oneLiner: A Capitol Hill pizza stop that earns a spot in the regular rotation.
capitale-pizzeria.blurb: For pizza on Capitol Hill, Capitale Pizzeria lands on the neighborhood's shortlist of reliable pies.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pizza at Capitale Pizzeria

mirabelle-by-orphee.name: Mirabelle by Orphée
mirabelle-by-orphee.oneLiner: An early Pioneer Square stop for French pastry on the way to work.
mirabelle-by-orphee.blurb: Mirabelle by Orphée opens early in Pioneer Square with inexpensive French pastries for the morning commute.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting French Bakery at Mirabelle by Orphée

arashi-ramen.name: Arashi Ramen
arashi-ramen.oneLiner: A dependable Ballard bowl of ramen when the drizzle sets in.
arashi-ramen.blurb: When the weather turns gray, Arashi Ramen has steaming bowls of noodles waiting in Ballard.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Ramen at Arashi Ramen

temple-pastries.name: Temple Pastries
temple-pastries.oneLiner: Get the caramelized shallot croissant first, then let the pastry case talk you into more.
temple-pastries.blurb: The pastries at Temple Pastries look almost too pretty to eat, though you'll get over that fast. Start with the croissant packed with jammy shallots and gruyere, then add a pistachio schnecken or a blood orange Campari cake donut. A few macarons for later never hurt, and nothing in this early-opening Central District bakery will dent your wallet.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at Temple Pastries

the-diller-room.name: The Diller Room
the-diller-room.oneLiner: Grab a marble barstool under the neon glow and order something classic.
the-diller-room.blurb: The Diller Room has been pouring drinks in some form for more than a hundred years, which puts it ahead of the Space Needle. At night the marble bar picks up light from the old Diller Hotel neon sign, and the menu mixes old standards with modern cocktails. The crowd is friendly and very Seattle.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at The Diller Room

fuji-bakery.name: Fuji Bakery
fuji-bakery.oneLiner: Get the curry bread warm and a few pastries for later.
fuji-bakery.blurb: Fuji Bakery brings Japanese bakery sensibilities to Queen Anne, with flaky French-style pastries alongside savory buns. The crunchy curry bread is a must, and prices stay low enough to grab extras before the street is busy.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at Fuji Bakery

uneeda-burger.name: Uneeda Burger
uneeda-burger.oneLiner: A no-fuss Fremont counter for a cheap burger without a reservation.
uneeda-burger.blurb: Walk in, order at the counter, and Uneeda Burger will hand you an inexpensive burger in Fremont.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Burgers at Uneeda Burger

harry-s-beach-house.name: Harry's Beach House
harry-s-beach-house.oneLiner: Grab a rooftop seat on a clear day and order the seafood.
harry-s-beach-house.blurb: Harry's Beach House brings seafood, an open-air roof deck, and morning hours to West Seattle.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at Harry's Beach House

backyard-bagel.name: Backyard Bagel
backyard-bagel.oneLiner: Start a Fremont morning with an inexpensive bagel before the crowds wake up.
backyard-bagel.blurb: Early Fremont mornings stay cheap and well fed thanks to Backyard Bagel.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bagels at Backyard Bagel

gelatiamo.name: Gelatiamo
gelatiamo.oneLiner: Order the rice gelato, which tastes like rice pudding straight from the freezer.
gelatiamo.blurb: Gelatiamo scoops the city's best gelato and gets you as close to a Roman vacation as Downtown Seattle allows. Every flavor is solid, stracciatella included, but the rice flavor is the one people talk about. It's creamy, gently sweet, and refreshingly free of cinnamon.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Ice Cream at Gelatiamo

family-donut.name: Family Donut
family-donut.address: 2100 N Northgate Way, Unit F, Seattle, WA 98133
family-donut.oneLiner: Get the buttermilk bar and a fruit-glazed donut, and arrive early on weekends.
family-donut.blurb: Family Donut in Northgate makes the city's best donuts for very little money. Glazes get their flavor from real blueberries, orange zest, and raspberry, while old fashioneds stay tender inside under crunchy ridges. You'll even get a free donut hole on a stick as you leave, but show up early on Saturday and Sunday before the cases empty.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Donuts at Family Donut

pizza-by-ruffin.name: Pizza by Ruffin
pizza-by-ruffin.address: 400 Fairview Ave N, Ste 107, Seattle, WA  98109
pizza-by-ruffin.oneLiner: Roman-style squares this crunchy are reason enough to rethink your weekday lunch.
pizza-by-ruffin.blurb: Tucked into a slim corner of an office-tower food court, Pizza by Ruffin sells al taglio slabs with a serious crackle. The margherita and the pepperoni are dependable, but the fun is in the odd ones, like mushroom lit up with green Jamaican curry or squash paired with brie. South Lake Union has never had much good pizza, so this counts as real progress.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pizza at Pizza by Ruffin

stampede-cocktail-club.name: Stampede Cocktail Club
stampede-cocktail-club.oneLiner: Pair a blueberry mule with dumplings and enjoy the dinosaur staring at you.
stampede-cocktail-club.blurb: At first glance Stampede Cocktail Club reads as a vintage-leaning cocktail bar, until you round a corner and come face to face with a dinosaur head hung against floral wallpaper. The drinks are excellent, including a blueberry mule and a passionfruit margarita with pineapple, and the steamed dumplings come from Little Ting's. It's fun for a date and open late.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Stampede Cocktail Club

some-random-bar.name: Some Random Bar
some-random-bar.oneLiner: Keep this bar in your pocket for dates, groups, and casual catchups alike.
some-random-bar.blurb: Great cocktails, a good crowd, and a menu that runs from burrata to crab nachos make Some Random Bar a dependable Belltown default. There's a patio for warm nights and the bar stays open late. Just warn your friends that it's a real name, not a vague suggestion.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Some Random Bar

olympia-coffee.name: Olympia Coffee
olympia-coffee.oneLiner: A sharp downtown espresso stop for people who actually care about the beans.
olympia-coffee.blurb: Downtown commuters get an early start with Olympia Coffee and its well-regarded roasts.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at Olympia Coffee

the-george.name: The George
the-george.oneLiner: Dress up, sit at the bar, and order the lamb agnolotti with fries.
the-george.blurb: The George brings real glamour to the renovated Fairmont Olympic Hotel, and it's somewhere you can dress up without feeling silly. The menu runs long, from seafood towers to pasta, and not all of it lands, so skip the steak and duck. Go for lamb agnolotti in parmesan broth and a side of fries with some bubbles. Expect a special-occasion bill.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pacific Northwest at The George

sugo-hand-roll-bar.name: Sugo Hand Roll Bar
sugo-hand-roll-bar.oneLiner: Sit at the counter, fill out the card, and order cold sake.
sugo-hand-roll-bar.blurb: Downtown is short on quality sushi lunches, so Sugo Hand Roll Bar at Pike Place fills a real gap with hand rolls built on excellent fish. The four-sided counter looks a bit like an airport bar, yet the room manages to feel calm and lively at once, with blowtorches searing king salmon on a pink salt block. Mark your order on the sheet at your seat and get a carafe of chilled sake.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sushi at Sugo Hand Roll Bar

stoneburner.name: Stoneburner
stoneburner.oneLiner: Skip the pasta, share a few pies, and settle in with a cocktail.
stoneburner.blurb: Neapolitan pizza and pasta share the menu at Stoneburner, but only one of them deserves your attention. Treat it as an upscale pizzeria in Ballard, with drinks, a few appetizers to pass around, and a couple of blistered pies. The dark, handsome room handles dates and group dinners equally well.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Mediterranean at Stoneburner

pono-ranch.name: Pono Ranch
pono-ranch.oneLiner: Hawaiian bar food and a kitchen open past eleven make an easy Ballard nightcap.
pono-ranch.blurb: Hawaiian plates and a late-running kitchen make Pono Ranch a handy stop on any Ballard bar crawl.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Hawaiian at Pono Ranch

maiz.name: Maíz
maiz.oneLiner: Skip the seafood for once and eat fresh masa tamales at the market.
maiz.blurb: Pike Place pushes everyone toward seafood, but Maíz makes a strong case for corn instead. This bright tortilleria grinds its own nixtamal masa and presses tortillas you'll want to eat every week. That masa shows up in tacos, tamales, and chips with a serious, shattering crunch.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Mexican at Maíz

nikko-teriyaki.name: Nikko Teriyaki
nikko-teriyaki.oneLiner: The best teriyaki chicken in West Seattle is worth every extra minute.
nikko-teriyaki.blurb: Expect a slightly longer wait at Nikko Teriyaki, because the chicken here is cooked low and slow. It lands somewhere between grilled and braised, with a beautiful sear, a gingery sauce, and a salad dressed with a sour-apple kick. Nobody in West Seattle does it better.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Teriyaki at Nikko Teriyaki

the-dressing-room.name: The Dressing Room
the-dressing-room.oneLiner: A late-night Pike Place stop for a cocktail or a glass of wine.
the-dressing-room.blurb: Near Pike Place Market, The Dressing Room pours cocktails and wine until late.

photos.alt: The Dressing Room in Seattle
photos.credit: The dressing room scene from "The Chorus Lady" (SAYRE 12356).jpg

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at The Dressing Room

di-fiora.name: Di Fiora
di-fiora.oneLiner: A First Hill Asian fusion spot to keep in mind for weeknights.
di-fiora.blurb: Di Fiora cooks Asian fusion dishes for the First Hill neighborhood.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Asian Fusion at Di Fiora

the-butcher-s-table.name: The Butcher's Table
the-butcher-s-table.oneLiner: A polished steakhouse for when you want serious beef without the downtown scene.
the-butcher-s-table.blurb: Steak is the whole point at The Butcher's Table, a polished spot in the Denny Triangle near South Lake Union.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Steakhouse at The Butcher's Table

molly-moon-s.name: Molly Moon's
molly-moon-s.oneLiner: Honey lavender in a waffle cone is the late-night move on Capitol Hill.
molly-moon-s.blurb: Molly Moon's has been Seattle's go-to scoop shop for years, and this location stays open late. Salted caramel and honey lavender are the classics to know.

photos.alt: Molly Moon's in Seattle
Illustration suggesting Ice Cream at Molly Moon's

ada-s-restaurant-bar.name: Ada's Restaurant & Bar
ada-s-restaurant-bar.oneLiner: Bring the parents here for a Turkish dinner that feels like an occasion.
ada-s-restaurant-bar.blurb: For a dressed-up Turkish meal in Phinney Ridge, Ada's Restaurant & Bar carries a special-occasion check that works well with family in tow.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Turkish at Ada's Restaurant & Bar

footprint-wine-tap.name: Footprint Wine Tap
footprint-wine-tap.address: 1222 E Madison St, Suite c, Seattle, WA 98122
footprint-wine-tap.oneLiner: A low-key weeknight hang for anyone who actually likes talking about grapes.
footprint-wine-tap.blurb: The taps behind the bar at Footprint Wine Tap give away its past life as a growler fill station, but now every line pours wine. It's a mellow Capitol Hill stop for people who genuinely care about viticulture. There's even a trivia game to test your vineyard knowledge.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Wine at Footprint Wine Tap

lonely-siren.name: Lonely Siren
lonely-siren.oneLiner: Head up to the rooftop for a late drink above Pike Place.
lonely-siren.blurb: Lonely Siren brings Portuguese cooking to Pike Place Market, with a roof deck and a kitchen that runs late.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Portuguese at Lonely Siren

hi-spot-cafe.name: Hi Spot Cafe
hi-spot-cafe.oneLiner: Order the breakfast burrito and plan to skip lunch entirely.
hi-spot-cafe.blurb: Set in a converted Madrona house, Hi Spot Cafe still feels warm and homey, with tables spread across the upstairs rooms. The pancakes and scrambles are solid, but the hulking breakfast burrito with black beans, eggs, and vegetables is the order. It arrives with potatoes, tomatillo salsa, and sour cream you should spread over every bite.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Breakfast & Brunch at Hi Spot Cafe

coffeeholic-house.name: Coffeeholic House
coffeeholic-house.oneLiner: Come early for a strong, sweet coffee and a seat to settle in.
coffeeholic-house.blurb: Coffeeholic House pours Vietnamese-leaning coffee drinks in Columbia City, and the doors open early.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at Coffeeholic House

lil-red-s.name: Lil Red's
lil-red-s.oneLiner: Get takeout from Lil Red's when the week calls for Jamaican comfort food.
lil-red-s.blurb: Lil Red's in Columbia City cooks Jamaican barbecue and soul food that works as a reset button on a stressful week. Every plate from this kitchen leans hard into comfort, and it's still a top takeout pick. It opens early, too.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting BBQ at Lil Red's

mr-west-cafe-bar-downtown.name: Mr West Cafe Bar Downtown
mr-west-cafe-bar-downtown.oneLiner: Bring the laptop, order a matcha latte, and camp out all day.
mr-west-cafe-bar-downtown.blurb: If you need somewhere to work all day without going hungry, Mr West Cafe Bar Downtown is the answer. The room is all plants, marble, and gold accents, which suits curried avocado toast and a green tea latte. Lunch brings polished panini and salads, and later on there are cheese boards and frozen wine slushies.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cafe at Mr West Cafe Bar Downtown

din-tai-fung.name: Din Tai Fung
din-tai-fung.oneLiner: Order the pork soup dumplings by the dozen and don't skip the green beans.
din-tai-fung.blurb: Dumpling makers work behind glass at Din Tai Fung near the university, pleating pork xiao long bao with famously tidy folds. Fill out the table with garlicky green beans and cucumber salad, and expect a wait at peak hours.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Chinese at Din Tai Fung

wild-fish-poke.name: Wild Fish Poke
wild-fish-poke.oneLiner: Grab a poke bowl at the market when you need a quick lunch.
wild-fish-poke.blurb: At Pike Place Market, Wild Fish Poke serves Hawaiian-style poke from a counter.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Poke at Wild Fish Poke

carmelo-s-tacos.name: Carmelo's Tacos
carmelo-s-tacos.oneLiner: Thick handmade tortillas and that chorizo, potato, and cactus filling are the move.
carmelo-s-tacos.blurb: Carmelo's Tacos presses its own hefty tortillas and fills them with well-marinated carne asada or a chorizo, potato, and nopal mix that sticks with you. Burrito people should know the cheese gets a quick sear on the griddle before it goes in. It's cheap, it's fast, and the Capitol Hill counter keeps going late.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Mexican at Carmelo's Tacos

dino-s-tomato-pie.name: Dino's Tomato Pie
dino-s-tomato-pie.oneLiner: Claim the big round booth in back and order garlic knots for the table.
dino-s-tomato-pie.blurb: Dino's Tomato Pie shares owners with Delancey but goes the opposite direction, trading minimalism for dim, old-school pizzeria charm. The charred pies are the draw, and the vodka sauce version is a crowd favorite. Bring your whole crew and try to grab the chandelier booth.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pizza at Dino's Tomato Pie

barolo-ristorante.name: Barolo Ristorante
barolo-ristorante.oneLiner: Belltown Italian for the hour when most kitchens have already closed.
barolo-ristorante.blurb: Late diners can still get a proper Italian meal at Barolo Ristorante, where the kitchen keeps going past eleven.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Barolo Ristorante

firn.name: Firn
firn.oneLiner: Head onto the roof deck for cocktails that stretch well past eleven.
firn.blurb: Firn mixes drinks high above Pioneer Square and keeps going late.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Firn

off-alley.name: Off Alley
off-alley.oneLiner: A Columbia City splurge for a date who appreciates serious cooking.
off-alley.blurb: Off Alley packs a lot of ambition into a tiny Columbia City room, and this is a dressed-up night that makes sense for a date night.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting New American at Off Alley

the-shambles.name: The Shambles
the-shambles.oneLiner: Start with the wagyu bavette and never skip the mushrooms with jammy egg yolk.
the-shambles.blurb: With its dive-bar look and stiff cocktails, The Shambles in Roosevelt doesn't advertise that it's a top-tier steakhouse. A chalkboard lists the cuts, and the wagyu bavette arrives crusty, rosy, and pooled with demiglace. Charred broccolini in a sharp Dijon sauce and creamy herbed mushrooms are just as essential. It works well for dinner with your parents.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting New American (Butcher at The Shambles

ananas-pizzeria.name: Ananas Pizzeria
ananas-pizzeria.oneLiner: Go for the weird pies, like pineapple with togarashi or the dill-heavy Lao one.
ananas-pizzeria.blurb: From the crew behind Taurus Ox, Ananas Pizzeria brings Lao flavors to pizza in First Hill. The stranger the pie, the better, and the namesake with ham, pineapple, and togarashi proves it. The Lao pie with bamboo shoots, lardon, provolone, and piles of dill is another winner, and the room handles a weeknight group dinner well.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pizza at Ananas Pizzeria

sweet-alchemy.name: Sweet Alchemy
sweet-alchemy.oneLiner: Get a scoop of Jitter Bars and chase it with something floral.
sweet-alchemy.blurb: Near campus in the U District, Sweet Alchemy scoops flavors you rarely see, like makgeolli, Persian rose, and smoked chocolate, along with mix-ins made from house-baked cakes and cookie dough. The caramel and espresso shortbread flavor called Jitter Bars is the standout, and the shop is open late enough for a post-study treat.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Ice Cream at Sweet Alchemy

the-angry-beaver.name: The Angry Beaver
the-angry-beaver.oneLiner: Come for hockey on every screen and a plate of poutine for the table.
the-angry-beaver.blurb: Hockey is always on at The Angry Beaver, a Greenwood sports bar where poutine is the move. It handles big groups without fuss.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bar Food at The Angry Beaver

founders-club.name: Founders Club
founders-club.oneLiner: A downtown drinks room for a nightcap that turns into a second round.
founders-club.blurb: Founders Club mixes polished drinks in the Downtown core and keeps the bar open late.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Founders Club

joey-university-village.name: JOEY University Village
joey-university-village.oneLiner: Use this one for a late dinner after a U Village shopping run.
joey-university-village.blurb: JOEY University Village serves New American food by campus and keeps going late.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting New American at JOEY University Village

cantinetta.name: Cantinetta
cantinetta.oneLiner: Bring a date to Wallingford for an Italian dinner that feels relaxed.
cantinetta.blurb: Couples looking for an Italian date night in Wallingford can count on Cantinetta.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Cantinetta

aqua-by-el-gaucho.name: AQUA by El Gaucho
aqua-by-el-gaucho.oneLiner: Come for seafood and stay for the view over the water.
aqua-by-el-gaucho.blurb: Seafood and outdoor seating with a view pull a crowd into AQUA by El Gaucho, a polished Belltown spot.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at AQUA by El Gaucho

joule.name: Joule
joule.oneLiner: Skip the usual steakhouse script and order the kalbi short rib.
joule.blurb: Joule takes the steakhouse formula and runs it through a Korean lens in Wallingford. Kalbi short rib stands in for the usual steak, sides include rice cakes tossed with chorizo and bitter mustard greens, and the bread basket gives way to scallion pancakes topped with salmon roe. Blue Victorian wallpaper and a great patio make it a strong pick for date night or dinner with parents.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Korean at Joule

kangaroo-kiwi.name: Kangaroo & Kiwi
kangaroo-kiwi.oneLiner: Bring a big group here for beers and pub food in Ballard.
kangaroo-kiwi.blurb: Big groups, cold beer, and bar food that runs late make Kangaroo & Kiwi an easy Ballard pick.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bar Food at Kangaroo & Kiwi

the-hart-and-the-hunter.name: The Hart and The Hunter
the-hart-and-the-hunter.oneLiner: An early-opening downtown spot for an American breakfast before a busy day.
the-hart-and-the-hunter.blurb: Downtown's The Hart and The Hunter serves American food starting before the street is busy.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting American at The Hart and The Hunter

luna-park-cafe.name: Luna Park Cafe
luna-park-cafe.oneLiner: Bring the kids for the jukeboxes and order a breakfast pile.
luna-park-cafe.blurb: Sitting under the West Seattle Bridge, Luna Park Cafe is a longtime greasy spoon packed with kitsch, from vintage lunch boxes to a giant guitar and a creepy clown game. Families fill the booths on weekends, with jukeboxes at the tables to keep kids busy. The food is plainer than the decor, but the breakfast piles are a satisfying bet.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Diner at Luna Park Cafe

seattle-dumpling-house.name: Seattle Dumpling House

orderThis.note: Order the dumplings the name promises.

seattle-dumpling-house.oneLiner: Start with the soup dumplings and let the rest of the order follow.
seattle-dumpling-house.blurb: Soup dumplings are the order at Seattle Dumpling House, a Wallingford spot for Chinese dumplings and dim sum.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Chinese (Dumplings at Seattle Dumpling House

rockcreek-seafood-spirits.name: RockCreek Seafood & Spirits
rockcreek-seafood-spirits.oneLiner: Grab a seat on the roof deck and make happy hour a seafood dinner.
rockcreek-seafood-spirits.blurb: Fremont's RockCreek Seafood & Spirits is a lively seafood house with a long menu of fish and shellfish and a solid cocktail list. Happy hour draws a crowd, and when the weather cooperates, the rooftop is where you want to be.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at RockCreek Seafood & Spirits

taurus-ox.name: Taurus Ox
taurus-ox.oneLiner: Bring the parents for Lao food that feels comforting and still like a real night out.
taurus-ox.blurb: Capitol Hill's Taurus Ox cooks Lao food with real heat and funk, and it rewards a table that's willing to share. Order sticky rice no matter what. The room works as well for a date as it does for dinner with your folks.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Lao at Taurus Ox

boat-bar.name: Boat Bar
boat-bar.oneLiner: A Hill bar with serious drinks to keep on your regular rotation.
boat-bar.blurb: On Capitol Hill, Boat Bar is a cocktail stop worth adding to the bar crawl.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Boat Bar

la-loba.name: La Loba
la-loba.oneLiner: Share a spread of Spanish tapas with friends on a Belltown night.
la-loba.blurb: Small Spanish plates made for sharing are the focus at La Loba in Belltown.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Spanish at La Loba

ben-paris.name: Ben Paris
ben-paris.oneLiner: A downtown New American spot that works for a breakfast meeting.
ben-paris.blurb: Downtown breakfast meetings work well at Ben Paris, which serves New American plates from early morning.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting New American at Ben Paris

unlisted.name: Unlisted
unlisted.oneLiner: Order the Eléphante 75 and toast the giant elephant in the corner.
unlisted.blurb: Unlisted hides behind an unmarked alley door inside The Ruins, an event venue in Queen Anne. Dark wood, velvet, a huge elephant statue, and diamond-shaped chandeliers set a moody scene. The cocktails, like the citrusy Sideshow and the Champagne-topped Eléphante 75, are carefully made. Good bars are scarce in this neighborhood, which helps it stand out.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Unlisted

dingfelder-s-delicatessen.name: Dingfelder's Delicatessen
dingfelder-s-delicatessen.oneLiner: Get the pastrami on rye and a pickle, and you're set until dinner.
dingfelder-s-delicatessen.blurb: East Coast Jewish deli energy comes to Capitol Hill at Dingfelder's Delicatessen, where piled-high pastrami sandwiches carry the meal. Morning service starts first and keeps the prices friendly.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sandwiches at Dingfelder's Delicatessen

wild-ginger-mckenzie.name: Wild Ginger McKenzie
wild-ginger-mckenzie.oneLiner: A stylish Denny Triangle spot for Southeast Asian cooking on a weeknight.
wild-ginger-mckenzie.blurb: Over in the Denny Triangle, Wild Ginger McKenzie serves Southeast Asian dishes in a polished setting.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Southeast Asian at Wild Ginger McKenzie

fat-s-chicken-waffles.name: Fat's Chicken & Waffles
fat-s-chicken-waffles.oneLiner: Order the chicken and waffles with Hennessy butter and a spiked fruit punch.
fat-s-chicken-waffles.blurb: Fat's Chicken & Waffles is where you go when the laundry can wait but the craving can't. The waffles are thin and airy with a pat of cognac butter, and the fried chicken holds its crunch even after the drive home. Eat in the laid-back Central District dining room, sweatpants welcome, with a sweet tea or boozy punch.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Soul Food at Fat's Chicken & Waffles

neko.name: Neko
neko.oneLiner: Capitol Hill coffee with a side of cats who may or may not like you.
neko.blurb: Neko lets you sip something warm while hanging out with cats on Capitol Hill, and it's inexpensive and open early.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cat Cafe at Neko

purple-cafe-and-wine-bar.name: Purple Café and Wine Bar
purple-cafe-and-wine-bar.oneLiner: Come for happy hour and stay for a glass from that towering list.
purple-cafe-and-wine-bar.blurb: The centerpiece at Purple Café and Wine Bar is a dramatic tower of wine bottles rising through the middle of a big downtown dining room. The list is long and the American menu is crowd-friendly.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting New American at Purple Café and Wine Bar

needle-and-thread.name: Needle and Thread
needle-and-thread.oneLiner: Skip the menu, name a spirit you like, and let the bartender decide.
needle-and-thread.blurb: Getting into Needle and Thread is half the fun. Book online, walk through Tavern Law, pick up an old phone in the corner, and wait for someone to lead you up a creaky staircase to a vintage parlor. There's no drink list, so tell the bartenders your preferences and they'll build something around them. It's easier to land a seat than you'd think, and it runs late.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Needle and Thread

carmine-s.name: Carmine's
carmine-s.oneLiner: Downtown Italian for when the group wants pasta and a proper sit-down dinner.
carmine-s.blurb: Carmine's brings a sit-down Italian menu to the Downtown core.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Carmine's

tilikum-place-cafe.name: Tilikum Place Café
tilikum-place-cafe.oneLiner: Book ahead for the potato waffle benedict, and let someone else order the dutch baby.
tilikum-place-cafe.blurb: Puffy, sugar-dusted dutch babies made Tilikum Place Café a Belltown brunch fixture, but the supporting cast is the real draw. Think thick-cut bacon, smoked salmon benedict on potato waffles, and bubbling egg skillets layered with gruyere. The small room fills as soon as the doors open, so reserve a table.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting European at Tilikum Place Café

queen-mary-tea-room.name: Queen Mary Tea Room
queen-mary-tea-room.oneLiner: For a proper afternoon tea with all the frills, start your search here.
queen-mary-tea-room.blurb: Ravenna's Queen Mary Tea Room goes all in on the ritual, with aproned servers passing around tea samples and decor that changes with the seasons. Tiered trays come loaded with things like tiny cups of tomato bisque plus fresh fruit for dragging through clotted cream. There's a gluten-free version that holds its own, and the tea list is huge.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Afternoon Tea at Queen Mary Tea Room

fogon-cocina-mexicana.name: Fogón Cocina Mexicana
fogon-cocina-mexicana.oneLiner: Don't leave without the al pastor tacos, and add the boozy fajitas.
fogon-cocina-mexicana.blurb: Fogón Cocina Mexicana is loud in the best way, with lime-green walls and cooks pressing fresh tortillas up front. The fajitas get a splash of tequila, beer, and wine, and they're excellent, but al pastor tacos are the real must. It can hold a crowd dinner or a solo seat at the bar.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Mexican at Fogón Cocina Mexicana

willmott-s-ghost.name: Willmott's Ghost
willmott-s-ghost.oneLiner: Book the Spheres room when a Roman pizza night should feel like a splurge.
willmott-s-ghost.blurb: Renee Erickson's Willmott's Ghost sits inside the Amazon Spheres, a blush-pink room serving Roman-inspired Italian food. Order the Roman-style pizza and pastas, and plan on a special-occasion check.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Willmott's Ghost

mr-fish-chips-chowder.name: Mr. Fish Chips & Chowder
mr-fish-chips-chowder.oneLiner: Fine for a patio break with visitors, but skip the pricey crab.
mr-fish-chips-chowder.blurb: Up at the north end of Pike Place, Mr. Fish Chips & Chowder caters to tourists with a menu that comes and goes in quality. The fried fish is fine, and the bacon-y clam chowder with its Goldfish-style crackers is the strongest play. A breezy patio over Elliott Bay makes it a decent rest stop with guests.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at Mr. Fish Chips & Chowder

the-flora-bakehouse.name: The Flora Bakehouse
the-flora-bakehouse.oneLiner: Take your almond croissant up to the rooftop and call it an afternoon.
the-flora-bakehouse.blurb: Up on a second floor in Beacon Hill, The Flora Bakehouse fills its case with cheddar-chive scones, fudgy vegan brownies, and twice-baked almond croissants that shatter everywhere. The real bonus is the U-shaped rooftop, which turns an iced cardamom rose latte or a soft serve into a lazy afternoon. Beacon Hill can get a scone before the neighborhood alarm clocks go off.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at The Flora Bakehouse

creamy-cone-cafe.name: Creamy Cone Cafe
creamy-cone-cafe.oneLiner: Stack lemon raspberry cheesecake and banana pudding in one waffle cone.
creamy-cone-cafe.blurb: Two scoops define Creamy Cone Cafe in Rainier Beach. The cheesecake flavor is bright and tart, with raspberry ribbons and graham crumbles, and the banana pudding eats like a frozen smoothie loaded with wafer cookies. The folks behind the counter are genuinely warm, and morning service starts first.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Ice Cream at Creamy Cone Cafe

oriental-mart.name: Oriental Mart
oriental-mart.oneLiner: Order the salmon sinigang, follow the signs, and don't rush the cook.
oriental-mart.blurb: In a quiet corner of Pike Place Market, a Filipino counter is wallpapered with handwritten signs pinned up by clothespins, each one warning you to behave. They seem gruff at first and get funnier the longer you read. Oriental Mart backs up the attitude with the best lunch in the market and some of the city's finest Filipino cooking. You can get in before work and won't cost much.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Filipino at Oriental Mart

dick-s-drive-in.name: Dick's Drive-In
dick-s-drive-in.oneLiner: A Deluxe, fries, and a chocolate shake is a Seattle rite of passage.
dick-s-drive-in.blurb: Dick's Drive-In has been slinging cheap burgers, fresh-cut fries, and thick milkshakes since the middle of the last century. Walk up, order fast, and eat in the car like generations of locals before you.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Burgers at Dick's Drive-In

lupo.name: Lupo
lupo.oneLiner: Get a pizza, but make sure someone orders the sausage rigatoni.
lupo.blurb: Fremont's Lupo bakes sourdough pies in a Neapolitan oven, so the crusts come out leopard-spotted with extra chew and tang. Purists can go for the margherita with Samish Bay mozzarella, while the cacio e pepe pie is better with the pancetta add-on. The kitchen makes just one pasta, a creamy tomato rigatoni with sausage, and it's spectacular.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pizza at Lupo

miss-pho.name: Miss Pho
miss-pho.oneLiner: Order the phở hà nội and drop that raw yolk right in.
miss-pho.blurb: It looks like any strip-mall Vietnamese spot in Greenwood, but Miss Pho cooks well above the setting. Phở hà nội comes brimming with broth and topped with a raw egg yolk, great stirred in or spooned over each bite of noodles and beef shank. The grilled chicken is fragrant with lemongrass, and vegetarians eat just as well here.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Vietnamese at Miss Pho

grillbird.name: Grillbird
grillbird.oneLiner: This is the West Seattle stop for rotisserie chicken that skips the gluten.
grillbird.blurb: The rotisserie chicken at Grillbird in West Seattle comes from a gluten-free kitchen.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Chicken (Rotisserie at Grillbird

petit-pierre-bakery.name: Petit Pierre Bakery
petit-pierre-bakery.oneLiner: A Magnolia morning stop for buttery French pastry on the cheap.
petit-pierre-bakery.blurb: Magnolia mornings start early at Petit Pierre Bakery, with inexpensive French pastries and bread.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting French Bakery at Petit Pierre Bakery

serafina.name: Serafina
serafina.oneLiner: Book the garden patio on a warm night and order a bottle of red.
serafina.blurb: Eastlake's Serafina has been a romantic Italian standby for decades, with a warm, rustic room and a leafy back patio. It's an easy call for an anniversary or a long dinner over pasta and wine.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Serafina

victrola-coffee-roasters.name: Victrola Coffee Roasters
victrola-coffee-roasters.oneLiner: Bring the laptop and grab a spot at the big communal table.
victrola-coffee-roasters.blurb: Victrola Coffee Roasters on Capitol Hill has strong espresso, a steady hum of people working, and a communal table roomy enough for your laptop and a giant mug. It's also air-conditioned, which matters during a summer heat wave. Their iced vanilla latte is great.

photos.alt: Victrola Coffee Roasters in Seattle
Illustration suggesting Coffee at Victrola Coffee Roasters

rondo-japanese.name: Rondo Japanese
rondo-japanese.oneLiner: Keep this Capitol Hill sushi spot in mind for an easy weeknight dinner.
rondo-japanese.blurb: Sushi is the focus at Rondo Japanese, a Japanese spot on Capitol Hill.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sushi at Rondo Japanese

roquette.name: Roquette
roquette.oneLiner: Belltown cocktail hour gets a little more polished in this small bar.
roquette.blurb: For a stirred drink in Belltown, Roquette is a cocktail bar to keep on your list.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Roquette

bait-shop.name: Bait Shop
bait-shop.oneLiner: Pineapple on the fried fish, a painkiller, and a booth big enough for Uno.
bait-shop.blurb: Bait Shop cannot pick between a nautical dive and a tiki shack, so the Capitol Hill room does both. Pineapple or bacon can land on the fried fish, and the fries have their own local following. Frozen drinks change by the day. Learn the painkiller by name: rum, pineapple, coconut, orange, nutmeg, and cinnamon. Take a big booth, deal a hand of Uno, and leave the amaro lecture for a different door on the hill.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at Bait Shop

bakery-nouveau.name: Bakery Nouveau
bakery-nouveau.oneLiner: Brave the morning line for a twice-baked almond croissant you won't want to share.
bakery-nouveau.blurb: Bakery Nouveau's twice-baked almond croissant is the order, messy with toasted almond slivers and powdered sugar. It's worth braving the long morning line, claiming a table, and settling in with a hot latte. Lunch holds up too, and the croque monsieur ranks with the best ham sandwiches in town.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at Bakery Nouveau

project-9-brewing-co.name: Project 9 Brewing Co.
project-9-brewing-co.oneLiner: Wild sours, hazy IPAs, and a pastrami truck out front settle every group debate.
project-9-brewing-co.blurb: The tap list here swings from peanut butter and jelly sours to turtle stout to fruit-loaded IPAs, so nobody needs a plan. A big patio sits on a busy Maple Leaf corner and makes for a long, summery session. For food, the Sammich truck parked outside does a pastrami sandwich that's the move. When friends are coming from opposite ends of the city, meet at Project 9 Brewing Co.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Beer at Project 9 Brewing Co.

mondello-italian-restaurant.name: Mondello Italian Restaurant
mondello-italian-restaurant.oneLiner: A Magnolia Italian dinner that saves you the drive across town.
mondello-italian-restaurant.blurb: Mondello Italian Restaurant gives Magnolia a neighborhood Italian dinner option close to home.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Mondello Italian Restaurant

bar-sur-mer.name: Bar Sur Mer
bar-sur-mer.oneLiner: Take a date to this Greenwood drinks room for a late round.
bar-sur-mer.blurb: Bar Sur Mer mixes cocktails in Greenwood until well past eleven.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Bar Sur Mer

katsu-ya.name: Katsu-ya
katsu-ya.oneLiner: Keep this casual Japanese spot in mind when you're around South Lake Union.
katsu-ya.blurb: Katsu-ya brings Japanese cooking to South Lake Union.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Japanese at Katsu-ya

oxbow.name: Oxbow
oxbow.oneLiner: Eat the garlic bagel with Calabrian chili cream cheese within the hour.
oxbow.blurb: The team behind Sea Wolf runs Oxbow in Montlake, and the bagels live up to that reputation. They have a crackly, shell-like crust, a dense chew, and a gentle sour tang, but they go stale fast, so eat them right away. With wifi, good smells from the ovens, and a late-afternoon close, it makes a fine daytime hangout.

photos.alt: Oxbow in Seattle
Illustration suggesting Bagels at Oxbow

taneda.name: Taneda
taneda.oneLiner: Book a solo seat for the multi-course kaiseki and sushi meal of your year.
taneda.blurb: Reservations for two at Taneda are nearly impossible, but single seats open up far more often, and a solo dinner here is a treat rather than a consolation. The meal runs around two dozen courses of sushi and kaiseki in a tiny spot at the back of a Capitol Hill indoor mall. The check is a special-occasion one, yet it is a strong value among the city omakase counters.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sushi at Taneda

the-french-guys.name: The French Guys
the-french-guys.oneLiner: Order the plain croissant, a steady classic that gets every essential right.
the-french-guys.blurb: The French Guys works out of a little stone cottage on Capitol Hill that looks lifted from a storybook. Their plain croissant isn't the flakiest or richest around, but it's buttery, crunchy, and dependable in a way you'll come to count on. It opens early, and prices are gentle.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting French Bakery at The French Guys

ciudad-grill.name: Ciudad Grill
ciudad-grill.oneLiner: A dependable pick for grilled meat and flatbread with almost any crowd.
ciudad-grill.blurb: Not every dinner needs to change your life, and Ciudad Grill knows it. This Georgetown spot is reliably easygoing, with a charcoal grill you notice before you even walk in. Expect smoky charred meats and warm flatbreads that suit a date, coworkers, or your in-laws equally well.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Mediterranean at Ciudad Grill

valhalla-sandwiches.name: Valhalla Sandwiches
valhalla-sandwiches.oneLiner: Order the Thanksgiving turkey sandwich and add tater tots for dunking.
valhalla-sandwiches.blurb: Valhalla Sandwiches in Greenwood manages to go big without getting sloppy. The sandwiches come on sturdy telera rolls with fillings like blackened shrimp and chorizo, chicken with sweet-hot mustard and slaw, or turkey with stuffing, cranberry, and rosemary aioli. Tater tots with chipotle mayo are a must, and the whole thing is inexpensive.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sandwiches at Valhalla Sandwiches

joe-z-bayside-market-cafe.name: Joe'z Bayside Market + Cafe
joe-z-bayside-market-cafe.oneLiner: Order the smashburger, because the homemade bun is the real star.
joe-z-bayside-market-cafe.blurb: Joe'z Bayside Market + Cafe took over the old Little Market space with Oklahoma-style smashburgers plus breakfast sandwiches in the bodega mold. Everything rides on the buttery, brioche-like house bun. The burger is the move, thanks to crusty patties, tangles of blackened onion, and a lemony garlic aioli. There are still a few shelves of crackers and wine, plus roomy tables for sharing fries.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cafe at Joe'z Bayside Market + Cafe

sushi-suzuki.name: Sushi Suzuki
sushi-suzuki.oneLiner: Serious omakase without the hush, tucked down an alley in Madison Park.
sushi-suzuki.blurb: Madison Park is all Porsches and pampered dogs, so a back-alley sushi counter fits right in. What surprises is how relaxed Sushi Suzuki feels, a small room squeezed between a bookstore and a salon that could pass for a brewery taproom. The courses are tiny and numerous, the fish does the talking, and the bill is firmly special-occasion.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sushi at Sushi Suzuki

bake-shop.name: Bake Shop
bake-shop.oneLiner: Order the cardamom horn first then linger over a salty whipped cream latte.
bake-shop.blurb: Near the Space Needle, where good options get scarce, Bake Shop is a welcome bright spot. You can linger over natural wine or a black sesame iced latte topped with salty whipped cream, but pastries are the real reason to come. The cardamom horn eats like a gentler honey bun, and the ham and cheese pastry rolled up like a cinnamon bun beats most croissant versions.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at Bake Shop

lioness.name: Lioness
lioness.oneLiner: Stand at the marble bar with a bergamot spritz and a few snacks.
lioness.blurb: Phinney Ridge's Lioness turns Italian aperitivo hour into an actual event. The narrow room glows with tea lights and a pair of chandeliers, and the soundtrack runs as fast as the date night chatter. Folks crowd the standing marble counter over bergamot spritzes, zero-proof garibaldis, and spotless martinis.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Lioness

the-5-point-cafe.name: The 5 Point Cafe
the-5-point-cafe.oneLiner: Open since 1929, and still pouring when Belltown has gone home.
the-5-point-cafe.blurb: The 5 Point Cafe faces the five-way at Tilikum Place, and the doors have been open since 1929. It is the oldest bar in Belltown and also a cafe that can serve breakfast as a nightcap. The city already filed it under dive: a long counter, regulars who do not surrender a stool, and no interest in a redesign. Eat something that can survive a second beer. Then stay later than the plan you walked in with.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Diner at The 5 Point Cafe

saint-bread.name: Saint Bread
saint-bread.oneLiner: Order the za'atar avocado toast and a custard bun, then sit by the water.
saint-bread.blurb: Saint Bread looks like a boathouse that floated in from some faraway fishing village, stained glass and all, but it sits on the U District edge of Portage Bay. The avocado toast is a standout thanks to a heavy hand with za'atar, good olive oil, and precise lemon and salt. There's also a take on Norwegian school buns stuffed with custard and raspberry jam, made for a slow Saturday breakfast.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at Saint Bread

dantini.name: Dantini
dantini.oneLiner: A low-key Interbay pizza option that deserves more attention than it gets.
dantini.blurb: Dantini turns out pizza in Interbay and keeps getting mentioned among the city's better pies.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pizza at Dantini

mountaineering-club.name: Mountaineering Club
mountaineering-club.address: 4507 Brooklyn Ave NE, FL 16, Seattle, WA 98105
mountaineering-club.oneLiner: Come for the view and the Banana Pancakes cocktail, not the hot dog.
mountaineering-club.blurb: Perched on the Graduate Hotel roof by campus, Mountaineering Club does camp-lodge decor with real polish and a sweeping view east. The drinks lean into the outdoorsy theme, with the Banana Pancakes and Orange Snack leading the list. If you're eating, go for the bacon sandwich and pass on the pricey frank. Service continues after eleven.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Mountaineering Club

pho-bac.name: Phở Bắc
pho-bac.oneLiner: Order the short rib bowl and ask about the half-chicken special.
pho-bac.blurb: Not every night calls for a dress code, and Phở Bắc in the CID is proof. The vibe is casual and cool, the menu runs from phở to Vietnamese drinking snacks, and parking is actually easy. Brisket and meatball bowls are great, but the huge short rib version and the occasional off-menu bowl with a whole poached half-chicken are the stars.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Vietnamese at Phở Bắc

espresso-vivace.name: Espresso Vivace
espresso-vivace.oneLiner: Order a ristretto and sip it slowly, because this is Seattle's espresso benchmark.
espresso-vivace.blurb: Espresso Vivace pulls the best shots in town, and the obsessive care shows in every cup. The room hums steadily without getting so packed you can't work, and on warm days a roll-up door opens the whole cafe to the sidewalk. Drop your drink on the way out and they'll make you another, no charge.

photos.alt: Espresso Vivace in Seattle
Illustration suggesting Coffee at Espresso Vivace

altura.name: Altura
altura.oneLiner: Save this Capitol Hill tasting menu for an anniversary or a milestone date.
altura.blurb: Big nights on Capitol Hill often end up at Altura, where a multi-course Italian tasting menu leans on Northwest ingredients. The check is firmly in special-occasion territory, so bring it out for a celebration that deserves the fuss.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Altura

canon.name: Canon
canon.oneLiner: Settle in with the encyclopedic menu and order something served in a light bulb.
canon.blurb: Canon on Capitol Hill treats cocktails like a fantasy factory, with a menu that runs for pages of classics and inventive originals. Drinks might involve smoke, rinses, house syrups, or a scoop of Cap'n Crunch ice cream, and they arrive in vessels like nesting dolls, glass hearts, or IV bags. The back bar is a towering wall of bottles, and the place now takes walk-ins only, with the bar going late.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Canon

rachel-s-ginger-beer.name: Rachel's Ginger Beer
rachel-s-ginger-beer.oneLiner: Duck in for a spiked mule when the market crowds get to be too much.
rachel-s-ginger-beer.blurb: After a couple of hours dodging tourists at Pike Place, Rachel's Ginger Beer is a welcome breather. The house ginger beer comes plain or in flavors like pink guava and cucumber tarragon, and any of them can be turned into a boozy mule. It's cheap, it's open late, and it's right in the middle of everything.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Ginger Beer at Rachel's Ginger Beer

ivar-s.name: Ivar's
ivar-s.oneLiner: Alder-smoked salmon on the Lake Union deck is the plate that matters.
ivar-s.blurb: The Wallingford Ivar's faces Lake Union, and alder-smoked salmon justifies stopping at take a deck table. Clam chowder can sit beside it. Come for the water without making a ferry out of dinner.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at Ivar's

cafe-turko.name: Café Turko
cafe-turko.oneLiner: Book a summer patio lunch here for mezze and kebabs.
cafe-turko.blurb: Mezze and kebabs at Café Turko in Fremont are good enough that you'll stop worrying about the metal tea kettle dangling overhead. The room suits a summer lunch on the patio, a casual date, or weeknight takeout.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Turkish at Café Turko

hellenika-cultured-creamery.name: HELLENIKA Cultured Creamery
hellenika-cultured-creamery.address: 1920 Pike Pl, Unit A, Seattle, WA 98101
hellenika-cultured-creamery.oneLiner: Cool off between Pike Place errands with a cup of tangy frozen yogurt.
hellenika-cultured-creamery.blurb: Frozen yogurt and gelato come cheap at HELLENIKA Cultured Creamery inside the arcade.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Frozen Yogurt at HELLENIKA Cultured Creamery

ltd-edition.name: LTD Edition
ltd-edition.oneLiner: Splurge on the omakase and do not skip the sake pairing.
ltd-edition.blurb: Seattle has no shortage of exclusive omakase counters, but LTD Edition on Capitol Hill deserves priority. The highlight is the uni cart, which delivers a rich sea urchin hand roll like a treat from a street vendor. Chefs explain the story behind every piece, and the sake pairing keeps flowing all night.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sushi at LTD Edition

the-crumpet-shop.name: The Crumpet Shop
the-crumpet-shop.oneLiner: A warm crumpet with ricotta and pesto beats every other quick breakfast at the market.
the-crumpet-shop.blurb: Breakfast options at Pike Place Market are thin, which makes The Crumpet Shop so useful. The crumpets are springy and crisp, and their little holes trap toppings like pesto with ricotta or raspberry preserves. Be there while the crumpets are still warm and hardly anything is spent.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Crumpets at The Crumpet Shop

moto-pizza.name: Moto Pizza
moto-pizza.oneLiner: Square pies with crispy edges, best split with a friend in Belltown.
moto-pizza.blurb: Thick, square pies are the draw at Moto Pizza in Belltown, a casual pick for pizza night.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pizza at Moto Pizza

bounty-kitchen.name: Bounty Kitchen
bounty-kitchen.oneLiner: Gluten-free diners should head straight for the pancakes with cinnamon butter.
bounty-kitchen.blurb: If gluten is your nemesis, Bounty Kitchen belongs on your brunch shortlist. The bright all-day cafe on Queen Anne makes excellent gluten-free pancakes topped with fruit compote and cinnamon butter, plus egg and vegetable hashes. Wheat-friendly tables can go for the braised beef bowl or avocado toast, and expect a short wait during the weekend rush.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Breakfast & Brunch at Bounty Kitchen

asadero.name: Asadero
asadero.oneLiner: Come for wagyu sizzling on a skillet and a hibiscus margarita.
asadero.blurb: Carne asada can easily come out thin and leathery, but Asadero treats steak with real respect. Cuts like filet mignon land on a hot skillet, cooked medium rare, alongside corn tortillas, lime, and salsa for building your own tacos. There's chicken, fish, and vegetables on the menu, but the barely pink wagyu with a hibiscus margarita on the side is why you came.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Mexican at Asadero

shaker-spear.name: Shaker + Spear
shaker-spear.oneLiner: Reserve the big round table, order the brûléed mac and cheese, and share.
shaker-spear.blurb: Dinner at Shaker + Spear feels a bit like eating in a very nice home goods showroom, in the best way. The seafood is strong, the staff is sharp and warm, and one round table seats eight if you're bringing a group. Order the prawns in Old Bay butter, the parmesan truffle fries, the charred sprouts, and that torched mac and cheese, then move next door to Pennyroyal for cocktails.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at Shaker + Spear

koko-s-restaurant-and-tequila-bar.name: Koko's Restaurant and Tequila Bar
koko-s-restaurant-and-tequila-bar.oneLiner: Come late for tacos and a tequila list that keeps Capitol Hill up.
koko-s-restaurant-and-tequila-bar.blurb: Koko's Restaurant and Tequila Bar serves tacos and Mexican plates on Capitol Hill.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Mexican at Koko's Restaurant and Tequila Bar

the-carlile-room.name: The Carlile Room
the-carlile-room.oneLiner: Book it before a show when you want a stylish dinner steps from the theater.
the-carlile-room.blurb: Across from the Paramount Theatre, The Carlile Room serves New American plates in a colorful downtown room that's handy for pre-show meals.

photos.alt: The Carlile Room in Seattle
Illustration suggesting New American at The Carlile Room

damn-the-weather.name: Damn the Weather
damn-the-weather.oneLiner: Order the fennel-dusted fries cooked in chicken fat, then a cocktail, then the burger.
damn-the-weather.blurb: A brick-walled hideout from the drizzle, Damn the Weather cooks far better than a bar needs to. Cocktails come first, but the kitchen sends out parm-heavy spaghetti bolognese, bright crudo, and blistered shishitos. It's usually packed and open late, so be ready to circle for a seat.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Damn the Weather

sabine.name: Sabine
sabine.oneLiner: An early-morning Ballard stop for a cheap pastry and a coffee.
sabine.blurb: Open early and easy on the wallet, Sabine is a Ballard bakery and cafe for pastries and coffee.

photos.alt: Sabine in Seattle
Illustration suggesting Bakery at Sabine

empire-roasters-and-records.name: Empire Roasters and Records
empire-roasters-and-records.address: 3829 S Edmunds St, Unit A, Seattle, WA  98118
empire-roasters-and-records.oneLiner: Pair a made-to-order Belgian waffle with the house cashew milk latte.
empire-roasters-and-records.blurb: Empire Roasters and Records fits into a slim converted garage in Columbia City, and the food punches way above coffee-shop standards. Waffles are made fresh when you order, crowned with blueberries and a snowfall of sugar, or kept simple with butter and maple. Gluten-free and vegan versions are available, and the date-sweetened cashew drink deserves a spot on your tray.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at Empire Roasters and Records

little-jaye.name: Little Jaye
little-jaye.address: 309 S Cloverdale St, Unit A4, Seattle, WA  98108
little-jaye.oneLiner: Order the egg sandwich on brioche, but bring a fork and napkins.
little-jaye.blurb: The team behind Lady Jaye shows off its pastry skills at Little Jaye in South Park. Look for moist lemon loaf, miso chocolate chip cookies, and fluffy shokupan that disappears early. The breakfast sandwich, built on brioche with smashed sausage, a hash brown, and a runny yolk, is great and gloriously messy.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at Little Jaye

market-house-meats.name: Market House Meats
market-house-meats.oneLiner: The corned beef reuben here is the benchmark for every deli in town.
market-house-meats.blurb: Look for the huge corned beef sign over the Denny Triangle and you've found Market House Meats. The shop has fed office workers and early construction crews since the forties, and the griddle is always sizzling. That tender, salty corned beef goes into a reuben you'll measure every other one against. It's inexpensive, quick, and open early.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sandwiches at Market House Meats

momiji-slu.name: Momiji SLU
momiji-slu.oneLiner: A dependable Denny Triangle sushi stop for a weeknight roll fix.
momiji-slu.blurb: For sushi just north of the retail core without a big production, Momiji SLU is a solid pick.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sushi at Momiji SLU

aa-sushi.name: AA Sushi
aa-sushi.oneLiner: Excellent nigiri at casual prices, and you can usually walk right in with friends.
aa-sushi.blurb: AA Sushi in Ballard makes a casual sushi night feel like a splurge without the bill. Small groups can usually stroll in and sit down fast in a plain but comfortable room. Cover the table in nigiri, rolls, and miso soup, and pay attention to the rice, which holds together and stays just warm enough to soften a slice of yellowtail belly.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sushi at AA Sushi

wet-clay-cafe.name: Wet Clay Cafe
wet-clay-cafe.oneLiner: An early, inexpensive Fremont cafe for a morning coffee stop.
wet-clay-cafe.blurb: Wet Clay Cafe opens early in Fremont and keeps its prices low.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cafe at Wet Clay Cafe

lady-jaye.name: Lady Jaye
lady-jaye.oneLiner: Start with the crispy pork balls and a pimento cheese cream puff.
