lady-jaye.blurb: Lady Jaye takes West Seattle barbecue in unexpected directions, from panko-fried pulled pork balls to sandwiches piled with house bologna. Pastrami is made from pork collar, sausage goes into a creole dirty rice, and pimento cheese gets piped into cream puffs. Even the cocktails get creative with things like pumpkin seed orgeat. It's open late and works for brunch or a dinner with parents.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting New American at Lady Jaye

white-horse-tavern.name: White Horse Tavern
white-horse-tavern.oneLiner: Post Alley hides the sofa, the Spam birdcage, and a cardboard drinks list.
white-horse-tavern.blurb: White Horse Tavern sits in Post Alley, which is why market crowds walk past it. The ceiling holds photos, paintings, umbrellas, and a birdcage with a can of Spam inside. Drinks are listed in marker on cardboard. Order Bulls Blood if you want port mixed with dry champagne, then take the red velvet sofa. Three friends on a weekend is the right headcount. A party of twelve will not fit, and should not try.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bar Food at White Horse Tavern

ma-ono.name: Ma'ono
ma-ono.oneLiner: Order the fried chicken sandwich and a side of kimchi mac and cheese.
ma-ono.blurb: Years in, the chicken sandwich at Ma'ono in University Village still delivers. The crust is craggy, dunked in smoky pork fat and dusted with red spice, then stacked with daikon pickles and kewpie on a soft Hawaiian bun. There's a fried vegetarian patty too, and the mac and cheese with kimchi is a must.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Hawaiian at Ma'ono

bottlehouse.name: Bottlehouse
bottlehouse.oneLiner: A neighborhood wine bar in Madrona for a relaxed glass after work.
bottlehouse.blurb: Madrona has its own easygoing wine stop in Bottlehouse.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Wine at Bottlehouse

single-shot-kitchen-saloon.name: Single Shot Kitchen & Saloon
single-shot-kitchen-saloon.oneLiner: Order the margherita flatbread and a cocktail for a quiet, easy date.
single-shot-kitchen-saloon.blurb: Few people seem to know about Single Shot Kitchen & Saloon, which gives a date here some built-in novelty. It's a single handsome room, marble bar included, with candles on every table, oddly calm given the noise of Pike-Pine outside. Keep it simple with cocktails and the excellent flatbread, or celebrate with champagne, plenty of small plates, and a good piece of fish.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting New American at Single Shot Kitchen & Saloon

seafab.name: Seafab
seafab.oneLiner: A cheap, early U District cafe with a seafood bent worth checking out.
seafab.blurb: Seafood and cafe fare share the menu at Seafab, an inexpensive U District spot that opens early.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at Seafab

bonito-cafe-y-mercadito.name: Bonito Cafe Y Mercadito
bonito-cafe-y-mercadito.oneLiner: An early Capitol Hill coffee stop with a little Mexican market attached.
bonito-cafe-y-mercadito.blurb: Bonito Cafe Y Mercadito pours coffee and sells Mexican goods on Capitol Hill, opening early and staying gentle on a weekday budget.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at Bonito Cafe Y Mercadito

ooink.name: Ooink
ooink.oneLiner: Come solo or as a pair for the tenderest chashu in town.
ooink.blurb: Capitol Hill has no shortage of ramen, but Ooink earns its spot with the most tender sliced pork around and some seriously oversized gyoza. The room is small, so plan on going alone or with one friend. It's the bowl you want when you've got a cold.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Ramen at Ooink

bluwater-bistro-leschi.name: BluWater Bistro - Leschi
bluwater-bistro-leschi.oneLiner: Grab an outdoor table on a sunny day and watch the lake.
bluwater-bistro-leschi.blurb: Lake Washington views from the outdoor seating are the main draw at BluWater Bistro - Leschi.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting French at BluWater Bistro - Leschi

artusi.name: Artusi
artusi.oneLiner: Grab two seats at the long bar for an easy, early-stage date.
artusi.blurb: Walking up to Artusi, you catch the smell of grilled bread and olive oil drifting from the kitchen, and the night only gets better inside. This smaller sibling to Spinasse is mostly one big L-shaped counter, and that's where you want to be for sharp cocktails and Italian snacks. It suits a newer date or any night when you want great food in lighter portions.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Artusi

farestart-restaurant.name: FareStart Restaurant
farestart-restaurant.oneLiner: Eat well and help fund culinary job training while you're at it.
farestart-restaurant.blurb: Every meal at FareStart Restaurant supports a nonprofit program, with students learning the ropes in the kitchen and on the floor. The American menu is approachable, and it opens early enough for a Denny Triangle breakfast meeting.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting American at FareStart Restaurant

doce-donut-co.name: DOCE Donut Co.
doce-donut-co.oneLiner: An early-morning donut stop in Wallingford that's easy on the wallet.
doce-donut-co.blurb: Wallingford's early risers get their inexpensive sugar fix at DOCE Donut Co.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Donuts at DOCE Donut Co.

copper-tree-coffee-house.name: Copper Tree Coffee House
copper-tree-coffee-house.oneLiner: An early-opening Capitol Hill coffee shop for the commute or a slow morning.
copper-tree-coffee-house.blurb: Copper Tree Coffee House opens early for Capitol Hill coffee runs, and the prices stay low.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at Copper Tree Coffee House

triangle-spirits-fremont.name: Triangle Spirits Fremont
triangle-spirits-fremont.oneLiner: Come for the fried chicken sandwich and stay for a coupe cocktail.
triangle-spirits-fremont.blurb: Inside what looks like a wood-paneled Fremont dive, Triangle Spirits Fremont makes a chicken sandwich that rivals anyone's, with a crackly crust, juicy breast meat, and just lettuce, pickles, and mayo. The cheeseburger with American cheese and relish-heavy sauce is just as strong. Add fries or gravy-soaked mashed potatoes and you've got a real dinner, not just drinks.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Triangle Spirits Fremont

bottega-gabriele.name: Bottega Gabriele
bottega-gabriele.oneLiner: Order the spicy 'nduja focaccia sandwich and stay for the bossa nova soundtrack.
bottega-gabriele.blurb: Seattle has long needed a serious Italian deli, and Bottega Gabriele in Pioneer Square fills the gap nicely. They import tangy, spicy 'nduja and spread it on springy focaccia, alongside mortadella, dolce sardo, lemony arugula, and purple olive tapenade. Italian-speaking staff and soft bossa nova make lunch feel lively yet relaxed, and the damage stays small.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Bottega Gabriele

midnite-ramen.name: Midnite Ramen
midnite-ramen.oneLiner: A solid Fremont noodle stop when the weather turns and you want broth.
midnite-ramen.blurb: A casual Fremont ramen shop, Midnite Ramen is an easy call for a bowl of noodles.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Ramen at Midnite Ramen

san-fermo.name: San Fermo
san-fermo.oneLiner: Bring a date here when you need dinner to go exactly as planned.
san-fermo.blurb: Some restaurants just know what you need, and San Fermo in Ballard is reliable in exactly that way. Set in a pair of old houses, the room feels warm and lived-in, and the pasta gives you a reason to come back. It's the Italian spot you book when there's no room for a dud evening.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at San Fermo

dead-line.name: Dead Line
dead-line.oneLiner: Come at happy hour, when the chips, olives, and nuts arrive free with drinks.
dead-line.blurb: Dead Line is small, dark, and polished, with shelves of bottles so tall the bartenders need a rolling ladder. Beyond the serious cocktails, the kitchen turns out South American small plates like brisket arepas and squash al pastor tacos. The pre-dinner window is a steal, and the bar pours past eleven.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Dead Line

stevie-s-famous.name: Stevie's Famous
stevie-s-famous.oneLiner: A Beacon Hill pizza spot to keep in mind for an easy neighborhood dinner.
stevie-s-famous.blurb: Pizza is the main event at Stevie's Famous, a casual spot on Beacon Hill.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pizza at Stevie's Famous

biang-biang-noodles.name: Biang Biang Noodles
biang-biang-noodles.address: 601 E Pike St, Unit 100, Seattle, WA 98122
biang-biang-noodles.oneLiner: Go for the wide, hand-pulled noodles and plan to get chili oil everywhere.
biang-biang-noodles.blurb: Capitol Hill noodle fans head to Biang Biang Noodles for the broad, belt-like hand-pulled noodles that give the dish its name.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Chinese at Biang Biang Noodles

communion-restaurant-bar.name: Communion Restaurant & Bar
communion-restaurant-bar.oneLiner: Order the stewed pork neck and save serious room for peach cobbler.
communion-restaurant-bar.blurb: Communion Restaurant & Bar sits in the Liberty Bank Building and cooks like a tribute to both the American South and the Central District around it. Berbere-rubbed chicken over lemony lentils tips its hat to the neighborhood's Ethiopian community, while the pork neck is pure Southern comfort. The bill belongs to a celebration, and the meal earns it.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Soul Food at Communion Restaurant & Bar

homer.name: Homer
homer.oneLiner: Fill the table with dips and warm pita, then save room for soft serve.
homer.blurb: Homer brings Mediterranean cooking to Beacon Hill with a wood-fired oven at the center of the room. Puffy pita and spreads anchor the meal, and the soft serve is a sweet way to end it.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Mediterranean at Homer

georgetown-brewing.name: Georgetown Brewing
georgetown-brewing.oneLiner: Drink a pint of Manny's where it's brewed, ideally with a friend you've neglected.
georgetown-brewing.blurb: Georgetown Brewing makes Manny's, the pale ale that seems to be on every tap in Seattle. The gravel-lot tasting room is where to try it fresh alongside other pales, IPAs, and a chocolatey porter. Bring a big group or an old friend you owe a catch-up.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Beer at Georgetown Brewing

sushi-kashiba.name: Sushi Kashiba
sushi-kashiba.oneLiner: For the city's best sushi, book the counter and let the chefs decide.
sushi-kashiba.blurb: Skip the waterfront oyster crawl and the fish and chips shops, because the finest seafood in town is at Sushi Kashiba. Shiro Kashiba, who trained under Jiro Ono, opened it at the edge of Pike Place Market in 2015 after leaving his namesake restaurant. Expect impeccable nigiri and a special-occasion check.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sushi at Sushi Kashiba

earl-s-on-the-ave.name: Earl's on the Ave
earl-s-on-the-ave.oneLiner: Show up as a crowd, find a screen, and keep the tab cheap.
earl-s-on-the-ave.blurb: Cheap drinks, games on the TVs, and room for a big group make Earl's on the Ave a U District standby that stays open late.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bar Food at Earl's on the Ave

tall-grass-bakery.name: Tall Grass Bakery
tall-grass-bakery.oneLiner: Pick up an early-morning loaf here on your way through Ballard.
tall-grass-bakery.blurb: An inexpensive Ballard bakery that opens early, Tall Grass Bakery is a reliable stop for bread and baked goods.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at Tall Grass Bakery

the-sitting-room.name: The Sitting Room
the-sitting-room.oneLiner: Pick the back sofas for friends or a candlelit table for a date.
the-sitting-room.blurb: Dim and friendly, The Sitting Room is where you sip spritzes and work through olives and truffled almonds. Potato chips with house onion dip could easily be dinner. Sofas fill the back, the bar has a library-desk feel, and the row of candlelit tables suits a date.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Wine at The Sitting Room

the-corson-building.name: The Corson Building
the-corson-building.oneLiner: Save this Georgetown garden house for an anniversary dinner you'll talk about for years.
the-corson-building.blurb: Set inside an early twentieth-century house in Georgetown, The Corson Building glows with candles and vintage decor, and the garden terrace has wood nymph statues. It's only open Thursday through Sunday, with à la carte dinners at the start of the stretch and prix fixe on weekends. Expect a special-occasion check and make a reservation.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pacific Northwest at The Corson Building

la-marea.name: La Marea
la-marea.oneLiner: Order the ahi tostada with salsa macha and a crisp saison.
la-marea.blurb: Running a Mexican seafood kitchen inside Fair Isle Brewing, La Marea proves brewery food can go well beyond burgers. Crunchy tostadas lead the menu, especially the one stacked with buttery ahi and fiery salsa macha. Pair it with a farmhouse saison to tame the heat.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at La Marea

goldfinch-tavern.name: Goldfinch Tavern
goldfinch-tavern.oneLiner: Request glass-side seating at sunset and let the Elliott Bay view do the work.
goldfinch-tavern.blurb: Inside the Four Seasons downtown, Goldfinch Tavern serves polished American food with big windows facing the water. It opens early for breakfast and keeps the bar going late, so the room suits a morning meeting or a nightcap.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting American at Goldfinch Tavern

blue-moon.name: Blue Moon
blue-moon.oneLiner: Band stickers, sunk leather stools, and cheap beer when a band is loading in.
blue-moon.blurb: Blue Moon Tavern is the U District bar for cheap beer and whatever band is hauling amps through the door. Stickers from old shows cover the walls, the stools have collapsed into their leather, and the booths look sawed from a backyard tree. Sit down if you like a room that remembers its own concerts. Walk on if you wanted a host stand. The Ave has plenty of those, and none of them have this many stickers.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bar at Blue Moon

il-nido.name: il nido
il-nido.oneLiner: This is where West Seattle goes for anniversaries and unfussy pasta nights alike.
il-nido.blurb: Alki may feel like a summer-only scene, but il nido gives West Seattle a reason to go out all year. The Italian cooking is consistent enough that even a plain bowl of noodles lands, and the staff handles off-menu requests without blinking. It sits inside a historic homestead, which makes the setting feel special without getting stuffy.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at il nido

a-k-pizza.name: A.K. Pizza
a-k-pizza.address: 6901 Martin Luther King Jr Way S, Suite A, Seattle, WA  98118
a-k-pizza.oneLiner: Charred, crackly crust and a cloud of chew make this the city's pizza to beat.
a-k-pizza.blurb: Getting your hands on a pie from A.K. Pizza takes real effort, but the crust that shatters outside and tears open into airy fluff makes it worth every bit. Go for the scamorza and vodka sauce pie or a plain cheese, then grab one of the enormous salted chocolate cookies on the way out.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pizza at A.K. Pizza

the-boat.name: The Boat
the-boat.oneLiner: Order the garlic fried chicken rice and eat lunch aboard a landlocked wooden ship.
the-boat.blurb: Docked in a parking lot in the International District, The Boat is a wooden ship the Phở Bắc team brought back to life in 2022. The main reason to climb aboard is the fried Cornish hen over rice, slicked with garlicky fish sauce. Think of it as a quick, unfussy lunch that doesn't require much planning.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Vietnamese at The Boat

bateau.name: Bateau
bateau.oneLiner: Check the chalkboard for the night's cuts and order a steak to share.
bateau.blurb: Bateau brings a French accent to steak, with a chalkboard of whichever cuts showed up that day. It shares a family tree with the Ballard oyster room, and the bright little space makes a strong argument for a date.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Steakhouse at Bateau

marco-polo-bar-grill.name: Marco Polo Bar & Grill
marco-polo-bar-grill.oneLiner: Georgetown since 1950, Cougar flags on the wall, and broasted chicken.
marco-polo-bar-grill.blurb: Marco Polo Bar & Grill has poured in Georgetown since 1950, under enough Washington State memorabilia to stock a small museum. Cornmeal-dusted pickles and a cold beer make a complete snack. The plate to get is the broasted chicken, pressure-fried, with salty skin and pieces large enough that the bouncer may be holding a drumstick at the door. Karaoke shares the same room. Stay for one song you did not pick.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting American at Marco Polo Bar & Grill

el-gaucho.name: El Gaucho
el-gaucho.oneLiner: Dress up, order a dry-aged steak, and let the tableside show unfold.
el-gaucho.blurb: Dim lights, live piano, and servers working tableside carts make El Gaucho the old-school supper club Belltown never outgrew. Get a dry-aged cut with a Caesar tossed right in front of you. Bring a fat budget, since this is a special-occasion check through and through.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Steakhouse at El Gaucho

pancita.name: Pancita
pancita.oneLiner: Come to Ravenna for tacos that are worth a detour across town.
pancita.blurb: Mexican cooking comes to Ravenna at Pancita, and the tacos are the reason to go.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Mexican at Pancita

ozzie-s.name: Ozzie's
ozzie-s.oneLiner: Lower Queen Anne karaoke, priced like a dive, and open until 2.
ozzie-s.blurb: Ozzie's is a Lower Queen Anne dive with karaoke and an American kitchen, and the lights stay on until 2. Prices sit at the cheap end on purpose. Pick a song you can finish, stand where people will clap, and skip the night if nobody in the group will sing. A plainer pub can sell you a beer anywhere on Queen Anne. This room only earns the walk once the microphone is switched on.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting American at Ozzie's

caffe-vita.name: Caffe Vita
caffe-vita.oneLiner: A reliable neighborhood espresso stop before a show at Seattle Center.
caffe-vita.blurb: Lower Queen Anne's early risers get house-roasted coffee at Caffe Vita, and it won't cost much.

photos.alt: Caffe Vita in Seattle
Illustration suggesting Coffee at Caffe Vita

big-mario-s-pizza.name: Big Mario's Pizza
big-mario-s-pizza.oneLiner: New York style slices on the Hill for when only a big fold will do.
big-mario-s-pizza.blurb: For a foldable slice on Capitol Hill, Big Mario's Pizza does the New York thing.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pizza at Big Mario's Pizza

wataru-sushi-restaurant.name: WATARU Sushi Restaurant
wataru-sushi-restaurant.oneLiner: Wear flannel, grab a table for two, and order the seared black cod.
wataru-sushi-restaurant.blurb: WATARU Sushi Restaurant in Ravenna is a dressy-casual date spot where flannel fits right in, even though prices run high. Nigiri highlights include Hokkaido scallop with bamboo salt and lightly seared black cod. The omakase counter is tough to book, but tables come with set dinners and great starters like a fish cake slider on lotus root buns.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sushi at WATARU Sushi Restaurant

the-nest.name: The Nest
the-nest.oneLiner: Go for sunset views over Elliott Bay and accept that the drinks cost more.
the-nest.blurb: On top of the Thompson Hotel, The Nest serves cocktails with sweeping views of the water and the downtown skyline. Expect a special-occasion tab, and know the bar stays open late.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at The Nest

charlotte-restaurant-lounge.name: Charlotte Restaurant & Lounge
charlotte-restaurant-lounge.oneLiner: Book it for the skyline views and a dinner that feels like an occasion.
charlotte-restaurant-lounge.blurb: High up in the Lotte Hotel, Charlotte Restaurant & Lounge pairs New American plates with sweeping views over downtown and the water. The bill belongs to a celebration, so save it for anniversaries and visiting parents who love a view.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting New American at Charlotte Restaurant & Lounge

un-bien.name: Un Bien

orderThis.note: The same family of sandwich as Paseo.

un-bien.oneLiner: Order the Caribbean Roast and accept that your shirt will suffer.
un-bien.blurb: Un Bien comes from the Lorenzo family, who created the original recipes at Paseo before the two businesses split. The Caribbean Roast, marinated pork on a toasted baguette, is the sandwich to get at this Ballard counter. It's cheap, messy, and better than the version that made the old shop famous.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cuban at Un Bien

ghost-note-coffee.name: Ghost Note Coffee
ghost-note-coffee.oneLiner: Order the espresso float and discover that root beer belongs in coffee.
ghost-note-coffee.blurb: The baristas at Ghost Note Coffee reach for cocktail shakers as often as steam wands. That precision shows in a smoked grapefruit and rosemary cold espresso served in a coupe, and in a malty mocha shake brightened with orange peel. The real showstopper is the espresso float, which pairs iced latte with local root beer and vegan cream.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at Ghost Note Coffee

the-flour-box.name: The Flour Box
the-flour-box.oneLiner: The brioche donuts justify showing up two hours early with a camp chair.
the-flour-box.blurb: People line up outside The Flour Box well before the doors open, and the brioche donuts explain why. Flavors rotate constantly, from torched crème brûlée to savory everything-spiced cream cheese, Oreo mascarpone, or Thai tea. If the Basque cheesecake is around, get it. The shop sits in Hillman City, just south of Columbia City.

photos.alt: The Flour Box in Seattle
Illustration suggesting Donuts at The Flour Box

the-harvest-vine.name: The Harvest Vine
the-harvest-vine.oneLiner: Head downstairs to the candlelit wine cellar for the most romantic tapas in town.
the-harvest-vine.blurb: The Harvest Vine looks modest from the street in Madison Valley, but the stone wine cellar downstairs, lit by candles and lined with dusty Tempranillo, does the romantic work for you. Order olives, jamón, a wedge of tortilla española, and the sherry-soaked mushrooms. Servers mostly leave you alone, and the place also works for a group sharing tapas.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Spanish at The Harvest Vine

bacco-cafe.name: Bacco Cafe
bacco-cafe.oneLiner: An easy Market brunch stop that's open before most shops roll up their gates.
bacco-cafe.blurb: Breakfast and brunch start early at Bacco Cafe, a morning stop inside the arcade.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Breakfast & Brunch at Bacco Cafe

the-traveling-goat.name: The Traveling Goat
the-traveling-goat.address: 621 1/2 Queen Anne Ave N, Seattle, WA 98109
the-traveling-goat.oneLiner: A low-key Lower Queen Anne cocktail bar for a drink near Seattle Center.
the-traveling-goat.blurb: In Lower Queen Anne, The Traveling Goat mixes cocktails at friendly prices.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at The Traveling Goat

west-of-chicago-pizza-company.name: West of Chicago Pizza Company
west-of-chicago-pizza-company.oneLiner: Neon cheese, Italian beef, and great pizza will make homesick Chicagoans very happy.
west-of-chicago-pizza-company.blurb: With ramekins of neon-orange cheese, red plastic cups for soda, and the smell of Italian beef in the air, West of Chicago Pizza Company could pass for a suburban Chicago joint. The pizza is genuinely great, Chicagoan or not. It works for a group dinner or a laid-back date in West Seattle.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pizza at West of Chicago Pizza Company

the-pink-door.name: The Pink Door
the-pink-door.oneLiner: Go for the lasagna and the cabaret, and fight for a seat on the deck.
the-pink-door.blurb: Behind an unmarked pink door in Post Alley, The Pink Door has paired Italian-American comfort food with trapeze acts and cabaret for decades. The summer deck looks out over Elliott Bay, and lasagna is the order. It works for a date, a visiting friend, or a late dinner near Pike Place Market.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at The Pink Door

vindicktive-wings.name: Vindicktive Wings
vindicktive-wings.oneLiner: Come for the wings, stay for the chaos, and catch the game if you must.
vindicktive-wings.blurb: Vindicktive Wings looks like a generic Belltown sports bar at first, all big booths and TVs, but people show up here for wings first and the game second. Give it time and the room starts to feel like a great college party, with loud music and bartenders who remember you. The wings are inexpensive.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Wings at Vindicktive Wings

armistice-coffee-roaster.name: Armistice Coffee Roaster
armistice-coffee-roaster.oneLiner: Roosevelt locals get a careful espresso here before the workday starts.
armistice-coffee-roaster.blurb: Roosevelt's morning crowd gets coffee roasted in house at Armistice Coffee Roaster, which opens early.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at Armistice Coffee Roaster

layers.name: Layers
layers.address: 7900 E Green Lake Dr N, Unit 107, Seattle, WA  98103
layers.oneLiner: Stop here for a cheap sandwich before a lap around Green Lake.
layers.blurb: Green Lake has an inexpensive sandwich counter in Layers.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sandwiches at Layers

rainier-teriyaki.name: Rainier Teriyaki
rainier-teriyaki.oneLiner: This is the teriyaki to settle any argument about the city's signature takeout.
rainier-teriyaki.blurb: Teriyaki is a Seattle invention, and Rainier Teriyaki in Mount Baker is the standard everyone else gets measured against. The chicken comes off the grill with a smoky char and a glaze that caramelizes on the edges. Little touches seal it, like iceberg salad packed on the side so it stays crisp, blistered gingery gyoza, and extra sauce tucked in without asking. Takeout comes together fast without slipping.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Japanese at Rainier Teriyaki

bangrak-market.name: Bangrak Market
bangrak-market.oneLiner: A Belltown Thai spot to remember when the group wants something with heat.
bangrak-market.blurb: Belltown gets a dose of Thai cooking at Bangrak Market.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Thai at Bangrak Market

biscuit-bitch.name: Biscuit Bitch
biscuit-bitch.oneLiner: Go hungry and order a gravy-smothered biscuit sandwich with plenty of hot sauce.
biscuit-bitch.blurb: Biscuit Bitch serves hefty breakfast biscuits stacked with fillings, and the whole menu leans into its trailer-park-to-table joke. Try The Canadian Bitch, built on banana and maple peanut butter, or the Bitchwich loaded with sausage, egg, cheese, and gravy plus hot sauce.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Breakfast & Brunch at Biscuit Bitch

d-la-santa.name: D' La Santa
d-la-santa.oneLiner: Easy to drive past for years, and a pleasant shock once you finally stop.
d-la-santa.blurb: D' La Santa hides in plain sight on a quiet stretch of north Capitol Hill, and plenty of locals have passed it without noticing. Finding it feels like discovering cash in an old coat pocket. Grab street parking and settle in for a Mexican meal that rewards the detour.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Mexican at D' La Santa

deep-dive.name: Deep Dive
deep-dive.oneLiner: Worth the long wait for a celebratory round under the sea.
deep-dive.blurb: Deep Dive comes from the team behind The Walrus and the Carpenter, and it feels like a fancy aquarium dreamed up by Disney. Getting in is a project, since the entrance tucks into the Amazon Spheres and reservations aren't a thing. Expect to wait an hour or more, then order something festive and toast whatever you came to celebrate.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at Deep Dive

grand-central-bakery.name: Grand Central Bakery
grand-central-bakery.oneLiner: Grab a rustic loaf and a pastry for the walk home.
grand-central-bakery.blurb: For decades, Grand Central Bakery has been a Seattle name for crusty, rustic bread. The Wallingford shop opens early, so stop in for a morning croissant and leave with a loaf under your arm.

photos.alt: Grand Central Bakery in Seattle
photos.credit: President Barack Obama holds a round table discussion with local small business owners.jpg

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at Grand Central Bakery

dog-in-the-park.name: Dog in the Park
dog-in-the-park.oneLiner: A cheap downtown hot dog when lunch needs to happen in five minutes.
dog-in-the-park.blurb: Dog in the Park handles quick, inexpensive franks for Downtown lunch breaks.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Hot Dogs at Dog in the Park

un-po-tipsy.name: Un Po Tipsy
un-po-tipsy.oneLiner: A casual Pioneer Square pizza stop that holds its own among better pies.
un-po-tipsy.blurb: Pioneer Square has a solid pizza option in Un Po Tipsy, where prices stay moderate.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pizza at Un Po Tipsy

cobb-s-pike-place-popcorn.name: Cobb's Pike Place Popcorn
cobb-s-pike-place-popcorn.oneLiner: An easy, cheap snack stop for grazing your way through the Market.
cobb-s-pike-place-popcorn.blurb: Snack on cheap popcorn from Cobb's Pike Place Popcorn while you wander the Market.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Snacks at Cobb's Pike Place Popcorn

seatangofoods.name: Seatangofoods
seatangofoods.address: 12728 Lake City Way NE, Seattle, WA 98125
seatangofoods.oneLiner: Come for the empanadas and leave with a box of alfajores for later.
seatangofoods.blurb: This Lake City counter is among the few places in Seattle specializing in Argentine baked goods, from dulce de leche alfajores to glossy medialunas and quince pastafrola. Still, the empanadas are why Seatangofoods deserves a lunch detour, golden and often fresh out of the oven. Lake City can get an empanada before the commute, which is the practical glory here.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Argentine at Seatangofoods

rhein-haus.name: Rhein Haus
rhein-haus.oneLiner: Bocce, a boot of lager, and bratwurst in a Capitol Hill hall.
rhein-haus.blurb: Rhein Haus is a Capitol Hill beer hall of long wooden tables, bratwurst, and bocce played hard enough to sour a friendship. Lager arrives by the liter in a glass boot. Pretzels come with beer cheese, and warm months set the slushie machines spinning. The bathroom line can outlast a sitcom episode. The crowd is young and loud, which is the recommendation. Claim a lane before the hall claims your whole night.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting German at Rhein Haus

citizen-collective.name: Citizen Collective
citizen-collective.oneLiner: An inexpensive Lower Queen Anne coffee stop that keeps going long after dark.
citizen-collective.blurb: Citizen Collective pours coffee by Seattle Center from early morning until late at night.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at Citizen Collective

anchorhead-coffee.name: Anchorhead Coffee
anchorhead-coffee.oneLiner: Downtown workers, the quaffle and a spiced cold brew beat any lobby breakfast.
anchorhead-coffee.blurb: Downtown is short on morning options that aren't chain coffee or a sad pastry, which makes Anchorhead Coffee a real find. Grab a small banana bread or a biscuit sandwich, or go big with the quaffle, a cinnamon roll, croissant, and waffle hybrid. The honey bunches of cold brew, with burnt honey, cinnamon, and oat milk, is the drink to get.

photos.alt: Anchorhead Coffee in Seattle
Illustration suggesting Coffee at Anchorhead Coffee

b-z-family-mexican-restaurant.name: B & Z Family Mexican Restaurant
b-z-family-mexican-restaurant.address: 2232 Queen Anne Ave N, Seattle, WA  98109
b-z-family-mexican-restaurant.oneLiner: A family Mexican spot on Queen Anne that's already open by breakfast.
b-z-family-mexican-restaurant.blurb: Tacos and other Mexican staples are the business at B & Z Family Mexican Restaurant, with doors open early on Queen Anne.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Mexican at B & Z Family Mexican Restaurant

otherside-market-deli.name: Otherside Market & Deli
otherside-market-deli.address: 2210 Eastlake Ave E, Ste 107, Seattle, WA  98102
otherside-market-deli.oneLiner: Get the Italian sub, add a breakfast sandwich, and bring patience.
otherside-market-deli.blurb: The owners once ran Lyon's Grocery in Queen Anne, and that pedigree shows in every sandwich at Otherside Market & Deli in Eastlake. The Italian sub piles on ham with pepperoncini and a hit of red wine vinegar, while breakfast sandwiches arrive gooey on Backyard bagels. Even a plain turkey and cheese on wheat is great here.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sandwiches at Otherside Market & Deli

pacific-inn-pub.name: Pacific Inn Pub
pacific-inn-pub.oneLiner: Fremont fish and chips in a pub that never pretended to be a dining room.
pacific-inn-pub.blurb: Pacific Inn Pub is the Fremont stop when dinner should be fish and chips and the room should stay a pub. Fried fish and a pint are the whole idea, eaten at a seat that is not auditioning to be a dining room. Finish the crust there. It will not be the same fish after a walk to the ship canal. Fremont has prettier patios. This room has been doing the plain job longer.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at Pacific Inn Pub

mykonos-greek-grill.name: Mykonos Greek Grill
mykonos-greek-grill.oneLiner: Order the chicken lemon rice soup and an overstuffed gyro, nothing more needed.
mykonos-greek-grill.blurb: Near Green Lake, Mykonos Greek Grill turns out Greek food that punches well above its casual setup. The falafel is crisp and nicely seasoned, the avgolemono is pure comfort, and the gyro comes stuffed to bursting. Grab a table or take a spread of mezze to go for a picnic.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Greek at Mykonos Greek Grill

mainstay-provisions.name: Mainstay Provisions
mainstay-provisions.oneLiner: An early, inexpensive Phinney Ridge coffee stop that keeps the morning simple.
mainstay-provisions.blurb: Mainstay Provisions opens early on Phinney Ridge as a neighborhood cafe that won't cost you much.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cafe at Mainstay Provisions

donna-s.name: Donna's
donna-s.oneLiner: A Capitol Hill bar for a round with friends that might turn into three.
donna-s.blurb: Donna's pours drinks on the Hill and makes the cut among the neighborhood's better bars.

photos.alt: Donna's in Seattle
Illustration suggesting Bar at Donna's

frankie-jo-s.name: Frankie & Jo's
frankie-jo-s.oneLiner: Dairy-free scoops so good you'll forget anything was missing in the first place.
frankie-jo-s.blurb: Frankie & Jo's makes Seattle's best ice cream without a drop of dairy or a speck of wheat. The cultured crème fraîche flavor, swirled with berries and studded with lemon cake, is unforgettable, and oat milk vanilla loaded with brown sugar blondies is close behind. Get your scoops in a house maple oat waffle cone, and know the Hill shop stays open late.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Ice Cream at Frankie & Jo's

saigon-drip-cafe.name: Saigon Drip Cafe
saigon-drip-cafe.oneLiner: Start a Pioneer Square morning here with a proper Vietnamese coffee.
saigon-drip-cafe.blurb: Vietnamese coffee is the specialty at Saigon Drip Cafe, a Pioneer Square cafe that's open early.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Vietnamese Coffee at Saigon Drip Cafe

serious-pie.name: Serious Pie
serious-pie.oneLiner: Order the sausage and peppers pie and grab a seat at the communal tables.
serious-pie.blurb: Pizza night for adults looks like Serious Pie, a Belltown room with an open kitchen, long shared tables, and lighting that's moody but still lets you see your food. Pies come out oval and blistered, with combinations that are inventive without getting silly. The sausage, peppers, and provolone is the standout, and the crust keeps a satisfying chew under its crisp edges.

photos.alt: Serious Pie in Seattle
photos.credit: Serious Pie and Dahlia Bakery, Belltown, Seattle 2.jpg

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pizza at Serious Pie

metropolitan-grill.name: Metropolitan Grill
metropolitan-grill.oneLiner: The downtown steakhouse to book when the expense account is paying.
metropolitan-grill.blurb: Metropolitan Grill has been downtown's classic steakhouse since the eighties, all dark wood, big steaks, and expense-account energy. The kitchen stays open late, so it works after a game or a show.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Steakhouse at Metropolitan Grill

kitchen-market.name: Kitchen & Market
kitchen-market.oneLiner: Grab a cheap early breakfast here before the market crowds arrive.
kitchen-market.blurb: Opening early with inexpensive cafe fare, Kitchen & Market doubles as a small grocery inside Pike Place Market.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cafe at Kitchen & Market

windy-city-pie.name: Windy City Pie
windy-city-pie.oneLiner: Order the deep dish and fight over the caramelized cheese edge.
windy-city-pie.blurb: Phinney Ridge gets serious deep-dish pizza from Windy City Pie, where a crispy, caramelized cheese crust rings every pan.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pizza at Windy City Pie

made-in-house.name: Made in House
made-in-house.oneLiner: Order the daily bento and plan on skipping the rest of your afternoon.
made-in-house.blurb: Midafternoon on a weekday, this Fremont lunch spot is still full of people who clearly cleared their calendars. At Made in House, the bento changes daily and brings bulgogi, a jammy egg, springy japchae, and tempura kale that cracks apart at first bite. Salmon kimbop gets rolled fresh each day, and the shortbread bar tastes like a homemade candy bar.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Asian Fusion at Made in House

market-at-the-park.name: MARKET at the Park
market-at-the-park.oneLiner: Seafood up top in Belltown, best saved for a clear evening.
market-at-the-park.blurb: For seafood with rooftop seating in Belltown, MARKET at the Park is the move.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at MARKET at the Park

ramen-danbo.name: Ramen DANBO
ramen-danbo.address: 1222 E Pine St, Unit A, Seattle, WA 98122
ramen-danbo.oneLiner: Go thin and firm on the noodles, extra rich on the broth.
ramen-danbo.blurb: Expect a line at Ramen DANBO, and expect it to be worth it for Hakata-style tonkotsu this good. The order sheet lets you dial in noodle firmness, broth richness, and spice, so ask for extra fat plus extra karadare if you want it silky and hot. Plenty of counter seats make it an easy solo dinner.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Ramen at Ramen DANBO

shomon.name: Shomon
shomon.oneLiner: Snag a counter seat for eight courses and a crab nugget you'll crave later.
shomon.blurb: From the team behind Shiro's, Shomon gives Seattle omakase a looser, livelier spin. Chefs move around an open kitchen chatting with guests over a mellow lo-fi soundtrack, and the courses mix nigiri with other Japanese small plates, like Hokkaido scallop, futomaki with a soy-cured yolk, and a fried Dungeness crab croquette with béchamel. The counter is roomier than most, and the check lands firmly in special-occasion territory.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sushi at Shomon

shiro-s-sushi-restaurant.name: Shiro's Sushi Restaurant
shiro-s-sushi-restaurant.oneLiner: Order both the salmon and tuna samplers, plus a baked crab hand roll.
shiro-s-sushi-restaurant.blurb: A Belltown sushi institution, Shiro's Sushi Restaurant gets everything right, but the samplers are what you will remember. The salmon plate runs through four cuts and preparations, from seared belly to ikura, while the tuna plate shows off lean, marinated, fatty, and negitoro from a single fish. Sit at the counter for omakase at least once, and budget for a special-occasion check.

photos.alt: Shiro's Sushi Restaurant in Seattle
photos.credit: Agedashi dofu by pinkpucca in Seattle.jpg

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sushi at Shiro's Sushi Restaurant

joie-coffee.name: Joie Coffee
joie-coffee.oneLiner: Try a matcha latte with banana foam, which tastes better than it sounds.
joie-coffee.blurb: A pink La Marzocco anchors the counter at Joie Coffee, a tiny Ballard cafe obsessed with creamy toppings. Banana cream on iced matcha or brownie batter foam on a mocha sounds sugary, but the drinks stay surprisingly balanced. Purists can order a strong Vietnamese coffee, though the tiramisu and strawberry foams are more fun.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at Joie Coffee

jackalope-tex-mex-cantina.name: Jackalope Tex-Mex & Cantina
jackalope-tex-mex-cantina.oneLiner: Head here for tacos when Columbia City calls for Tex-Mex.
jackalope-tex-mex-cantina.blurb: Tacos and Tex-Mex plates explain the wait at Jackalope Tex-Mex & Cantina in Columbia City.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Tex-Mex at Jackalope Tex-Mex & Cantina

oddfellows-cafe-and-bar.name: Oddfellows Café and Bar
oddfellows-cafe-and-bar.oneLiner: Order the soft herby scrambled eggs and a latte, then linger awhile.
oddfellows-cafe-and-bar.blurb: Equal parts French bistro, espresso counter, and old-fashioned grocery, Oddfellows Café and Bar leans hard into exposed brick and Capitol Hill cool. Come early for coffee and soft scrambled eggs with cheese and herbs, or show up later for cocktails on the patio or a relaxed dinner date. There are no reservations, and weekend brunch is busier than dinner, so have a backup in mind.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cafe at Oddfellows Café and Bar

kajiken.name: Kajiken
kajiken.oneLiner: Skip the broth and go all in on a bowl of saucy aburasoba.
kajiken.blurb: Kajiken specializes in aburasoba, a brothless style of ramen where springy noodles get tossed in a rich sauce at the bottom of the bowl. The Capitol Hill shop keeps things casual.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Ramen at Kajiken

url-coffee.name: URL Coffee
url-coffee.oneLiner: Order a Walk To Work latte and settle into the calmest workspace in First Hill.
url-coffee.blurb: URL Coffee looks more like a furniture showroom than a cafe, with natural wood and paper lanterns everywhere. It's a relaxing place to work if you can grab a seat at the long table or one of the small ones. Whatever you do, get the Walk To Work, an iced latte under cinnamon whipped cream.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Coffee at URL Coffee

chuck-s-hop-shop.name: Chuck's Hop Shop
chuck-s-hop-shop.oneLiner: Wall-to-wall coolers, a deep tap list, and a crowd that treats it like a living room.
chuck-s-hop-shop.blurb: Chuck's Hop Shop pairs a long run of taps with coolers packed with bottles and cans. You can linger past eleven.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Beer at Chuck's Hop Shop

la-fontana-siciliana.name: La Fontana Siciliana
la-fontana-siciliana.oneLiner: Book a Belltown dinner here when you're craving Sicilian cooking.
la-fontana-siciliana.blurb: Belltown diners head to La Fontana Siciliana for Italian food with a Sicilian accent.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at La Fontana Siciliana

swel-restaurant.name: SWeL Restaurant
swel-restaurant.address: 3417 Evanston Ave N, Unit 104, Seattle, WA  98103
swel-restaurant.oneLiner: A Fremont spot for New American cooking when you want something easy nearby.
swel-restaurant.blurb: New American cooking is on the menu at SWeL Restaurant in Fremont.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting New American at SWeL Restaurant

harry-s-fine-foods.name: Harry’s Fine Foods
harry-s-fine-foods.oneLiner: An early Capitol Hill breakfast here makes an easy win with visiting parents.
harry-s-fine-foods.blurb: Opening early for breakfast and brunch, Harry’s Fine Foods serves New American cooking that suits a meal with the folks.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting New American at Harry’s Fine Foods

skalka.name: Skalka
skalka.oneLiner: Order the khachapuri, tear into the crust, and swirl the egg into the cheese.
skalka.blurb: Georgian cooking is the focus at Skalka, and the boat-shaped khachapuri, filled with molten cheese and topped with butter and a runny egg, is the reason to go. It opens early, so a cheese bread breakfast downtown is entirely on the table.

photos.alt: Skalka in Seattle
photos.credit: USS Philippine Sea (CV-47) flight deck crew with bombs.jpeg

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Georgian at Skalka

fram.name: Fram
fram.oneLiner: Order a honey lavender latte, claim the window seat, and pretend to work.
fram.blurb: Fram squeezes a lot of fun into a room about the size of a single garage. Lavender lattes sweetened with honey and constantly churning frosé lead the menu, and the fridge holds a good stash of cans and bottles. Strong wifi makes it a natural work spot, though the nearby lake makes a coffee walk awfully tempting.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cafe at Fram

cornelly.name: Cornelly
cornelly.oneLiner: Book it for date night when everyone at the table is craving Italian.
cornelly.blurb: Cornelly makes a strong case for an Italian dinner date on Capitol Hill.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Cornelly

sea-wolf.name: Sea Wolf
sea-wolf.oneLiner: Grab a crusty loaf and a pastry before the morning rush clears the shelves.
sea-wolf.blurb: Fremont's Sea Wolf is serious about bread, turning out naturally leavened loaves with dark, crackling crusts alongside a short run of pastries. You can get in before work and stays inexpensive, so it's easy to make a habit of.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at Sea Wolf

hot-cakes.name: Hot Cakes
hot-cakes.oneLiner: Get the molten cake, but don't overlook the soft serve with magic shell.
hot-cakes.blurb: Molten chocolate cakes are the specialty at Hot Cakes, with peanut butter and s'mores versions, plus a vegan version. The sleeper hit is vanilla soft serve under a shell of smoked chocolate. The Capitol Hill shop stays open late, which makes dessert after dinner easy.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Dessert at Hot Cakes

canlis.name: Canlis
canlis.oneLiner: Dress up and celebrate here, where the lake view does half the work.
canlis.blurb: Since the fifties, Canlis has been the city's go-to for big celebrations, set in a mid-century modern house perched above Lake Union. Service is famously polished, the tall windows put the water front and center, and the check matches the occasion. Book it for an anniversary, a proposal, or a parents' visit.

photos.alt: Canlis in Seattle
photos.credit: Front entrance to Canlis Restaurant, Seattle, Washington, 2012.jpg

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pacific Northwest at Canlis

volunteer-park-cafe-pantry.name: Volunteer Park Cafe & Pantry
volunteer-park-cafe-pantry.oneLiner: Order the BEC on a poppy roll, then grab a pastry for later.
volunteer-park-cafe-pantry.blurb: Tucked into a house in north Capitol Hill, Volunteer Park Cafe & Pantry would be worth a visit for pastries alone, like tahini caramel bars and buckwheat chocolate chunk cookies. The breakfast sandwich is the real star, with thin folded eggs, barely crisp bacon, and melty American cheese on a toasted house poppy seed roll. Laptops aren't allowed on weekends.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cafe at Volunteer Park Cafe & Pantry

the-pastry-project.name: The Pastry Project
the-pastry-project.oneLiner: In summer, get the soft serve buried under rainbow peanut crunch.
the-pastry-project.blurb: The Pastry Project is a training program for bakers, and in warm months its front door becomes a soft serve window. Even plain vanilla and chocolate get exciting with the rainbow peanut topping, which tastes like a Butterfinger without the sticky aftermath. Colder months bring cinnamon rolls and gooey chocolate chip cookies from the same Pioneer Square window.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at The Pastry Project

local-tide.name: Local Tide
local-tide.oneLiner: Order the belly dip with house chips first, then a crab roll.
local-tide.blurb: Local Tide makes a case for Seattle seafood beyond salmon and chowder, though it nails those too. At this Fremont counter, the smoked belly dip with thin, house-seasoned chips is a must. Sandwiches are the main event, from the weekend crab roll with lemon mayo and chives to a dover sole take on the Filet-O-Fish. Shrimp toast with pork fat and a happy hour make it easy to come back.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at Local Tide

cinnamon-works.name: Cinnamon Works
cinnamon-works.oneLiner: Grab a cinnamon roll early, before the Market crowds take over.
cinnamon-works.blurb: Among the market stalls, Cinnamon Works sells big, inexpensive pastries starting first thing in the morning.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at Cinnamon Works

rosellini-s.name: Rosellini's
rosellini-s.oneLiner: Order the croissant, then come back tomorrow for another one.
rosellini-s.blurb: The morning line at Rosellini's tells you everything about where Ballard gets its pastry. The baguette and cinnamon-swirled coffee cake are excellent, but the croissant is the reason to come, with shattering layers, deep butter flavor, and a crumb that springs back when you press it. Get there early, since the doors open before nine.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at Rosellini's

hello-robin.name: Hello Robin
hello-robin.oneLiner: Get the cookie ice cream sandwich with Molly Moon's and an espresso.
hello-robin.blurb: Fresh cookies are the whole point at Hello Robin, a Capitol Hill shop baking everything from classic chocolate chip to a blueberry pancake version. Buy them baked, take home dough, or have two pressed around a scoop of Molly Moon's. An espresso bar makes it an easy afternoon treat.

photos.alt: Hello Robin in Seattle
Illustration suggesting Ice Cream at Hello Robin

fortuna-bottega.name: Fortuna Bottega
fortuna-bottega.address: Building 1 7619 Greenwood Ave N, Seattle, WA  98103
fortuna-bottega.oneLiner: Cheap Italian sandwiches in Greenwood, no reservation needed, just show up hungry.
fortuna-bottega.blurb: Fortuna Bottega makes inexpensive Italian sandwiches at a walk-up Greenwood counter.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Italian at Fortuna Bottega

maria-luisa-empanadas.name: Maria Luisa Empanadas
maria-luisa-empanadas.address: 928 NW Leary Way, Ste 102, Seattle, WA  98107
maria-luisa-empanadas.oneLiner: Order more empanadas than you think you need, especially the creamed spinach.
maria-luisa-empanadas.blurb: Over in Ballard, Maria Luisa Empanadas turns out tender pastries stuffed with meats, cheeses, and vegetables, plus a chimichurri you'll want to bottle. The garage-style room has high-tops for a quick lunch, and takeout is easy even for a crowd. Picking a favorite is hard, but the creamed spinach and the tangy chorizo lead the pack.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Argentine at Maria Luisa Empanadas

tat-s-delicatessen.name: Tat's Delicatessen
tat-s-delicatessen.oneLiner: Order a cheesesteak with hot peppers and settle in under the Philly flags.
tat-s-delicatessen.blurb: When only East Coast comfort food will fix your mood, Tat's Delicatessen in Pioneer Square has you covered with hoagies, wings, and fries. It is a no-frills spot plastered with Pennsylvania sports flags. Go with the hot pepper cheesesteak, the Tatstrami, or a grinder with potato chips stuffed inside.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sandwiches at Tat's Delicatessen

fob-poke-bar.name: FOB Poke Bar
fob-poke-bar.oneLiner: A Belltown poke counter for a quick, fresh lunch you can eat walking.
fob-poke-bar.blurb: FOB Poke Bar builds Hawaiian-style bowls at a casual Belltown counter.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Poke at FOB Poke Bar

black-bottle.name: Black Bottle
black-bottle.oneLiner: Swing by after work for crab dip, cauliflower, and a round of cocktails.
black-bottle.blurb: Before trading work clothes for sweatpants, stop into Black Bottle in Belltown for a drink. The menu runs long, covering Korean fried chicken bites, spicy cauliflower, and a cheesy Dungeness crab dip, so you can mix it up on every visit. There's a happy hour.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Gastropub at Black Bottle

cheba-hut-toasted-subs.name: Cheba Hut Toasted Subs
cheba-hut-toasted-subs.address: 4730 University Way NE, Ste 108, Seattle, WA  98105
cheba-hut-toasted-subs.oneLiner: Cheap toasted subs that hit hardest when it's late and you're starving.
cheba-hut-toasted-subs.blurb: A stoner-themed chain counter near the university, Cheba Hut Toasted Subs keeps the oven running late and the prices low.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sandwiches at Cheba Hut Toasted Subs

nana-s-green-tea.name: Nana's Green Tea
nana-s-green-tea.oneLiner: Order the matcha parfait with cake on top and call it lunch.
nana-s-green-tea.blurb: After a rough morning, sometimes the fix is sitting alone with soft serve in a waffle cone crowned with a whole slice of cake. Nana's Green Tea, a matcha-everything Japanese cafe downtown, is happy to make that your midday meal.

photos.alt: Nana's Green Tea in Seattle
Illustration suggesting Japanese at Nana's Green Tea

sunfish.name: Sunfish
sunfish.oneLiner: Order the cod and the Greek-spiced fried oysters, and eat by the beach.
sunfish.blurb: Few things say West Seattle like Sunfish, an Alki fish and chips counter that goes dark for most of winter and flips its neon sign back on around February. Squeeze lemon over battered cod that flakes apart and meaty oysters fried with Greek spices for a sunny, casual lunch near the sand.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at Sunfish

marination.name: Marination
marination.oneLiner: Grab a patio seat at Alki and treat it like the beach shack you deserved.
marination.blurb: Think of every sad boardwalk snack bar from your childhood, then picture the opposite. That's Marination at Alki, a Hawaiian spot with a sunny patio and food that justifies the drive to West Seattle even if you live across town. Bring sunscreen if you're sitting outside.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Hawaiian at Marination

the-fonte-bar.name: The Fonté Bar
the-fonte-bar.oneLiner: A downtown cocktail bar that's already open when most bars are still asleep.
the-fonte-bar.blurb: Downtown, The Fonté Bar mixes pricier cocktails and opens its doors early in the day.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at The Fonté Bar

calozzi-s-cheesesteaks-georgetown.name: Calozzi's Cheesesteaks Georgetown
calozzi-s-cheesesteaks-georgetown.address: 7016 East Marginal Way S, Seattle, WA  98108
calozzi-s-cheesesteaks-georgetown.oneLiner: Always add fried onions, and go for the whiz if your shirt can handle it.
calozzi-s-cheesesteaks-georgetown.blurb: Easy to miss and easy to trip into, Calozzi's Cheesesteaks Georgetown is a tiny roadside shack that handles any Philly craving. The beef is shaved paper thin and piled so high you'll lose some before it reaches your mouth, and while it can run a little dry, the flavor is excellent. It's an inexpensive lunch, too.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Sandwiches at Calozzi's Cheesesteaks Georgetown

place-pigalle-restaurant-and-bar.name: Place Pigalle Restaurant and Bar
place-pigalle-restaurant-and-bar.oneLiner: Book a window table at sunset and let the Sound do half the romancing.
place-pigalle-restaurant-and-bar.blurb: Down a flight of stairs at the back of the market, Place Pigalle Restaurant and Bar hides a small French dining room with big windows over Elliott Bay. The check is a special-occasion one, but the view, the quiet, and the French cooking make a date night feel planned well in advance.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting French at Place Pigalle Restaurant and Bar

the-independent-pizzeria.name: The Independent Pizzeria
the-independent-pizzeria.oneLiner: A small neighborhood pizzeria worth a detour when you're craving a serious pie.
the-independent-pizzeria.blurb: Madison Park locals and pizza obsessives alike head to The Independent Pizzeria for its pies.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pizza at The Independent Pizzeria

terra-plata.name: Terra Plata
terra-plata.oneLiner: Rooftop brunch here is worth a sunburn, so bring sunscreen and a big appetite.
terra-plata.blurb: Terra Plata's rooftop garden on Capitol Hill turns brunch into a long, sunny affair, with a Spanish-leaning breakfast that kicks off nicely with patatas bravas. The roof gets brutally hot in summer, so plan accordingly. Come back around sunset for wine and snacks, which is when the waffled potato chips with truffle salt appear. It also makes a strong date spot.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting New American at Terra Plata

wood-shop-bbq.name: Wood Shop BBQ
wood-shop-bbq.oneLiner: Get the ribs, plus whatever else your finger happens to land on.
wood-shop-bbq.blurb: Wood Shop BBQ started as a food truck and now runs a Central District restaurant with a patio, and its smoked meats rank with the best in town. Brisket, brined chicken thigh, pulled pork sandwiches, and even portobello machaca on brioche are all safe bets. Save room for the ribs, which are the main event.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting BBQ at Wood Shop BBQ

monkey-loft.name: Monkey Loft
monkey-loft.oneLiner: A SoDo dance floor for when last call feels way too early.
monkey-loft.blurb: Monkey Loft keeps the SoDo dance floor going late and well into the early hours.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Nightlife at Monkey Loft

daniel-s-broiler.name: Daniel's Broiler
daniel-s-broiler.oneLiner: A classic steakhouse splurge with lake views that make the bill easier to swallow.
daniel-s-broiler.blurb: Right on the water at Lake Union, Daniel's Broiler does old-school steak dinners with big cuts and bigger views. Expect a milestone bill, and plan it around sunset if you can.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Steakhouse at Daniel's Broiler

finn-maccools.name: Finn Maccools
finn-maccools.oneLiner: Beer pong, trivia, and a karaoke contest for anyone pretending to attend UW.
finn-maccools.blurb: Finn Maccools is the Irish pub on the Ave where a night arrives with a student activity sheet: strong wells, beer pong, trivia, and a karaoke contest. The crowd is mostly collegiate, plus anyone willing to blend in. Walk past it on University Way after dark and you missed the block's loudest room. Pizza can wait on the table. The contest is why that stool is still warm.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bar Food at Finn Maccools

ben-s-bread-co.name: Ben’s Bread Co.
ben-s-bread-co.oneLiner: Phinney Ridge locals line up early for loaves and pastries at this bakery.
ben-s-bread-co.blurb: Walk in early for inexpensive bread and baked goods in Phinney Ridge at Ben’s Bread Co.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bakery at Ben’s Bread Co.

paseo.name: Paseo

orderThis.note: The pork sandwich the shop is built around.

paseo.oneLiner: Order the Caribbean Roast and grab extra napkins, you will need them.
paseo.blurb: Seattle's most famous sandwich might be the Caribbean Roast at Paseo, a pile of marinated roast pork and caramelized onions on a toasted baguette. It's gloriously messy, so eat it right away in Fremont rather than letting it sit.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Caribbean at Paseo

billiard-hoang.name: Billiard Hoang
billiard-hoang.oneLiner: Get the fish sauce wings and a lemongrass vermicelli bowl, then shoot some pool.
billiard-hoang.blurb: Billiard Hoang has long been a Columbia City favorite spread by word of mouth, and it still hasn't slipped. Inside a no-frills pool hall with a roomy dining area, nearly everything on the menu is terrific and inexpensive. Those fish sauce wings are famous for good reason, and the lemongrass chicken vermicelli bowls are big enough to cover two meals.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Vietnamese at Billiard Hoang

seattle-biscuit-company.name: Seattle Biscuit Company
seattle-biscuit-company.oneLiner: Order the Gus, with fried chicken, pickles, an egg, and sausage gravy.
seattle-biscuit-company.blurb: The Fremont room feels like a boxcar diner shrunk down by a tiny-house builder, and Seattle Biscuit Company serves breakfast all day. Biscuits anchor everything, and they are excellent, whether in a sandwich like the peanut butter, apple, and jam Lunch Pail or smothered in classic gravy. Very hungry groups can tackle a huge platter of biscuits and eggs.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Breakfast & Brunch at Seattle Biscuit Company

six-seven-restaurant.name: Six Seven Restaurant
six-seven-restaurant.oneLiner: Come at sunset, when the view over Elliott Bay does most of the work.
six-seven-restaurant.blurb: Inside the Edgewater Hotel on the waterfront, Six Seven Restaurant is all about the scenery, with big windows and a deck right over the water. The Northwest menu leans on seafood, and happy hour is the low-commitment way to soak it all in.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pacific Northwest at Six Seven Restaurant

atoma.name: Atoma
atoma.oneLiner: Book the old Wallingford house when you want vegetables treated like the main event.
atoma.blurb: Plenty of pricey Seattle restaurants talk up local produce, but Atoma actually delivers on it. Expect a few familiar plates like sturgeon and beef tartare, though the vegetable cooking is where the kitchen really shines. The dining room still feels like the Wallingford home it used to be, and the check makes it a special-occasion dinner.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting New American at Atoma

hey-bagel.name: Hey Bagel
hey-bagel.oneLiner: Start a U District morning here with a bagel that won't cost much.
hey-bagel.blurb: Inexpensive bagels and early hours make Hey Bagel a handy U District morning stop.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Bagels at Hey Bagel

roma-roma.name: Roma Roma
roma-roma.oneLiner: Come for crunchy al taglio squares, linger over a lambrusco granita and an old movie.
roma-roma.blurb: On Capitol Hill, Roma Roma cuts thick, crisp al taglio slabs and sells them by weight. Toppings range from pepperoni cups to wild boar bolognese, and not all of them land, but the room makes up for it with wild floor tiles and classic Hollywood films projected overhead. It's easy to drop in any time, ideally when a musical is on.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Pizza at Roma Roma

the-alley.name: The Alley
the-alley.oneLiner: Walk through a locker door into a velvet cocktail lounge hiding behind a Vietnamese restaurant.
the-alley.blurb: The Alley hides behind Bonjour Vietnam, a sleepy West Seattle restaurant, past what looks like a storage room stacked with booster seats and coolers. Open the right locker and you land in a plush bar of crystal chandeliers and velvet stools, with liquor locked inside glass cabinets. Order the jungle punch with cajun wings from the kitchen up front. Live jazz plays Sunday and Monday nights, and the bar keeps going late.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Cocktails at The Alley

barnacle.name: Barnacle
barnacle.oneLiner: Sip an amaro at the long wooden bar while waiting for a table next door.
barnacle.blurb: Barnacle pours beside Ballard's famous oyster bar, and it might be the cooler room. One long wood counter is the whole floor plan, a bowl of Lay's lands at your elbow, and the bartenders make drinks that embarrass a home setup. Oysters, cured meats, and cheese suit a promising date, and the early drink window is worth using.

photos.alt: Illustration suggesting Seafood at Barnacle
